relations.note: CORE's worker-ownership and selected-manager arrangement provides a concrete case for separating governance authority from everyday organizational coordination.

original_record.card: Public health works to prevent illness and protect health across communities. Vaccination, safer environments and reducing exposure to hazards can change risks before an individual needs treatment. Its population focus connects personal health with shared conditions, policies and collective actions that affect many people at once.

evidence.locator: What is public health?; Prevention examples
evidence.note: APHA describes community-wide prevention, protective environments and examples including vaccination and health-hazard reduction.

original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect community-wide prevention with safer water, vaccination and protection from health hazards.
original_record.original_description: Studying and supporting health at the level of populations and communities.

relations.note: Framingham’s population follow-up illustrates how evidence about shared risk factors can inform preventive public-health work.

original_record.card: Linguistics investigates how people actually use language, rather than simply declaring which usages they ought to prefer. Researchers compare patterns and test possible explanations against observations. A word that sounds impossible in a language can be informative evidence about its structure, even when no rule was explicitly taught.

evidence.note: Checked empirical versus prescriptive distinction and possible-word judgments; not every intuition is treated as unbiased or sufficient evidence alone.

original_record.learning_takeaway: Investigate language through systematic observations rather than treating preferred usage as an empirical rule.
original_record.original_description: Studying the structures, meanings and uses of human language.

relations.note: The descriptive scientific approach becomes concrete in phonology's investigation of permitted sound combinations and recurring pronunciation patterns.

original_record.card: Peer learning develops understanding through exchanges between learners. Explaining why an answer seems right and listening to another person's reasoning can expose gaps that solitary work misses. Peer Instruction provides one structured classroom example, but the broader activity is not limited to that particular voting-and-discussion sequence.

evidence.note: Checked reasoning exchange and specific protocol example; no guarantee that every peer discussion corrects errors or improves learning.

imported_records.description: Developing understanding through collaboration and exchange among learners.

original_record.label: Peer learning
original_record.learning_takeaway: Develop understanding by explaining reasoning to other learners and considering their explanations.
original_record.original_description: Developing understanding through collaboration and exchange among learners.

relations.note: The Peer Instruction paper explicitly describes learners explaining reasoning to each other within a collaborative classroom protocol.

original_record.card: Bread dough needs both expanding gas and a structure that can retain it. In wheat bread, yeast produces gas while hydrated flour proteins form a stretchy gluten network. Baking expands the pockets and sets the dough, connecting fermentation, material structure and heat in one everyday craft.

evidence.note: Exploratorium describes yeast gas production, gluten development, gas pockets expanding during cooking and dough solidification.

imported_records.description: Making bread through mixing, fermentation, shaping and baking.

original_record.label: Bread baking
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect dough structure and microbial gas production with the rise of bread.
original_record.original_description: Making bread through mixing, fermentation, shaping and baking.

relations.note: Gluten formation is a specific material mechanism within the broader bread-baking process.

original_record.card: Chess ends in checkmate when the opposing king is attacked and no legal move can remove the threat. The king is never actually captured. A different ending, stalemate, occurs when a player has no legal move but their king is not attacked.

evidence.note: Articles 1.4 and 5.2.1 support the objective, prohibition of king capture and contrasting stalemate condition; no claim that every immobile king is stalemated.

imported_records.description: Exploring strategic play, tactics and positional thinking in chess.

original_record.label: Chess
original_record.learning_takeaway: Understand why checkmate ends play without capturing the king.
original_record.original_description: Exploring strategic play, tactics and positional thinking in chess.

relations.note: The laws distinguish checkmate from stalemate through whether the immobile side's king is attacked.

original_record.card: Shogi is Japanese chess with a distinctive form of piece reuse. Captured pieces become reserves for their captor. Instead of moving a piece already on the board, a player can spend a turn returning a captured piece to play on their own side.

evidence.locator: Physical PDF pages 2, 4 and 13 (zero-based tool page indices 1, 3 and 12): introduction, Comparisons and Placing Captured Pieces
evidence.note: Captured pieces become the captor’s reserves and may be returned to play instead of moving a board piece; no unrestricted-drop or automatic-promotion claim is used.

imported_records.description: Exploring Japanese chess and its distinctive piece-reuse strategies.

original_record.label: Shogi
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explain the piece-reuse feature of shogi through a directly supported broad-game overview, leaving the perpetual-check exception to its separate rule card.
original_record.original_description: Exploring Japanese chess and its distinctive piece-reuse strategies.

relations.note: The guide explicitly compares shogi with European chess and identifies returning captured pieces as a difference.

original_record.card: Backgammon combines a race with obstacles. Each player moves fifteen checkers according to dice rolls, aiming to gather them in the home board and remove them. Landing on a lone opposing checker sends it to the bar, where it must re-enter before other checkers move.

evidence.locator: Object of the Game and Movement
evidence.note: USBGF Object, Movement and Hitting sections support fifteen checkers, dice movement, bearing-off objective and priority of bar entry; a hit requires landing on a lone checker.

imported_records.description: Exploring strategic play involving movement, probability and dice.

original_record.label: Backgammon
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect dice-limited movement with the race to remove all fifteen checkers.
original_record.original_description: Exploring strategic play involving movement, probability and dice.

relations.note: The rules make re-entry of hit checkers a compulsory interruption of normal checker movement.

original_record.card: In contract bridge, four players form two partnerships. Bidding establishes a contract specifying a number of tricks and a trump suit, or no trumps. During play, one partner's cards are exposed as dummy, and the declarer chooses cards from both partnership hands.

evidence.note: ACBL Basics, Auction and Play support partnerships, contract denomination and dummy control; bidding numbers count tricks above the initial six, so the card avoids equating the printed bid with total tricks.

imported_records.description: Exploring partnership bidding and trick-taking strategy.

original_record.label: Contract bridge
original_record.learning_takeaway: See how bidding fixes a partnership's trick-taking target before play.
original_record.original_description: Exploring partnership bidding and trick-taking strategy.

relations.note: ACBL's play explanation assigns the exposed partnership hand to declarer's decisions after the auction.

original_record.card: Woodworking shapes and joins wood into useful or decorative objects. Adhesive bonds, for example, let separate pieces share loads and form structures that a single piece could not easily provide. Understanding the material and the joint together helps explain why successful making involves more than choosing a shape.

evidence.note: The USDA adhesive chapter describes load transfer, bonded panels/structures and furniture uses; the registered field description supplies shaping/joining scope.

imported_records.description: Shaping and joining wood to create practical or decorative objects.

original_record.label: Woodworking
original_record.learning_takeaway: See joining wood as a way to build objects whose size and behavior differ from a single solid piece.
original_record.original_description: Shaping and joining wood to create practical or decorative objects.

relations.note: End-grain gluing provides a specific example of how wood’s cellular structure influences a woodworking joint.

original_record.card: Weaving interlaces two sets of threads to build cloth. The warp is held on the loom under tension, while the weft passes over and under it. Separating those roles helps explain how a loom organizes many individual strands into a stable, patterned textile structure.

evidence.note: Ashford defines warp held under tension and weft passing over/under it to form woven fabric.

imported_records.description: Interlacing threads or fibers to create textiles.

original_record.label: Weaving
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish the held warp from the interlacing weft that creates woven cloth.
original_record.original_description: Interlacing threads or fibers to create textiles.

relations.note: Managing the held warp’s tension is a specific operational concern within the interlacing process.

original_record.card: Color theory examines relationships among colors and the effects those relationships can produce. A color’s appearance depends partly on its surroundings and on what was seen before it. Comparing these situations reveals why choosing a color is also choosing a context in which viewers will encounter it.

evidence.note: Simultaneous and successive contrast support context-dependent appearance.

imported_records.description: Exploring how colors interact perceptually and compositionally.

original_record.label: Color theory
original_record.learning_takeaway: Color relationships include changes caused by neighboring colors and by colors seen immediately beforehand.
original_record.original_description: Exploring how colors interact perceptually and compositionally.

relations.note: Neighboring-color effects supply a specific case of perceptual color interaction.

original_record.card: Epistemology investigates knowledge, justification, understanding and other kinds of cognitive success. It asks how evidence should constrain belief and what separates knowing from merely being right. Different approaches examine individual reasoning, sensory experience or the social interests that influence which evidence receives attention.

evidence.locator: Opening historical overview and cognitive-success definition
evidence.note: SEP's opening survey explicitly discusses knowledge versus true opinion, sensory justification, formal evidence constraints and feminist attention to interests; the card avoids reducing the field to one proposed knowledge analysis.

imported_records.description: Investigating knowledge, justification and the limits of understanding.

original_record.label: Epistemology
original_record.learning_takeaway: Investigate what distinguishes knowledge, justified belief and other forms of cognitive success.
original_record.original_description: Investigating knowledge, justification and the limits of understanding.

relations.note: The tripartite analysis is one particular attempt to explain knowledge within a broader field that also studies justification, understanding and evidence; it is not the definition of epistemology itself.

original_record.card: Religious studies examines religion through historical, social and interpretive methods. What researchers count as religion affects which practices and institutions enter their questions. Comparing definitions and methods therefore matters alongside learning about any one tradition’s beliefs, texts or ceremonies.

evidence.note: Academic methods and definitional consequences are discussed.

imported_records.description: Investigating religions through historical, cultural and social approaches.

original_record.label: Religious studies
original_record.learning_takeaway: The academic study of religion uses multiple methods, and different definitions change which practices or institutions enter its questions.
original_record.original_description: Investigating religions through historical, cultural and social approaches.

relations.note: Comparing traditions is one approach within a wider academic study of religious phenomena.

original_record.card: Islamic religious life is shaped by commitments to God, Muhammad and the Qur’an, while communities differ in interpretation and practice. Prayer offers a concrete entry point: preparation and orientation connect shared commitments with repeated bodily actions performed in many different settings.

evidence.note: Introduction supports foundations and diversity; r02 supports the prayer example.
Prayer preparation and orientation supply the embodied example.

imported_records.description: Exploring Islamic beliefs, practices, institutions and histories.

original_record.label: Islam
original_record.learning_takeaway: Commitments to God, Muhammad and the Qur’an coexist with differing interpretations of leadership, scripture and religious practice.
original_record.original_description: Exploring Islamic beliefs, practices, institutions and histories.

relations.note: Prayer direction makes one shared orientation within Muslim practice concrete.

original_record.card: Jewish life connects sacred texts and religious practice with collective history, culture and changing communities. Scriptural interpretation offers one way to explore these connections. The Talmud’s preserved arguments, for example, show how teaching can develop through discussion rather than only through a single final statement.

evidence.note: Introduction supports communal/textual context; r11 supports preserved argument.
Rabbinic disputation supports the argumentative-text example.

imported_records.description: Exploring Jewish religious traditions, practices and intellectual histories.

original_record.label: Judaism
original_record.learning_takeaway: Jewish religious life connects sacred texts and monotheistic traditions with collective history, culture and changing communal practices.
original_record.original_description: Exploring Jewish religious traditions, practices and intellectual histories.

relations.note: The Talmud provides a documented example of rabbinic learning through discussion.

original_record.card: Buddhist traditions look to Buddha, Dharma and Sangha: the awakened teacher, the teaching and the community. Those shared points of reference coexist with varied practices and interpretations. Beginning with the community’s relationship to teaching helps make that diversity visible without reducing Buddhism to one uniform routine.

evidence.note: Three Treasures and traditions’ diversity are described.

imported_records.description: Exploring Buddhist traditions, communities, teachings and practices.

original_record.label: Buddhism
original_record.learning_takeaway: Buddhist traditions share reference to Buddha, Dharma and Sangha while interpreting and practicing these commitments in diverse ways.
original_record.original_description: Exploring Buddhist traditions, communities, teachings and practices.

relations.note: Sangha is one of the Three Treasures identified in the introduction.

original_record.card: Shinto shrine traditions center on the veneration of kami in places called jinja. Visits, festivals and sacred objects connect these places with ordinary life. An ofuda taken home, for example, can extend a shrine relationship into the household through an object treated with religious reverence.

imported_records.description: Exploring Japanese religious traditions associated with kami and ritual life.

original_record.learning_takeaway: Kami are enshrined and venerated in diverse jinja; visits, festivals and protective objects connect sacred places with everyday life.
original_record.original_description: Exploring Japanese religious traditions associated with kami and ritual life.

relations.note: Jinja Honcho presents ofuda as one way a shrine relationship enters domestic practice.

original_record.card: Distributed systems spread computation across machines that communicate over a network. Keeping their work coordinated becomes difficult when messages are delayed or machines fail. Replicated state machines offer one approach: replicas agree on commands and execute them deterministically in the same order to maintain matching results.

evidence.note: The paper, Section 2, requires deterministic state machines as well as an agreed command order for matching states and outputs. This is one distributed-systems pattern, not a condition met by all distributed programs.

imported_records.description: Coordinating computation across multiple networked machines.

original_record.label: Distributed systems
original_record.learning_takeaway: Coordinate machines through messages while preserving shared results despite some machine failures.
original_record.original_description: Coordinating computation across multiple networked machines.

relations.note: The Raft paper's replicated-state-machine discussion gives one concrete coordination approach within the broad distributed-systems field.

original_record.card: Cryptography uses keyed mathematical techniques to protect information and verify messages or participants. Encryption can hide content, while authentication and integrity mechanisms help detect impersonation or alteration. TLS illustrates how several cryptographic tools are combined into a communication protocol rather than relying on secrecy of the design.

evidence.note: Checked TLS security goals and key/design distinction; encryption alone is not claimed to provide every cryptographic property.

evidence.note: Supplementary inspected premise for the card or its comparison: TLS provides a concrete protocol combining encryption, authentication and integrity goals; Saltzer's open-design principle clarifies the distinction between public mechanisms and secret keys.

original_record.label: Cryptography
original_record.learning_takeaway: Combine keyed encryption and authentication to protect message confidentiality, integrity, and peer identity.
original_record.original_description: Protecting information through mathematical encoding and verification techniques.

relations.note: TLS provides a concrete protocol combining encryption, authentication and integrity goals; Saltzer's open-design principle clarifies the distinction between public mechanisms and secret keys.

original_record.card: Probability studies uncertain outcomes by assigning them numerical likelihoods and organizing those likelihoods into distributions. A distribution can describe individual possible values or a continuous range. Cumulative probability combines the possibilities up to a threshold, connecting uncertainty about outcomes with quantities that can be compared.

evidence.locator: Probability -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1, 3, 5 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2; paragraph-4; paragraph-6

original_record.original_description: Modeling uncertainty and random events mathematically.

original_record.card: Graph theory studies structures made of vertices and connecting edges. A graph’s drawing or numbering can change without altering its connections. An adjacency matrix provides one numerical representation, making it possible to analyze the same underlying network through different arrangements of symbols.

evidence.locator: Graph Theory -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2

original_record.original_description: Studying networks of vertices and connecting edges.

relations.note: The adjacency-matrix reference explicitly represents graph connections while allowing different vertex labelings.

original_record.card: Topology studies properties of spaces preserved by continuous, reversible changes of shape. Stretching a circle into an ellipse changes lengths but preserves its connected loop. Focusing on such structure lets mathematicians compare objects without treating every geometric distortion as a fundamentally new space.

evidence.note: Study connectivity and properties preserved by continuous changes rather than exact lengths or angles.

original_record.label: Topology
original_record.learning_takeaway: Study connectivity and properties preserved by continuous changes rather than exact lengths or angles.
original_record.original_description: Studying properties of spaces preserved under continuous deformation.

original_record.card: Information theory measures the choices involved in sending messages and the limits of communication systems. In Shannon's formulation, a message is selected from possible alternatives; its personal meaning is a separate question. Using base-two logarithms measures those choices in bits.

evidence.note: Checked the message-selection problem, explicit separation from semantics, and logarithm-base choice in the introduction; no claim that human meaning is unimportant generally.

imported_records.description: Quantifying information, uncertainty and communication limits.

original_record.learning_takeaway: Measure communication choices without treating message meaning as the engineering quantity.
original_record.original_description: Quantifying information, uncertainty and communication limits.

relations.note: Shannon's paper provides a concrete historical entry into the field by formulating message selection and its bit-based measure.

original_record.card: Physics seeks common explanations for matter, energy, motion, and interactions across scales. The gravity governing a galaxy’s stars is connected with the gravity involved in water flowing through a dam. Such links let a few tested principles explain phenomena that initially seem unrelated.

evidence.note: Use common laws of matter, energy, space, and time to connect laboratory and cosmic phenomena.

original_record.learning_takeaway: Use common laws of matter, energy, space, and time to connect laboratory and cosmic phenomena.

original_record.card: Optics studies light’s behavior and its interactions with materials. Refraction offers a concrete example: a ray can change direction when it enters a medium where light travels at a different speed. The same principle helps explain lenses, distorted underwater views, and optical-fiber systems.

original_record.learning_takeaway: Explain image formation and light guidance through refraction and related behavior at material boundaries.
original_record.original_description: Studying light and its interactions with matter.

original_record.card: Chemistry connects observable substances with the particles and interactions that explain their behavior. A visible change can be described through a molecular model and represented by a formula or equation. Moving among these descriptions helps make sense of experiments.

evidence.note: Connect observable changes in matter with particle-level explanations and chemical representations.

original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect observable changes in matter with particle-level explanations and chemical representations.
original_record.original_description: Studying substances, their properties and their transformations.

original_record.card: Geology investigates Earth’s materials, physical processes and history. Rocks preserve evidence of earlier conditions, while tectonics, weathering and erosion continue to change landscapes. Reading a place geologically means connecting what is visible today with the processes and timescales that produced it.

imported_records.description: Investigating Earth's materials, structures and history.

original_record.original_description: Investigating Earth's materials, structures and history.

relations.note: Subduction offers one concrete tectonic process through which geology connects material movement and landscape formation.

original_record.card: Oceanography studies the ocean through its water movement, chemistry, living communities and seafloor history. These perspectives overlap: circulation can move nutrients that influence marine life. Field observations, experiments and models connect the ocean’s physical setting with the organisms and chemical processes operating within it.

original_record.original_description: Investigating the physical, chemical and biological properties of oceans.

relations.note: Coastal upwelling illustrates how circulation delivers nutrients and connects physical with biological oceanography.

original_record.card: Genetics studies inheritance and variation, including how genes interact with the environment. A DNA difference can influence a trait without determining it alone. Studying genes alongside behavior and surroundings helps explain why genetic information is only part of the story of health.

original_record.original_description: Studying inheritance and variation in living organisms.

original_record.card: Ecology investigates how organisms interact with one another and with their surroundings. A butterfly’s food plant, predators and climate can all shape where it survives. Moving between individuals, populations and communities helps researchers connect small interactions with larger patterns of abundance and distribution.

evidence.note: OpenStax defines ecology and its levels, then uses the Karner blue butterfly to connect organismal requirements with community interactions.

imported_records.description: Studying relationships between organisms and their environments.

original_record.label: Ecology
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect organisms’ distribution and abundance with living and nonliving surroundings.
original_record.original_description: Studying relationships between organisms and their environments.

relations.note: The Karner blue example connects the field’s organism and community scales through habitat requirements and ant–larva interactions.

original_record.card: Material culture examines social life through objects and their uses. A coffee-house trade token, for example, advertised goods while presenting a particular image of the business. Its wording and pictures let a small commercial object become evidence about consumption, exchange and public identity.

imported_records.description: Understanding social life through objects and their uses.

original_record.label: Material culture
original_record.learning_takeaway: A trade token’s imagery and product list provide evidence of commercial life and how a coffee house represented itself.
original_record.original_description: Understanding social life through objects and their uses.

relations.note: The named token supplies a specific object through which to investigate commercial representation.

original_record.card: Human geography studies how communities, cultures and economies relate to places and environments. imported_records.description: Studying relationships among people, places and spatial organization.

original_record.original_description: Studying relationships among people, places and spatial organization.

original_record.card: Cultural landscapes record relationships between people and their environments. imported_records.description: Examining landscapes shaped by relationships between people and environments.

original_record.card: An access control list associates a protected object with the principals permitted to use it. When access is requested, that object-centered list helps determine authority. This differs from a capability system, where a principal presents an unforgeable ticket naming the object and conveying access authority.

evidence.locator: Glossary, Access control list and List-oriented
evidence.note: Checked object-to-principal list meaning and contrast with capabilities; no assumption that every list has identical permission syntax.

original_record.label: Access control list
original_record.learning_takeaway: Associate an object with a list of principals authorized to access it.

relations.note: The glossary's list-oriented and ticket-oriented descriptions provide the factual basis for contrasting two arrangements of authority.

original_record.card: An achieved status is a social position acquired through activity or choice, such as becoming a nurse. The term distinguishes its route of acquisition from an ascribed position. Status names the position; role describes the patterns of behavior expected of someone who holds it.

evidence.note: Checked nurse example and position-versus-behavior distinction; not claimed that achieved outcomes reflect effort alone or equal opportunity.

original_record.label: Achieved status
original_record.learning_takeaway: Identify social positions acquired through activity or choice, while separating the position from its expected behaviors.

relations.note: The source directly presents achieved and ascribed statuses as contrasting acquisition categories, alongside the status/role distinction.

original_record.card: An acid–base indicator has differently colored acid and base forms. Changing pH shifts their relative amounts, producing a visible transition rather than an infinitely sharp switch. An indicator therefore reports a range of acidity, and its useful color interval depends on its own acid–base equilibrium.

evidence.locator: 14.7 Acid-Base Titrations; inspected passage indices 48, 50, 52 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-idm39085312; fs-idm68547888; fs-idm188576256
evidence.note: Different colors of a weak acid and its conjugate base report the solution’s pH range.

original_record.label: Acid-base indicator
original_record.learning_takeaway: Different colors of a weak acid and its conjugate base report the solution’s pH range.

relations.note: The titration section uses indicator color-change intervals to choose suitable endpoint signals.

original_record.card: An acid–base titration uses a reagent of known concentration to measure an unknown acid or base. Tracking pH reveals progress toward stoichiometric equivalence. The equivalence point is not always neutral: titrating a weak acid with a strong base typically leaves a basic solution.

evidence.locator: 14.7 Acid-Base Titrations; inspected passage indices 6, 8, 35 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-idm43847120; fs-idp135875056; fs-idm40620912
evidence.note: Use controlled neutralization and a pH curve to determine acid or base concentration.

original_record.label: Acid-base titration
original_record.learning_takeaway: Use controlled neutralization and a pH curve to determine acid or base concentration.

relations.note: The source explicitly presents acid–base titrimetry as a quantitative analytical technique.

original_record.card: In a collision model, activation energy marks the barrier reactants must overcome to reach a transition state. Collisions can fail even when molecules meet: insufficient energy prevents productive rearrangement. A higher barrier leaves fewer collisions energetic enough to react at a given temperature.

evidence.locator: 12.5 Collision Theory; inspected passage indices 18, 21, 23 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-idm58992896; fs-idm102149680; fs-idm92123120
evidence.note: Relate the energy barrier between reactants and the transition state to successful molecular collisions.

original_record.label: Activation energy
original_record.learning_takeaway: Relate the energy barrier between reactants and the transition state to successful molecular collisions.

relations.note: The Arrhenius equation in the same section relates activation energy to the temperature dependence of the rate constant.

original_record.card: Actuarially fair insurance charges a premium equal to the expected claim payment for the relevant risk group. It is a benchmark, not necessarily the price an insurer can sustainably offer. Administration, other business costs, and profit require additional funding beyond that expected-claims amount.

evidence.note: Checked expected payment definition and excluded expense/profit loading; fairness here is a technical pricing term rather than an ethical verdict.

original_record.label: Actuarially fair insurance
original_record.learning_takeaway: Separate a premium equal to expected claims from one that also funds operating expenses and profit.

relations.note: The source explicitly derives insurance premiums from group losses before distinguishing expected claims from operating costs and profit.

original_record.card: Samuel Barber's Adagio for Strings provides a textbook example of a 4–3 suspension. A prepared note becomes dissonant against the bass before resolving downward by step. The numbers describe the suspension and resolution as interval classes, so compound intervals can receive the same analytical label.

evidence.note: Puget Sound 10.9 labels the Barber example 4–3 and explains reduction of compound intervals in suspension labels. The revised card does not require the sounding interval to occupy a literal simple-fourth register.

original_record.label: Adagio for Strings
original_record.learning_takeaway: Hear how a 4–3 suspension delays resolution in Barber's work.

relations.note: The named score example is explicitly introduced as a 4–3 suspension.

original_record.card: Adaptive optics counters atmospheric blurring by measuring distortion and rapidly changing the shape of a flexible mirror. The corrections help incoming light reach a sharper focus. A ground-based telescope can therefore recover detail that its aperture permits but turbulent air would otherwise obscure.

evidence.locator: 6.2 Telescopes Today; inspected passage indices 37, 41 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-id1167471084189; fs-id1167470614614
evidence.note: Rapidly reshape a flexible mirror to compensate for atmospheric distortion of incoming starlight.

original_record.label: Adaptive optics
original_record.learning_takeaway: Rapidly reshape a flexible mirror to compensate for atmospheric distortion of incoming starlight.

relations.note: The source explicitly presents adaptive optics as a correction for atmospheric image distortion.

original_record.card: Additive minimalism develops music by expanding repeated material in small steps. In Glass's examples, repetitions may be added or chords given extra subdivisions. The listener can follow a process of gradual growth rather than waiting for an entirely new theme to replace the existing pattern.

evidence.locator: 35.1 Two Pages and Einstein on the Beach examples
evidence.note: Section 35.1 supplies Two Pages, Music in Fifths and lengthened chords in Einstein on the Beach; this describes the demonstrated processes rather than all minimalist composition.

original_record.label: Additive minimalism
original_record.learning_takeaway: Track growth by gradually extending repeated musical patterns.

relations.note: The textbook uses Glass's Two Pages as an explicit example of additive process combined with subtraction within repetitions.

original_record.card: Antidiuretic hormone increases the number of aquaporin water channels in the kidney’s collecting-duct cell membranes. Water can then leave the forming urine along an osmotic gradient. With less hormone, fewer channels are inserted, less water is recovered and the urine can remain more dilute.

evidence.locator: Collecting Ducts and Recovery of Water
evidence.note: The collecting-duct passage states ADH-dependent apical insertion, osmotic water movement and fewer channels/more dilute urine with less ADH.

original_record.label: ADH-dependent aquaporin trafficking
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explain how reversible water-channel insertion changes collecting-duct water recovery.

relations.note: Aquaporin-dependent water recovery uses the medullary osmotic gradient generated in part by countercurrent multiplication.

original_record.card: An adjacency pair links two conversational actions, such as a question and its answer or an invitation and its response. Once the first action occurs, a particular kind of second action becomes relevant. An appropriate response can also show whether the listener understood what the first speaker meant.

evidence.note: Checked conditional relevance and understanding evidence; no claim that paired actions must be physically consecutive without inserted clarification.

original_record.label: Adjacency pair
original_record.learning_takeaway: See how an initial conversational action makes a specific kind of response relevant, such as an answer after a question.

relations.note: Clark and Brennan explicitly discuss relevant second actions as positive evidence of understanding within grounding.

original_record.card: Adverse selection can arise when insurance buyers know more about their own risk than the insurer. A pooled premium may attract high-risk buyers while discouraging lower-risk ones. The changing mix can then raise average claims, making coverage harder to price even before anyone changes their behavior.

evidence.note: Checked buyer composition, pooled pricing and before-versus-after agreement distinction; not every insurance pool is claimed to unravel.

original_record.label: Adverse selection
original_record.learning_takeaway: See how privately known risk changes which people seek insurance and can push low-risk buyers out.

relations.note: The insurance source contrasts hidden-risk selection with behavior changes after coverage; the comparison separates two different information problems.

original_record.card: Five protected Omani aflaj systems connect water sources, channels, cultivated land and settlement. Their structures also reveal arrangements for sharing and protecting scarce water. Looking across the systems shows how technical infrastructure and collective management together shaped inhabited landscapes in an arid region.

evidence.note: Five systems, linked built features and shared management are described.

original_record.label: Aflaj irrigation landscapes of Oman
original_record.learning_takeaway: Five protected systems display how water sources, channels, agriculture, defensive buildings and shared management shaped arid settlements.

relations.note: These named systems are documented cases of the wider water-sharing settlement pattern.

original_record.card: Aflaj water systems use gravity-fed channels to distribute water through arid settlements and agricultural land. Sharing access requires arrangements for timing, upkeep and allocation. Their geography is therefore institutional as well as hydraulic: reliable flow depends on people maintaining both channels and rules.

evidence.note: Gravity-fed distribution, timed shares and communal management are described.

original_record.label: Aflaj water-sharing settlements
original_record.learning_takeaway: Gravity-fed water channels and timed access support permanent settlement and require communities to coordinate maintenance and distribution.

relations.note: The protected Omani systems give named examples of channels, agriculture and cooperative water management.

original_record.card: Agha Shahid Ali helped bring the classical ghazal into English-language poetry and edited Ravishing DisUnities. The Academy’s account emphasizes his understanding of autonomous couplets and the anthology’s varied formal fidelity. His work offers a case for studying poetic adaptation across languages.

evidence.note: The glossary identifies Ali’s classical-ghazal advocacy, autonomous-couplet comparison and editorship of Ravishing DisUnities; it notes varied formal fidelity in the anthology.

original_record.label: Agha Shahid Ali
original_record.learning_takeaway: Ali promoted the traditional ghazal in English through poetry and anthology editorship, emphasizing the autonomy of its couplets.

relations.note: The source connects Ali’s work with transmitting the ghazal’s formal constraints into English.

original_record.card: Ait-Ben-Haddou groups earthen houses and communal facilities inside defensive walls along a former pre-Saharan trade route. Its compact arrangement shows collective settlement in built form. Examining the whole ksar connects domestic life with shared spaces, defense and the movement of goods through the region.

evidence.note: Earthen collective settlement, walls, communal facilities and trade-route setting are documented.

original_record.label: Ait-Ben-Haddou
original_record.learning_takeaway: Compact earthen dwellings and communal facilities inside walls show how a pre-Saharan trading post organized defense and shared life.

relations.note: UNESCO identifies Ait-Ben-Haddou as an example of the fortified collective settlement form.

original_record.card: An akhand path is an uninterrupted reading of the Guru Granth Sahib. Readers take successive turns so the recitation continues through the entire scripture. The practice combines sustained attention to the text with shared responsibility, making continuity possible through the coordinated participation of several people.

evidence.note: Readers rotate through an uninterrupted complete reading.

original_record.label: Akhand path
original_record.learning_takeaway: Readers work in successive shifts so the entire Guru Granth Sahib can be read without interruption.

relations.note: The scripture is the text read in full during akhand path.

original_record.card: Al Ain’s oasis landscape brings tombs, settlement remains and irrigation works into a long record of life at a desert crossroads. These different kinds of evidence connect burial, habitation and water management. Together they reveal how communities sustained settled activity within an arid environment.

evidence.note: Tombs, settlements and irrigation establish the archaeological sequence.

original_record.label: Al Ain oasis landscape
original_record.learning_takeaway: Tombs, settlement remains and irrigation works record long-term sedentary life at a desert crossroads.

relations.note: The named landscape is an archaeological case of settlement supported by managed water.

original_record.card: Allocation concealment keeps the next trial assignment unknown until enrollment is settled. If recruiters can predict the group a person will enter, they may selectively include participants and undermine randomization. This protection operates at recruitment, whereas blinding addresses knowledge of treatment after assignment.

evidence.note: Cochrane §8.3 defines unknown forthcoming assignments; §8.3.2 explains selective enrollment and explicitly distinguishes concealment from later blinding.

original_record.label: Allocation concealment
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explain why recruiters must not know the next treatment assignment before enrollment.

relations.note: Concealment is a specific protection of assignment within a randomized controlled trial, rather than a synonym for random sequence generation.

original_record.card: Allomorphs are different forms expressing one morpheme. English a and an vary with the following sound, while plural forms show both predictable sound changes and word-specific patterns. Recognizing the shared grammatical function helps distinguish this variation from entirely different morphemes that merely resemble each other.

evidence.note: Checked a/an, plural variants and phonological versus lexical conditioning; variation is not limited to written spelling changes.
Supplementary inspected premise for the card or its comparison: The morphology chapter explicitly presents allomorphy as variation in a morpheme's form while its function remains consistent.

original_record.label: Allomorph
original_record.learning_takeaway: Recognize different forms of one morpheme, with variants conditioned by sounds or specific lexical roots.

relations.note: The morphology chapter explicitly presents allomorphy as variation in a morpheme's form while its function remains consistent.

original_record.card: Allophones are physically different realizations of one phoneme. In many North American English varieties, the consonant in atom differs from the aspirated consonant in atomic, yet both are analyzed as versions of /t/. Their distribution depends partly on the surrounding sounds and stress pattern.

evidence.locator: §4.1, The phonological units of spoken language
evidence.note: Checked atom/atomic and stress environment; retained variety qualification and avoided claiming the analysis is the only possible theoretical treatment.

original_record.label: Allophone
original_record.learning_takeaway: Recognize physically different pronunciations treated as realizations of a single abstract phoneme.

relations.note: Section 4.1 explicitly identifies determining phonemes, allophones, and their environments as a central task of phonology.

original_record.card: A gene’s RNA can be assembled in different ways by joining different combinations of exons. Alternative splicing therefore produces related RNA transcripts from one gene, and these can encode proteins with different structures or functions. One gene need not yield just one protein product.

evidence.note: NHGRI’s definition states different exon combinations, related mRNA transcripts and possible proteins with distinct structure/function.

original_record.label: Alternative splicing
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explain how different exon combinations produce multiple related transcripts from one gene.

relations.note: Alternative splicing is a specific way gene information produces varied outputs, an editorial route from the broad genetics field into gene processing.

original_record.card: A curveball's behavior depends partly on the air around it. In NASA's simplified model, lower air density weakens the aerodynamic deflection of a spinning pitch, all else equal. High-altitude conditions can therefore make a curveball travel along a straighter path.

evidence.note: NASA's equation discussion directly links lower density with larger curvature radius; all-else-equal and simplified-model language avoid unsupported prediction of every pitch or game statistic.

original_record.label: Altitude effects on baseball pitches
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explore why thinner air weakens a spinning baseball's curvature, other factors equal.

relations.note: The source derives the altitude effect as a particular prediction of its curveball trajectory model.

original_record.card: Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring collects repeated readings while a person goes about ordinary life, usually over twenty-four hours. A worn monitor is returned after the recording period. This provides a pattern across time and circumstances, rather than relying only on one measurement taken in a clinic.

evidence.note: NHS describes a monitor worn at home for 24 hours and returned the next day for repeated blood-pressure assessment.

original_record.label: Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish repeated measurements during ordinary activity from one clinic reading.

relations.note: The baroreflex regulates a changing pressure, while ambulatory monitoring samples that variable over everyday conditions; this is an editorial physiology-to-measurement bridge.

original_record.card: In US court practice, an amicus curiae is a nonparty offering arguments or information through a brief. An interest in the case does not make the contributor a litigant. Each court's applicable rules govern when and how such outside submissions may be made.

evidence.note: Cornell defines the nonparty role and cites US Supreme Court Rule 37 and Federal Appellate Rule 29. US scope is explicit, while court-specific requirements avoid a universal permission or party-status claim.

original_record.label: Amicus curiae
original_record.learning_takeaway: Understand how a nonparty can contribute a brief to a court's consideration.

relations.note: Compare a nonparty's rule-governed contribution with the injury-based requirements for a plaintiff's federal standing. An amicus brief does not itself give its author party status.

original_record.card: Anadiplosis repeats the end of one clause or line at the beginning of the next. The shared wording acts as a hinge between units, allowing the second statement to grow from the first. Its chained position differs from repeating all beginnings or all endings.

evidence.note: Boundary-to-boundary repetition is defined and exemplified.

original_record.label: Anadiplosis
original_record.learning_takeaway: The closing word of one unit becomes the opening word of the next, linking statements into a chain.

relations.note: Compare a chain across adjacent units with repetition at each unit’s opening.

original_record.card: Anamorphosis deliberately distorts an image so that it becomes recognizable from a particular viewing position or arrangement. Holbein’s stretched skull in The Ambassadors resolves from an oblique angle. The viewer’s position therefore becomes part of how the image is constructed and encountered.

evidence.note: The skull’s distortion and resolving viewpoint are explicitly described.

original_record.label: Anamorphosis
original_record.learning_takeaway: A deliberately distorted image becomes recognizable from a particular viewing position, as the stretched skull in Holbein’s Ambassadors does from the lower right.

relations.note: The gallery identifies the painting’s skull as an anamorphic image.

original_record.card: Rhetorical anaphora repeats a word or phrase at the beginnings of successive units. The shared opening creates a recognizable pattern while later words accumulate differences. It can shape momentum or emphasis, whether the units are poetic lines, clauses or statements in a longer passage.

evidence.note: Initial repetition and accumulative rhetorical effects are described.

original_record.label: Anaphora (rhetoric)
original_record.learning_takeaway: Repeating initial words across phrases or lines can build rhythmic and emotional accumulation.

relations.note: The glossary contrasts repeated beginnings with repeated endings.

original_record.card: For a classical particle, angular momentum combines linear momentum with position relative to a chosen origin. Even straight-line motion can have angular momentum about a point away from that path. A different origin changes the lever arm, so this quantity is not defined by speed alone.

evidence.locator: 11.2 Angular Momentum; inspected passage indices 9, 11, 13, 17 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-id1165038184327; fs-id1165038218862; fs-id1165038332421; fs-id1165038202948
evidence.note: Rotational momentum depends on linear momentum and position relative to a chosen origin.

original_record.label: Angular momentum
original_record.learning_takeaway: Rotational momentum depends on linear momentum and position relative to a chosen origin.

relations.note: The gyroscope passage explains torque-induced precession as a change in angular-momentum direction.

original_record.card: Song examination procedures could replace candidates’ names with numbers and have clerks recopy their answers. These steps reduced clues supplied by identity and handwriting. The practice shows a historical attempt to make assessment depend more on the submitted work than on recognizing its author.

evidence.note: Numbering and recopying are explicit anti-recognition measures.

original_record.label: Anonymization in Song examinations
original_record.learning_takeaway: Numbers replaced candidates’ names and clerks recopied answers to reduce recognition through identity or handwriting.

relations.note: Name removal and recopying are specific examination procedures described within this system.

original_record.card: A growing shoot tip can suppress the development of lateral buds. Apical dominance involves hormonal signals, including auxin from the tip, while cytokinins can favor bud growth. Removing the tip changes that balance, helping explain why pruning can encourage a plant to branch.

evidence.note: OpenStax’s auxin and cytokinin passages describe tip-related lateral inhibition, bud promotion and release after tip removal.

original_record.label: Apical dominance
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect growth at a shoot tip with suppression of lateral buds and the effects of pruning.

relations.note: Pruning applies knowledge of shoot-tip control to a practical gardening decision about branching.

original_record.card: Rhetorical apostrophe directly addresses an absent person, an abstraction or something nonhuman as if it could listen. The address creates a speaker’s imagined relationship with its recipient. It is a figure of speech, distinct from the punctuation mark that shares its name.

evidence.note: The glossary defines direct address to absent or nonhuman recipients.

original_record.label: Apostrophe (rhetoric)
original_record.learning_takeaway: A speaker directly addresses an absent person, an abstraction or a nonhuman thing, creating an imagined listener.

relations.note: Distinguish the recipient invoked by a speaker from the recipient-image inferred from a whole work.

original_record.card: Apple's historical iPhone supply-chain example in The Economy separates product ownership, component manufacturing, and final assembly across different firms and countries. The case shows why calling a product American or Chinese can conceal several distinct production roles, rather than identifying one place where all its value was created.

evidence.note: Checked historical framing and distinct production roles; no current supplier arrangement, percentage or national value-added estimate is asserted.

original_record.label: Apple Inc.
original_record.learning_takeaway: Examine a historically documented separation of product ownership, component sourcing, and final assembly across firms and countries.

relations.note: The textbook explicitly identifies Foxconn as the assembler in its historical Apple supply-chain example.

original_record.card: An appoggiatura is a non-chord tone approached by a leap and left by a step. It is usually accented, placing the dissonance on a strong moment before resolution. The resolving step can go upward or downward; the expressive effect does not require one fixed direction.

evidence.note: Puget Sound 10.4 supports leap approach, step departure, usual accent and either resolution direction; maintain its analytical sense rather than every historical ornamental use of the term.
The prepared same-note approach of a suspension supports the editorial contrast.

original_record.label: Appoggiatura
original_record.learning_takeaway: Follow an expressive non-chord note approached by leap and resolved by step.

relations.note: Both can create accented non-chord tension, but an appoggiatura arrives by leap whereas a suspension is prepared by the same note.

original_record.card: Archaeological context includes where a find lay, what accompanied it and its chronological, social and cultural setting. These relationships constrain interpretation. The same object can support different historical explanations when found in different associations, which is why documenting its surroundings matters.

evidence.note: Spatial, chronological, cultural and social contexts and associations are explicit.

original_record.label: Archaeological context
original_record.learning_takeaway: An object’s location, associations and chronological, social and cultural setting determine what historical inferences it can support.

relations.note: Context is one of the evidential concerns within archaeological investigation.

original_record.card: Archaeological cross-dating compares evidence from different contexts to establish their relative ages. A recognizable pattern at one site can be compared with another, or across layers within a site. The comparison links sequences without necessarily giving either context an exact calendar date.

evidence.note: Cross-dating row explicitly covers comparisons within and between sites.

original_record.label: Archaeological cross-dating
original_record.learning_takeaway: Matching evidence across archaeological contexts can place otherwise undated finds in a relative sequence.

relations.note: Seriation offers one neighboring way to compare patterns of chronological evidence.
The dating-methods table includes cross-dating for archaeological evidence.

original_record.card: Seriation arranges archaeological evidence into a relative sequence by tracking changes in artifact styles. Styles rise and fall in popularity, producing overlapping periods of use. Comparing those patterns can order assemblages, even when the method alone supplies no precise calendar date.

evidence.note: Style popularity and battleship-curve discussion support relative ordering.

original_record.label: Archaeological seriation
original_record.learning_takeaway: Changes in the relative popularity of artifact styles allow assemblages to be arranged into a relative chronological sequence.

relations.note: Both compare evidence to establish chronology, but seriation emphasizes ordered style change.
The NPS explains seriation among methods used to date archaeological sites.

original_record.card: Archaeological stratigraphy uses the sequence of deposited layers to investigate earlier human activity. In an undisturbed sequence, lower layers generally precede those above. The qualification matters: rearranged deposits cannot automatically be read as a simple oldest-to-newest stack.

evidence.note: Superposition is explicitly conditional on undisturbed deposits.

original_record.label: Archaeological stratigraphy
original_record.learning_takeaway: In undisturbed deposits, the ordering of layers supplies relative evidence for the sequence of human activities.

relations.note: Apply the stratigraphic ordering of layers to archaeological deposits and activities.

original_record.card: Archival provenance keeps records connected to the person or organization that created them. Records from different origins are not simply mixed because they discuss the same subject. Preserving that grouping helps researchers reconstruct the activities and relationships that generated the documents.

evidence.note: Creator-origin grouping and nonintermingling are explicit archival principles.

original_record.label: Archival provenance
original_record.learning_takeaway: Keeping records grouped by their creating person or organization preserves relationships that would disappear if unrelated origins were mixed.

relations.note: Provenance preserves origin groups; original order addresses arrangement within them.

original_record.card: Territory scoring counts enclosed empty points and captured stones; area scoring counts enclosed points and stones still occupying the board. That difference changes whether filling your own territory costs a point. AGA rules use pass stones to permit territory-style counting within an area-scoring framework.

evidence.note: BGA comparison explicitly supports both definitions, defensive-fill consequence and pass-stone accommodation; the card avoids claiming universal exact equality of final counts.

original_record.label: Area and territory scoring in Go
original_record.learning_takeaway: Compare counting occupied points with counting territory plus prisoners.

relations.note: The comparison identifies these as alternative Go scoring systems and explains their practical counting differences.

original_record.card: An area cartogram resizes places according to a chosen quantity, such as population. Geographic area becomes a visual measure of that variable instead of land size. The transformation can make comparisons striking, while distorting familiar shapes or spatial relationships that help readers recognize places.

evidence.note: Variable-proportional area and distortion tradeoffs are explained.

original_record.label: Area cartogram
original_record.learning_takeaway: Resizing geographic units according to a quantity displays that variable directly, at a cost to familiar shape or adjacency.

relations.note: Cartograms alter area to encode quantity; choropleths typically retain areas and change their shading.
Resizing areas to encode a variable is a particular representational choice in mapmaking.

original_record.card: Argo floats repeatedly move through the ocean to measure conditions such as temperature and salinity. Pumping oil into an external bladder changes volume without changing mass, allowing a float to rise or sink. On a typical profiling cycle, it surfaces to transmit data, then descends again.

evidence.locator: What does an Argo float do?; External bladder
evidence.note: The Argo program describes its standard profiling mission, CTD measurements, buoyancy changes through an oil bladder and satellite communication at the surface. The card marks this as a typical cycle.

original_record.label: Argo
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explore how buoyancy-changing floats repeatedly profile the ocean and return data by satellite.

relations.note: Argo is a named observational system that supplies oceanographic measurements through repeated profiles.

original_record.card: The Arrhenius equation connects a reaction’s rate constant with temperature and activation energy. Measuring rates at several temperatures can reveal the barrier through a graph of logarithmic rate constant against inverse temperature. This inference assumes the reaction follows the Arrhenius model over that range.

evidence.locator: 12.5 Collision Theory; inspected passage indices 24, 25, 26, 29, 30 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-idm93458160; fs-idp69522176; fs-idm378964576; fs-idm217118448; fs-idm161357136
evidence.note: Use temperature-dependent rate measurements to infer activation energy under the Arrhenius model.

original_record.label: Arrhenius equation
original_record.learning_takeaway: Use temperature-dependent rate measurements to infer activation energy under the Arrhenius model.

relations.note: The source presents an Arrhenius plot as a method of determining activation energy.

original_record.card: An arterial blood gas test analyzes a blood sample for oxygen, carbon dioxide and pH. These measurements address oxygenation, removal of carbon dioxide and acid–base balance together. Unlike a light-based pulse-oximeter reading, the test requires blood from an artery and supplies information beyond oxygen saturation.

evidence.locator: What is an arterial blood gas test?
evidence.note: Supports arterial blood sampling and the oxygen, carbon dioxide and pH measurements.
Supports the light-based, noninvasive oxygen-saturation comparison.

original_record.label: Arterial blood gas testing
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish blood oxygenation, carbon-dioxide removal and acid-base measurements in one arterial sample.

relations.note: An arterial sample can assess CO2 and pH alongside oxygen, whereas the optical method estimates saturation; the methods are not interchangeable.

original_record.card: An artesian aquifer holds groundwater under pressure beneath relatively impermeable layers. Water in a well tapping it can rise above the aquifer’s top, but water flows out at the surface only if the pressure level is high enough. Depth alone does not make a well artesian.

evidence.locator: Artesian Water; Example of an aquifer system
evidence.note: USGS distinguishes confined pressure, rise above the aquifer, flowing versus nonflowing wells and the insufficiency of depth alone.

original_record.label: Artesian aquifer
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explain why confined water rises in a well but may not flow out at the surface.

relations.note: Pressure in confined groundwater and deliberate recharge address different aspects of underground water storage; the comparison does not imply Sand Hollow is an artesian system.

original_record.card: An ascending open auction raises the price while bidders remain active or drop out. When only one bidder remains willing to continue, that bidder wins. Unlike sealed bids, the process makes others' continued participation visible, so the sequence itself can convey information during the auction.

evidence.note: Checked rising-price/dropout mechanism and observable participation; no claim that every online auction implements this exact format.

original_record.label: Ascending open auction
original_record.learning_takeaway: Reveal progressively higher offers until only one bidder remains willing to pay the rising price.

relations.note: The lecture contrasts open ascending participation with privately submitted sealed bids, explaining each format's sequence.

original_record.card: In Asch's line-judgment experiments, participants heard a group give an obviously wrong answer before responding aloud. Many agreed with the group at least once. Dissenting allies and private responding changed conformity, showing that agreement depended partly on the social arrangement of the task.

evidence.note: Section 12.4 supports confederates' wrong answers, public responses and effects of dissent/privacy; many avoids generalizing one percentage to all studies or people.

original_record.label: Asch's conformity experiments
original_record.learning_takeaway: Examine public agreement with a clearly mistaken majority in a particular experimental setting.

relations.note: The textbook explicitly interprets conformity in the unambiguous Asch task as fitting in and avoiding ridicule, an instance of normative influence.

original_record.card: An ascribed status is a social position assigned without the person's choosing it, such as being someone's child. The status comes with expectations and relationships. It describes how the position is acquired, which is different from the behavior people perform while occupying that position.

evidence.note: Checked acquisition without choice and child example; no inference about an individual's worth, ability or immutable destiny.

original_record.label: Ascribed status
original_record.learning_takeaway: Identify social positions assigned without personal choice and the expectations attached to them.

relations.note: The roles-and-status passage explicitly contrasts ascribed positions with achieved ones and separates status from expected role behavior.

original_record.card: The assembling perspective examines what people in crowds actually do: gather, orient together, move, speak, or manipulate objects. It shifts attention toward component actions and the lifecycle of gatherings. This makes coordination observable, though critics argue that focusing so closely on actions can miss wider cultural context.

evidence.note: Checked component examples, gathering lifecycle and criticism; not portrayed as evidence that every crowd has one mind or one shared purpose.

original_record.label: Assembling perspective
original_record.learning_takeaway: Examine how gatherings form and act through observable component processes instead of treating a crowd as one mind.

relations.note: The chapter explicitly presents McPhail's assembling perspective as a process-focused approach to collective behavior and notes its contextual limitation.

original_record.card: Astronomical interferometry combines signals from separated antennas so they operate together as an observing instrument. In ALMA, changing antenna configurations changes the maximum separation and the angular detail the array resolves. The arrangement turns carefully coordinated measurements into a larger effective observing baseline.

evidence.locator: ALMA; inspected passage indices 14 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-15
evidence.note: Combine separated antennas as one telescope and vary their spacing to change angular resolution.

original_record.label: Astronomical interferometry
original_record.learning_takeaway: Combine separated antennas as one telescope and vary their spacing to change angular resolution.

relations.note: ESO explicitly identifies ALMA’s cooperating antennas as an interferometer.

original_record.card: Astronomical seeing describes the blurring produced when starlight crosses turbulent air. Patches with different temperatures bend rays differently, and moving air continually changes those paths. The resulting image shifts and blurs; related fluctuations can also make stars appear to twinkle when seen from the ground.

evidence.locator: 6.2 Telescopes Today; inspected passage indices 37, 38, 39 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-id1167471084189; fs-id1167470709434; fs-id1167470679458
evidence.note: Turbulent air continually redirects starlight, blurring ground-based images and making stars twinkle.

original_record.label: Astronomical seeing
original_record.learning_takeaway: Turbulent air continually redirects starlight, blurring ground-based images and making stars twinkle.

relations.note: The telescope section explains adaptive optics immediately as a response to this atmospheric blurring.

original_record.card: The Atlas linguistique de la France turned regional speech observations into maps. Around the turn of the twentieth century, fieldwork gathered detailed transcriptions from hundreds of French locations. The atlas shows how systematically placing comparable forms on maps can make geographical variation visible rather than merely listing local words.

evidence.note: Checked survey scale, transcription and mapping; omitted the source's apparent fieldworker-name typo rather than reproducing it.

original_record.label: Atlas linguistique de la France
original_record.learning_takeaway: See how mapped transcriptions from many places make regional language variation inspectable.

relations.note: The atlas is a named collection of geographically organized language observations, providing a historical comparison with modern sociolinguistic corpora.

original_record.card: Atmospheric perspective suggests distance by changing the color and tone of receding forms. A landscape can gradually shift from foreground to background as though intervening air alters its appearance. The painter creates depth through these transitions rather than relying only on the geometry of drawn edges.

evidence.note: Distance-related color and tonal changes are explicitly described.

original_record.label: Atmospheric perspective
original_record.learning_takeaway: Changing color and tone as a landscape recedes can represent the effect of atmosphere and create pictorial depth.

relations.note: Compare distance-dependent tonal changes with soft contour transitions; the pictorial purposes differ.

original_record.card: An atmospheric river is a concentrated corridor of water vapor moving through the atmosphere. When it reaches land, that moisture can fall as rain or snow. Such events supply useful water, but stronger or persistent landfalls can also produce flooding, so their effects depend on the event.

evidence.note: NOAA defines water-vapor transport and explains landfall precipitation, water-supply importance and potential flooding.

original_record.label: Atmospheric river
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect a concentrated corridor of water-vapor transport with both useful precipitation and flood risk.

relations.note: Mountain lifting can turn transported vapor into uneven precipitation, connecting atmospheric-river supply with rain-shadow geography.

original_record.card: Atomic commit makes a transaction's changes appear all-or-nothing, even though storage writes occur sequentially. SQLite uses recovery mechanisms to preserve that appearance across crashes or power failures under documented storage assumptions. The guarantee concerns which changes take effect, rather than requiring hardware to write everything simultaneously.

evidence.locator: Section 1 Introduction; Section 2 Hardware Assumptions; Section 3.5 Creating A Rollback Journal File
evidence.note: The all-or-nothing appearance is described in Section 1; Section 2 explicitly states storage/OS assumptions behind crash recovery, including correct flush behavior and uncorrupted stored content. Section 3.5 supplies rollback-journal preservation as the related mechanism.
Supplementary inspected premise for the card or its comparison: SQLite's atomic-commit documentation explains rollback journals as the recovery mechanism used for atomic commit in rollback mode.

original_record.label: Atomic commit
original_record.learning_takeaway: Make a transaction appear all-or-nothing even though storage writes happen sequentially and can be interrupted.

relations.note: SQLite's atomic-commit documentation explains rollback journals as the recovery mechanism used for atomic commit in rollback mode.

original_record.card: Stretch of the heart’s atria can stimulate release of atrial natriuretic peptide. The signal promotes sodium and water loss through the kidneys and suppresses hormones that retain them. It connects increased cardiac filling with a response that helps reduce excess circulating volume.

evidence.note: The atrial-natriuretic paragraph describes stretch-triggered secretion, sodium/water loss and opposition to renin, aldosterone and ADH.

original_record.label: Atrial natriuretic peptide
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explain how cardiac stretch signals the kidneys to lose sodium and water.

relations.note: ANP’s excretory response opposes the sodium/water-retaining hormonal cascade, a physiological comparison rather than identity equivalence.

original_record.card: An augmented sixth chord contains notes a semitone below and above the dominant scale degree. The raised fourth moves upward while the lowered sixth moves downward toward dominant pitches. This characteristic voice-leading explains the chord family's predominant role in the cited tonal framework.

evidence.note: Puget Sound 21.1 states simultaneous semitone approaches to scale degree five and predominant function. Revised wording avoids describing the voices as converging in register; it only states the supported pitch-class movements.

original_record.label: Augmented sixth chord
original_record.learning_takeaway: Follow two chromatic voices approaching the dominant from opposite semitone directions.

relations.note: Both are chromatic predominant devices, but their construction differs: semitone approaches to dominant pitches versus a lowered-supertonic major triad.

original_record.card: Authentication rate limiting restricts repeated failed login attempts. A verifier might impose waiting periods or disable an authenticator after too many failures. These controls make online guessing harder, but designers must also consider attackers who deliberately trigger the limit to lock out legitimate users.

evidence.note: Checked throttling, increasing waits, disabling, and lockout tradeoff; no fixed attempt count is presented as a universal recommendation.

Supplementary inspected premise for the card or its comparison: Limiting online authentication guesses protects access decisions; NIST explicitly discusses both guessing resistance and malicious lockout risks.

original_record.label: Authentication rate limiting
original_record.learning_takeaway: Constrain failed online guesses while balancing attack resistance against legitimate users being locked out.

relations.note: Limiting online authentication guesses protects access decisions; NIST explicitly discusses both guessing resistance and malicious lockout risks.

original_record.card: Autochrome makes a color transparency on glass using a screen of tiny colored starch grains. Light passes through this filtering layer as part of the photographic process. The resulting color image depends on the arrangement of the grains, not simply on coloring a monochrome print afterward.

evidence.note: Colored starch filter and glass transparency are described.

original_record.label: Autochrome
original_record.learning_takeaway: A layer of colored starch grains acts as a filter in a glass photographic plate, producing a color transparency rather than an ordinary monochrome print.

relations.note: Autochrome is a particular material solution for making color photographic images.

original_record.card: Bach's C-minor fugue from the first Well-Tempered Clavier offers a compact lesson in contrapuntal development. Its opening exposition introduces the subject in every voice. Episodes then work with smaller fragments of subjects and countersubjects, allowing recognizable material to generate passages without a complete subject statement.

evidence.note: The detailed analysis identifies first exposition, all-voice entries and fragmented material in episodes; no unsupported numerical count of voices or episodes is added.

original_record.label: Bach's Fugue in C minor, BWV 847
original_record.learning_takeaway: Trace full subject entries alternating with development through fragmented motives.

relations.note: The source explicitly analyzes BWV 847 as a fugue with expositions and episodes.

original_record.card: Bach's C-major Invention shows how a short idea can sustain development. The opening notes return with their melodic direction inverted, and fragments also appear in rhythmic augmentation. These transformations preserve recognizable material while changing its contour or the amount of time it occupies.

evidence.note: Section 11.2 identifies the first seven notes inverted later and an augmented fragment; the wording does not claim every occurrence transforms the whole theme.

original_record.label: Bach's Invention in C major, BWV 772
original_record.learning_takeaway: Recognize inversion and rhythmic augmentation within one tightly developed keyboard work.

relations.note: The textbook explicitly labels the invention's returning opening notes as melodic inversion.

original_record.card: Back-calculation anti-windup feeds information about an actuator’s saturation back into a controller’s integrator. The feedback unwinds internal demand that the actuator cannot realize. This helps the controller return to its usable range more quickly after saturation, rather than waiting for accumulated error to disappear unaided.

evidence.locator: Anti-Windup Control Using PID Controller Block; inspected passage indices 16, 17, 18 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-17; paragraph-18; paragraph-19
evidence.note: Feed saturation information back into a controller’s integrator so it unwinds toward an achievable output.

original_record.label: Back-calculation anti-windup
original_record.learning_takeaway: Feed saturation information back into a controller’s integrator so it unwinds toward an achievable output.

relations.note: The reference explicitly describes back-calculation as a response to integrator windup under saturation.

original_record.card: Bali’s protected subak landscape links forests, water temples, canals and rice terraces across volcanic watersheds. These components show how farming and ritual organization work through the same environment. The place makes an irrigation institution visible through the connected spaces and structures that sustain it.
