original_record.card: Eternalism holds that past and future objects exist as well as present ones. An object can belong to reality without occupying the present moment. The disagreement with presentism concerns what exists, rather than whether past events are now occurring or can presently be observed.

evidence.locator: 6 Presentism, Eternalism, and the Growing Block Theory
evidence.note: SEP Time section 6 separates ontological existence from temporal location and includes past and future objects. The card avoids an extra spatial analogy and does not claim past events are happening at the present time.

original_record.label: Eternalism
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish existing from being present when considering past and future objects.

relations.note: Section 6 explicitly defines eternalism as a way of opposing presentism's restriction of existence to present objects.

original_record.card: An ideal straight, slender column can lose stability and bend sideways under axial compression. Euler’s pinned-end model makes the critical load proportional to elastic modulus and second moment of area, and inversely proportional to length squared. The result assumes linear elasticity and correctly specified end conditions.

evidence.locator: Chapter 8: Beam Bending, Buckling, and Torsion; inspected passage indices 225, 230, 231, 236, 237, 238, 239, 240, 241, 242 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-226; paragraph-231; paragraph-232; paragraph-237; paragraph-238; paragraph-239; paragraph-240; paragraph-241; paragraph-242; paragraph-243
evidence.note: An ideal slender elastic column loses stability at a load controlled by stiffness, length, and end constraints.

original_record.label: Euler column buckling
original_record.learning_takeaway: An ideal slender elastic column loses stability at a load controlled by stiffness, length, and end constraints.

relations.note: The source’s Euler critical-load formula explicitly depends on the cross-section’s second moment of area.

original_record.card: For a polyhedron with sphere-like topology, the number of vertices minus edges plus faces equals two. This is the genus-zero case of the Euler characteristic. The condition matters: a surface with a handle changes the topological count, so the formula is not universal for all polyhedra.

evidence.locator: Polyhedral Formula -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1, 2, 3 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2; paragraph-3; paragraph-4
evidence.note: States the vertex-edge-face formula for genus-zero polyhedra.

evidence.locator: Euler Characteristic -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1, 2, 3 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2; paragraph-3; paragraph-4
evidence.note: Explicitly connects the polyhedral formula with the genus-zero Euler characteristic.

original_record.label: Euler’s polyhedron formula
original_record.learning_takeaway: For a sphere-like polyhedron, vertices minus edges plus faces equals two.

relations.note: The Euler-characteristic reference explicitly identifies the polyhedral formula as its genus-zero special case.

original_record.card: Sweat cools the body when it evaporates from the skin and carries heat into the surrounding air. Producing liquid alone is not the whole cooling mechanism. The response works alongside changes in skin blood flow as part of the body’s feedback control of temperature.

evidence.note: The homeostasis passage links increased sweating, skin blood flow and heat removed as sweat evaporates.

original_record.label: Evaporative cooling by sweating
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explain why sweat cools the body when it evaporates from the skin.

relations.note: Sweating is an effector response in the cited temperature-regulation feedback example.

original_record.card: A feature’s current job need not be the reason it originally evolved. Exaptation describes a trait co-opted for a use that did not originally shape it by natural selection. Feathers possibly selected for insulation before flight illustrate the distinction between origin and later function.

evidence.note: Berkeley defines co-option and presents insulation-first feathers as a possible historical example.

original_record.label: Exaptation
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish a trait’s present use from the selective context in which it arose.

relations.note: Comparing exaptation with convergence separates a change of function in an inherited feature from the independent evolution of similar functions.

original_record.card: A researcher's expectations can influence how ambiguous observations are scored. Someone who knows which participants received an intervention may interpret borderline responses in its favor. Concealing group assignments from the scorer helps reduce this route of bias, without guaranteeing that every other source of error disappears.

evidence.note: Section 2.3's test-scoring example motivates observer blinding; helps reduce avoids the textbook's stronger implication that blinding alone removes all alternative explanations.

original_record.label: Experimenter expectancy bias
original_record.learning_takeaway: Understand how a researcher's expectations can shape interpretation of ambiguous responses.

relations.note: The source introduces researcher blinding to address experimenter expectations and then defines double blinding as concealing assignment from participants as well.

original_record.card: The exponential distribution models waiting times between events in a positive constant-rate Poisson process. Its probability density decreases as the waiting time grows. It is memoryless: having already waited does not change the distribution of the additional time until the next event.

evidence.locator: Exponential Distribution -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1, 2, 4 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2; paragraph-3; paragraph-5
evidence.note: Model waiting times between events of a constant-rate Poisson process with a continuous memoryless law.

original_record.label: Exponential distribution
original_record.learning_takeaway: Model waiting times between events of a constant-rate Poisson process with a continuous memoryless law.

relations.note: The source derives exponential waiting times from the Poisson event model.

original_record.card: An eye is an internal space in a connected Go group. Two genuine, separate eyes can keep a group safe: an opponent cannot fill both in one move, and occupying the first would be self-capture rather than capturing the surrounding stones.

evidence.locator: Life and death and the concept of eyes
evidence.note: BGA Life and death and self-capture examples support two-eye safety; genuine eyes prevents confusing superficial holes with the protected spaces in the rule explanation.

original_record.label: Eyes in Go
original_record.learning_takeaway: Understand why two separate internal spaces protect a group from capture.

relations.note: The guide explains eye-based survival through internal liberties and the prohibition on noncapturing self-capture.

original_record.card: A monatomic face-centered cubic structure places atoms at cube corners and face centers. Shared boundaries leave four atoms per conventional cell, with twelve nearest neighbors around each atom. The arrangement can also be described as cubic close packing, using an ABC layer sequence.

evidence.locator: 10.6 Lattice Structures in Crystalline Solids; inspected passage indices 31, 32 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-idp30613264; fs-idp4268832
evidence.note: Corner and face atoms form a close-packed cubic structure with four atoms per conventional cell.

original_record.label: Face-centered cubic structure
original_record.learning_takeaway: Corner and face atoms form a close-packed cubic structure with four atoms per conventional cell.

relations.note: The source explicitly contrasts ABC cubic close packing with AB hexagonal close packing.

original_record.card: Faded worked examples gradually turn a demonstrated solution into a problem the learner completes. Early steps may remain visible while later steps are removed. As expertise develops, learners supply more of the solution themselves, creating a transition from studying a model to carrying out the procedure independently.

evidence.note: Checked direction of fading and expertise-dependent increase in responsibility; not merely shortening an explanation arbitrarily.

original_record.label: Faded worked examples
original_record.learning_takeaway: Gradually remove later solution steps so learners supply more of the solution as expertise develops.

relations.note: The guide explicitly describes fading by retaining early steps and requiring progressively more later steps from learners.

original_record.card: Fahrenheit 451 follows a book-burning fireman whose allegiance changes as he begins reading. Its major sections end in increasingly expansive fires, while a community of readers preserves books through memory. An editorial reading connects these elements with the vulnerability of cultural memory.

evidence.note: Fireman’s change, three escalating fires and memorizing community are described.

original_record.label: Fahrenheit 451
original_record.learning_takeaway: The book-burning fireman’s changing allegiance is structured through expanding fires and a counter-community that preserves books by memory.

relations.note: The NEA guide compares imagined worlds as a means of exposing familiar social flaws.

original_record.card: Fail-safe defaults make lack of permission the starting point for access decisions. A system grants access only when a rule explicitly permits it. If a permission rule is missing or incomplete, the design tends to deny access instead of accidentally creating an unprotected opening.

evidence.note: Checked allow-by-rule versus exclusion-list design; fail-safe here concerns authorization defaults, not every conceivable hardware failure.

original_record.label: Fail-safe defaults
original_record.learning_takeaway: Deny access unless a permission rule explicitly allows it so missing rules tend to fail closed.

relations.note: The protection paper explicitly names permission-based default denial as a security design principle.

original_record.card: Network Rail describes a fail-safe response in which a failed track circuit normally indicates occupancy. Trains can be stopped even when none is present because reliable clearance is lost. This favors a restrictive signal over uninterrupted service while the section’s status is uncertain.

evidence.locator: Track circuits explained; inspected passage indices 8, 9, 10, 12 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-9; paragraph-10; paragraph-11; paragraph-13
evidence.note: Many circuit failures are treated as occupied track, prioritizing safe train separation over uninterrupted service.

original_record.label: Fail-safe track-circuit signalling
original_record.learning_takeaway: Many circuit failures are treated as occupied track, prioritizing safe train separation over uninterrupted service.

relations.note: The operator explains this fail-safe occupied response as a behavior of track circuits.

original_record.card: In the fake-barn case, Henry happens to see a real barn in a landscape full of convincing facades. His belief is true and apparently justified, yet could easily have been mistaken. The example challenges whether accurate perception alone guarantees knowledge in a systematically deceptive environment.

evidence.note: SEP section 4's Barn County passage supplies Henry, the real barn and facades; apparently and challenges preserve the evaluative character of the knowledge verdict.

original_record.label: Fake-barn case
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explore how a deceptive environment can undermine otherwise accurate perception.

relations.note: The source presents Barn County as a challenge to the no-false-lemmas repair because Henry's belief need not involve inference from a false premise.

original_record.card: Fangyan is a Han-era collection of regional words associated with the scholar Yang Xiong. By recording different expressions and pronunciations across places, it preserved evidence about linguistic diversity. Later scholars used that material to infer earlier dialect groupings, showing how a vocabulary work can become historical evidence.

evidence.locator: §10.5, Dialectology: Then and now, Yang Xiong paragraph
evidence.note: Checked regional vocabulary, Yang Xiong attribution, and later scholarly use; no unverified precise date or exhaustive dialect classification is asserted.

Supplementary inspected premise for the card or its comparison: The methods chapter describes later inferences about earlier dialect groups from Fangyan, linking the particular work to historical language study.

original_record.label: Fangyan
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explore how a Han-era collection of regional words preserves evidence used to infer earlier dialect groupings.

relations.note: The methods chapter describes later inferences about earlier dialect groups from Fangyan, linking the particular work to historical language study.

original_record.card: Faraday’s laws connect electrical charge with the amount of material transformed during electrolysis. Charge gives the number of transferred electrons; the balanced electrode reaction gives how many electrons each converted ion requires. Equal charge can therefore deposit different amounts of different metals.

evidence.locator: 17.7 Electrolysis; inspected passage indices 27, 28, 29 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-idm90272368; fs-idm90332432; fs-idm371971168
evidence.note: Convert transferred electric charge into deposited material using the reaction’s electron stoichiometry.

original_record.label: Faraday’s laws of electrolysis
original_record.learning_takeaway: Convert transferred electric charge into deposited material using the reaction’s electron stoichiometry.

relations.note: The electrolysis section derives stoichiometric material calculations from the charge transferred in the electrode reaction.

original_record.card: John Ashbery’s Farm Implements and Rutabagas in a Landscape places Popeye characters inside a sestina. Recurring end-words produce comic surprises while domestic unease persists beneath them. The poem demonstrates how a demanding inherited form can accommodate cartoon familiarity, melancholy and playful resistance to its own constraints.

evidence.note: The glossary describes the Popeye cast, comic recurrence and domestic pathos.

original_record.label: Farm Implements and Rutabagas in a Landscape
original_record.learning_takeaway: Ashbery places Popeye characters in a sestina whose repeated words produce comic surprises alongside domestic unease.

relations.note: The glossary names the poem as a playful use of the sestina form.

original_record.card: Under fixed conditions, each successive half-life of a first-order reaction removes half the reactant still present. The half-life depends on the rate constant, not the starting concentration. Equal time intervals therefore produce equal fractional losses rather than equal amounts disappearing.

evidence.locator: 12.4 Integrated Rate Laws; inspected passage indices 70, 72, 74, 75 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-idm99562880; fs-idp162624; fs-idp123084256; fs-idm124479504
evidence.note: First-order half-life depends on the rate constant rather than the initial reactant concentration.

original_record.label: First-order reaction half-life
original_record.learning_takeaway: First-order half-life depends on the rate constant rather than the initial reactant concentration.

relations.note: The integrated-rate section explicitly contrasts the concentration-independent first-order half-life with other orders.

original_record.card: In a first-price sealed-bid auction, bidders submit offers privately, the highest bidder wins, and the winner pays their own bid. The bid therefore helps determine both the chance of winning and the payment if successful. That payment rule differs from a second-price auction.

evidence.note: Checked sealed submission, highest-bid winner and own payment; no unqualified optimal-bidding formula or revenue comparison is asserted.

original_record.label: First-price sealed-bid auction
original_record.learning_takeaway: Submit bids privately and let the highest bidder win while paying their own bid.

relations.note: The Yale lecture directly compares highest-bid allocation with own-bid versus second-highest-bid payment rules.

original_record.card: A flat-felled seam wraps one fabric edge within a folded edge and secures the assembly flat with stitching. The enclosed raw edges and additional stitching produce a durable finish familiar from jeans and other hard-wearing garments. Its flattened construction distinguishes it from a French seam’s enclosed ridge.

evidence.note: Supports folded enclosure, stitching flat, durability and jeans use.
Supports the contrast with enclosing one seam inside another.

original_record.label: Flat-felled seam
original_record.learning_takeaway: Create an enclosed-edge seam that is folded down and secured flat with visible stitching.

relations.note: The connection compares two genuinely different enclosed-edge constructions rather than counting synonymous finishes.

original_record.card: Florence Nightingale used mortality data to argue for changes in military health care after the Crimean War. Her campaign involved checking inconsistent records and communicating results through writing and the Rose Diagram. The example joins data reconstruction with making statistical evidence understandable to a broader audience.

evidence.locator: Abstract; Rose Diagram; mortality dataset reconstruction
evidence.note: The historical research article describes seven months of dataset checking, the sanitary-reform campaign and collaboration with Martineau using prose and the Rose Diagram.

original_record.label: Florence Nightingale
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explore how checking mortality records and explaining them visually supported sanitary reform.

relations.note: Using population mortality evidence to campaign for sanitary reform is a specific historical example of public-health reasoning.

original_record.card: Focalization concerns how a narrative selects or restricts information in relation to what characters or narrators can know. It differs from identifying who speaks. A story may remain close to one character’s knowledge even when someone else supplies the narrative voice.

evidence.note: Information restriction and separation from narrative voice are explained.

original_record.label: Focalization
original_record.learning_takeaway: The information a narrative reveals can be limited by a character’s knowledge without making that character the speaker.

relations.note: Narrator participation and limits on available information are separate analytical questions.

original_record.card: FOIA segregability means an exempt passage does not necessarily justify withholding an entire record. Federal agencies must consider partial disclosure and release reasonably separable nonexempt portions after redaction. The practical question is what can still be disclosed without revealing the information protected by a valid exemption.

evidence.note: 5 USC 552(a)(8)(A)(ii) and the final paragraph of (b) require reasonable segregation and partial release; reasonably and valid exemption preserve limits rather than promising every document has releasable fragments.

original_record.label: FOIA segregability
original_record.learning_takeaway: See why an exempt passage need not justify withholding the entire record.

relations.note: The statute itself imposes partial-disclosure and segregation duties within FOIA, tying the mechanism directly to the federal records-access regime.

original_record.card: The foot-in-the-door technique begins with a small request before asking for something larger. In Freedman and Fraser's study, people who first accepted a small sign or petition were more likely to accept a large yard sign. This was an experimental tendency, not guaranteed compliance.

evidence.note: Section 12.3 describes the 1966 sign/petition comparison; the final sentence preserves probabilistic scope and avoids presenting a guaranteed method of controlling another person.

original_record.label: Foot-in-the-door technique
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explore the qualified finding that a small request can precede increased agreement to a larger one.

relations.note: Compare a request-sequencing procedure with a model of message processing. Both concern persuasion, but the cited section does not make one an instance of the other.

original_record.card: Passing in Othello is compulsory when you cannot legally outflank an opposing disc, but forbidden when a legal move is available. Your opponent may therefore move twice in succession. If neither player can move, the game ends even when some squares remain empty.

evidence.note: World Othello rules 2 and 8 support mandatory pass, prohibition of voluntary pass and early ending; no claim that every pass immediately ends play.

original_record.label: Forced passing in Othello
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish being unable to move from choosing to pass strategically.

relations.note: The official game rules define passing entirely through legal outflanking moves.

original_record.card: A formal organization specifies official relationships, responsibilities, and reporting lines. Its chart shows how work is supposed to be coordinated and who is accountable for particular duties. That planned structure may differ from the informal network of people others actually consult to get things done.

evidence.note: Checked planned versus emergent relationships; formal structure is not treated as a complete description of everyday behavior.

original_record.label: Formal organization
original_record.learning_takeaway: Specify official roles, reporting lines, and responsibilities so work has an explicit coordination structure.

relations.note: The source explicitly contrasts officially defined formal relationships with emergent informal ties and their practical influence.

original_record.card: Formative assessment uses evidence during learning to improve what happens next. An instructor may identify a misconception and adjust teaching, while a learner redirects study. The defining feature is this feedback purpose: even information from a final exam can later be used formatively in another course.

evidence.note: Checked ongoing feedback and later formative use of summative information; low stakes is typical rather than a necessary definition.

evidence.locator: What is it?; distinction from teaching for mastery
evidence.note: Supplementary inspected premise for the card or its comparison: Mastery learning uses checks and corrective support to guide progression, providing a specific comparison with formative assessment's broader feedback purpose.

original_record.label: Formative assessment
original_record.learning_takeaway: Use evidence during learning to adjust teaching and study, with purpose mattering more than a test's format.

relations.note: Mastery learning uses checks and corrective support to guide progression, providing a specific comparison with formative assessment's broader feedback purpose.

original_record.card: The Forth railway bridge uses a double-cantilever arrangement to carry trains across an estuary. Its design followed abandonment of an earlier scheme after the Tay Bridge collapse. Large steel spans and shipping clearance show how a railway crossing must also accommodate the waterway beneath it.

evidence.locator:
Firth of Forth Railway Bridge | ASCE
; inspected passage indices 6, 9, 10 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-7; paragraph-10; paragraph-11
evidence.note: A double-cantilever design carried railway spans across the Forth after an earlier proposal was abandoned.

original_record.label: Forth Bridge
original_record.learning_takeaway: A double-cantilever design carried railway spans across the Forth after an earlier proposal was abandoned.

relations.note: ASCE identifies the structure as a railway bridge and explicitly describes its double-cantilever design.

original_record.card: Forward secrecy limits the damage from later compromise of a long-term key. In an appropriate protocol mode, revealing that key after a handshake does not reveal the earlier session key. The guarantee depends on conditions such as erasing session secrets; it does not cover every pre-shared-key mode.

evidence.locator: Appendix E.1, Forward secret with respect to long-term keys
evidence.note: Checked compromise timing, erased session-key condition, and PSK-only exception; secrecy is not promised after the session key itself is exposed.

original_record.label: Forward secrecy
original_record.learning_takeaway: Keep earlier session keys safe after later long-term-key compromise, subject to the protocol's mode and key-erasure assumptions.

relations.note: RFC 8446 Appendix E explicitly defines forward secrecy relative to long-term keys and names a PSK mode that lacks it.

original_record.card: Foundation species help build the physical setting of a community. Kelp forms underwater forests, while reef-building corals create habitats used by many other organisms. Their importance comes from shaping the environment that supports the community, rather than simply being another species within it.

evidence.note: OpenStax’s Foundation Species passage identifies kelp forests and coral habitat construction as community-shaping examples.

original_record.label: Foundation species
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect habitat structure supplied by organisms with the communities that depend on it.

relations.note: Habitat construction by foundation species can be compared with ecosystem engineering, while avoiding an assertion that the two categories are identical.

original_record.card: When a new population begins with only a few colonists, its genetic frequencies can differ markedly from the source population. The founder effect arises because those founders are a small sample. Their descendants may inherit unusual frequencies without the variants offering any local advantage.

evidence.note: The Berkeley founder-effect section describes colonization by a few individuals and altered genetic variation/frequencies through sampling.

original_record.label: Founder effect
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explain how a few colonists can establish unrepresentative genetic frequencies.

relations.note: Founding a population from a small sample is a specific demographic route to drift, distinct from survival after a population crash.

original_record.card: Foxconn appears in The Economy's historical iPhone example as a contract assembler within a wider supply chain. Components came from several other firms and countries, while Apple coordinated the product. The case distinguishes assembling a finished device from producing all its parts or owning the consumer-facing product.

evidence.note: Checked case framing and component/assembly distinction; did not assert that Foxconn currently assembles every Apple device or that assembly captures all product value.

original_record.label: Foxconn
original_record.learning_takeaway: See how contract assembly fits into a larger value chain whose components and product ownership sit elsewhere.

relations.note: The inspected textbook directly relates Foxconn's assembly role to Apple's historical product supply chain.

original_record.card: Fracture toughness describes a material’s resistance to extension of an existing crack. In linear-elastic fracture mechanics, crack growth can become unstable when stress intensity reaches the appropriate critical value. This connects material resistance with flaw size and loading, rather than treating applied stress alone as sufficient.

evidence.locator: Chapter 10: Creep, Fracture, and Fatigue; inspected passage indices 142, 143, 144, 145 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-143; paragraph-144; paragraph-145; paragraph-146
evidence.note: Compare crack-tip loading with a material’s resistance to crack extension.

original_record.label: Fracture toughness
original_record.learning_takeaway: Compare crack-tip loading with a material’s resistance to crack extension.

relations.note: The source states the fracture condition by comparing applied stress intensity with the material’s critical toughness.

original_record.card: Frame alignment connects a movement's interpretations and goals with potential participants or allied groups. Shared concerns may be bridged, emphasized, extended, or transformed to support cooperation. The concept focuses on how people understand an issue and their relationship to it, rather than only counting the movement's resources.

evidence.note: Checked the four named alignment processes and audience/goal connection; not reduced to organizational merger alone or asserted as a guarantee of recruitment.

original_record.label: Frame alignment
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect a movement's interpretations and goals with prospective participants or allied groups to support coordinated action.

relations.note: Comparing interpretive alignment with resource acquisition distinguishes two ways the source analyzes collective organizing.

original_record.card: The Framingham Heart Study follows community participants over time, with repeated examinations and later generations joining the research. It connected factors such as blood pressure and cholesterol with future cardiovascular disease. Its long view shows how risk can be studied before illness becomes apparent.

evidence.note: NHLBI describes repeated cohort examinations, multigenerational participation and identification of cardiovascular risk factors including pressure and cholesterol.

original_record.label: Framingham Heart Study
original_record.learning_takeaway: See how repeated examinations across generations established patterns of cardiovascular risk.

relations.note: Population follow-up can identify prevention targets, linking this specific study with public health’s community-level focus.

original_record.card: The US Freedom of Information Act lets people request existing federal agency records, subject to specified exemptions. It does not require an agency to create new records, conduct research or answer a questionnaire. The right therefore concerns access to recorded information rather than a general government research service.

evidence.locator: What is the FOIA?; What can I ask for?
evidence.note: FOIA.gov's definition and What can I ask for? support agency-record scope, exemptions and no new-research obligation; people avoids incorrectly limiting requesters to US citizens.

original_record.label: Freedom of Information Act (United States)
original_record.learning_takeaway: Understand access to existing federal agency records subject to specified exemptions.

relations.note: FOIA concerns access to agency records; the Sunshine Act concerns observation of covered agency meetings. Their comparison distinguishes two transparency mechanisms with different scopes and exceptions.

original_record.card: A French cleat hangs a fixture using two matching beveled strips: one attached to the wall and one to the object. Their opposing slopes engage to carry the load while allowing a flexible storage layout. Secure anchoring and suitable load distribution remain part of the system.

evidence.note: Lee Valley’s workshop account describes wall strips, opposing fixture bevels, movable storage and added cleats for heavier objects.

original_record.label: French cleat
original_record.learning_takeaway: Support a removable wall fixture with two mating beveled strips.

relations.note: The paired wooden strips apply shaped joinery to mounting movable fixtures rather than permanently joining board ends.

original_record.card: A French seam encloses raw fabric edges inside a second seam. The first pass joins the fabric with wrong sides together; after turning, another pass hides that initial allowance. This creates a tidy enclosed finish, useful when exposed edges would show through a sheer fabric.

evidence.note: BERNINA’s original tutorial defines two-part edge enclosure, wrong-sides-first sequencing and usefulness for sheer fabrics.

original_record.label: French seam
original_record.learning_takeaway: Enclose raw fabric edges inside a second seam rather than leaving them exposed to fray.

relations.note: Both enclose raw edges, but a French seam contains the first seam within a second while a flat-felled seam is secured down flat.

original_record.card: Fresco a secco applies paint to a dry plaster surface. That distinction separates it from buon fresco, where painting takes place while the plaster is wet. Comparing the methods shows why the condition of the wall matters alongside the pigments and the image itself.

evidence.note: Dry-versus-wet plaster distinction is explicit.

original_record.label: Fresco a secco
original_record.learning_takeaway: Fresco a secco applies paint to a dry plaster surface, contrasting with buon fresco on wet plaster.

relations.note: The glossary directly contrasts painting on dry plaster with painting on wet plaster.
The National Gallery distinguishes dry-plaster painting as another wall-painting method.

original_record.card: Functional fixedness restricts thinking about an object to its usual purpose. In Duncker's candle problem, seeing a box only as a container can obscure its use as a candle support. Overcoming that restriction requires reconsidering what the available materials can do.

evidence.note: Section 7.3, Duncker problem and Figure 7.10, support the box's alternative use; the prose avoids repeating the source's apparent typo about using fixedness to overcome the problem.

original_record.label: Functional fixedness
original_record.learning_takeaway: See how an object's conventional use can hide an alternative solution.

relations.note: The source expressly describes functional fixedness as a kind of mental set: a familiar use constrains the attempted solution.

original_record.card: A functional organizational structure groups people by expertise, such as production, marketing, or finance. It supports specialization and clear reporting within departments. The same boundaries can create silos, making cross-department decisions slower or encouraging units to compete for resources instead of coordinating their work.

evidence.note: Checked specialization/reporting benefits and coordination costs; these are potential tendencies, not guaranteed outcomes in every firm.

original_record.label: Functional organizational structure
original_record.learning_takeaway: Group specialists by expertise while recognizing the risk that departmental boundaries hinder coordination.

relations.note: The source contrasts expertise-based departments with divisions that contain several functions around products or markets.

original_record.card: Gaia repeatedly measured stellar positions, distances, motions, and brightness to construct a detailed three-dimensional view of the Milky Way. Its catalog treats stars as moving objects rather than fixed points on a sky map, providing evidence for the Galaxy’s structure, origin, and history.

evidence.locator: ESA; inspected passage indices 7, 8, 10 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-8; paragraph-9; paragraph-11
evidence.note: Repeated positional measurements build a three-dimensional map of stellar distances and motions.

original_record.label: Gaia mission
original_record.learning_takeaway: Repeated positional measurements build a three-dimensional map of stellar distances and motions.

relations.note: ESA explicitly connects Gaia’s positional and velocity measurements with the reconstruction of stellar motions.

original_record.card: In the gambler’s ruin model, two players transfer one unit after each independent fair coin toss until one has everything. With finite starting funds, absorption eventually occurs with probability one. The player starting with less has a greater chance of losing everything despite fair odds.

evidence.locator: Gambler's Ruin -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1, 2, 3 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2; paragraph-3; paragraph-4
evidence.note: Even a fair finite-bankroll game eventually absorbs one player, with ruin odds depending on starting capital.

original_record.label: Gambler’s ruin
original_record.learning_takeaway: Even a fair finite-bankroll game eventually absorbs one player, with ruin odds depending on starting capital.

relations.note: The changing bankroll is a one-dimensional random walk stopped at either boundary; the source’s unit transfers supply the model.

original_record.card: A backgammon loser who has not removed any checkers suffers a gammon, worth twice the doubling cube's value under standard scoring. If that loser also has a checker on the bar or in the winner's home board, the loss is instead a triple-value backgammon.

evidence.note: USBGF Gammons and Backgammons supports the two scoring conditions; standard scoring qualification leaves room for the separately selected optional Jacoby rule.

original_record.label: Gammon
original_record.learning_takeaway: Understand why losing before bearing off any checker doubles the game's value.

relations.note: USBGF explicitly describes Jacoby as an optional rule changing when gammon and backgammon multipliers count.

original_record.card: For a compact smooth two-dimensional surface without boundary, the Gauss–Bonnet theorem links total Gaussian curvature to its Euler characteristic: the curvature integral equals two pi times that number. Changing the shape can redistribute curvature while leaving this topologically determined total unchanged.

evidence.locator: Gauss-Bonnet Formula -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 4, 5 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-5; paragraph-6
evidence.note: For a compact boundaryless surface, total Gaussian curvature is fixed by its Euler characteristic.

original_record.label: Gauss–Bonnet theorem
original_record.learning_takeaway: For a compact boundaryless surface, total Gaussian curvature is fixed by its Euler characteristic.

relations.note: The source explicitly equates total Gaussian curvature with two pi times the Euler characteristic.

original_record.card: Gaussian curvature is the product of the two principal curvatures at a surface point. Matching nonzero signs give a positive product; opposite signs give a negative one. This is an intrinsic geometric quantity, independent of the coordinates chosen to describe the surface.

evidence.locator: Gaussian Curvature -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1, 13, 21, 23 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2; paragraph-14; paragraph-22; paragraph-24
evidence.note: A surface has an intrinsic curvature determined by its two principal curvatures.

original_record.label: Gaussian curvature
original_record.learning_takeaway: A surface has an intrinsic curvature determined by its two principal curvatures.

relations.note: The Gauss–Bonnet formula relates integrated Gaussian curvature to Euler characteristic.

original_record.card: Some inherited disorders appear earlier or become more severe in successive generations. Genetic anticipation can arise when unstable repeated DNA sequences expand during transmission. Differences between relatives alone do not establish it: researchers consider the disorder’s genetic cause and patterns across several generations.

evidence.note: MedlinePlus connects anticipation with earlier/more severe manifestations and repeat expansion, while warning that ordinary variation among relatives has other causes.

original_record.label: Genetic anticipation
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect expanding repeat sequences with earlier or more severe inherited disease in some families.

relations.note: Contrasting anticipation with variable expressivity prevents ordinary differences among affected relatives from being mistaken for a generational expansion pattern.

original_record.card: Nearby positions on a chromosome tend to travel together from parent to offspring. Recombination during the formation of eggs or sperm can separate them, but closer markers are less likely to be split. Genetic linkage turns patterns of joint inheritance into clues about chromosome organization.

evidence.note: NHGRI linkage describes neighboring loci and recombination-dependent joint inheritance; the map definition links proximity to co-inheritance.

original_record.label: Genetic linkage
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect physical proximity on a chromosome with the likelihood of joint inheritance.

relations.note: Linkage mapping uses the co-inheritance pattern described by genetic linkage to infer marker order.

original_record.card: Genetic linkage mapping follows how markers are inherited together across generations. Markers that are rarely separated by recombination are generally closer together on a chromosome. Comparing inheritance patterns lets researchers infer relative order and position, rather than directly reading a physical sequence of DNA bases.

evidence.note: The inspected NHGRI Genetic Map definition specifically identifies linkage maps, co-inheritance, relative marker order and location.

original_record.label: Genetic linkage mapping
original_record.learning_takeaway: Infer marker order from joint inheritance rather than directly measuring physical DNA length.

relations.note: This mapping method applies the proximity-dependent co-inheritance relationship described by genetic linkage.

original_record.card: For some genes, the copy inherited from one parent is active while the other copy is largely switched off. Genomic imprinting establishes this parent-of-origin pattern through epigenetic regulation. It shows why inheriting a gene copy and using that copy are different questions.

evidence.note: The imprinting section identifies maternal-only and paternal-only expression for a small subset of genes and says the epigenome distinguishes their copies.

original_record.label: Genomic imprinting
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explain parent-of-origin gene expression without a difference in the inherited DNA sequence.

relations.note: Parent-of-origin expression is a specific inheritance-related phenomenon within the study of genetics.

original_record.card: The genus of a closed connected surface counts handles when the surface is orientable and cross-caps when it is not. A sphere has orientable genus zero, while a torus has genus one. The definition distinguishes kinds of holes rather than measuring physical size.

evidence.locator: Genus -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1, 2, 3 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2; paragraph-3; paragraph-4
evidence.note: Count handles or cross-caps to distinguish closed surfaces with different topology.

original_record.label: Genus of a surface
original_record.learning_takeaway: Count handles or cross-caps to distinguish closed surfaces with different topology.

relations.note: The source directly gives the relation between surface genus and Euler characteristic.

original_record.card: In Riemannian geometry, a geodesic is a locally length-minimizing path. In a plane it is straight; on a sphere it follows a great circle. Local shortestness matters: continuing along a great circle far enough need not give the shortest route between its endpoints.

evidence.locator: Geodesic -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1, 2 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2; paragraph-3
evidence.note: Locally shortest paths depend on the surface metric; great circles play this role on a sphere.

original_record.label: Geodesic
original_record.learning_takeaway: Locally shortest paths depend on the surface metric; great circles play this role on a sphere.

relations.note: Geodesics add metric information to the study of spaces; topology alone does not fix lengths or shortest paths.

original_record.card: A geographic buffer marks a zone within a chosen distance of a feature. It is useful for proximity questions, but distance alone does not say how someone can travel there. A circular zone around a facility can therefore differ from its reachable area along roads.

evidence.note: Buffer comparison distinguishes geometric proximity from network travel.

original_record.label: Geographic buffer
original_record.learning_takeaway: A fixed-distance zone measures proximity around a feature but does not by itself model roads, barriers or travel time.

relations.note: A network service area can answer the accessibility question that a simple buffer leaves open.

original_record.card: The geometric distribution describes how long repeated independent trials with a fixed positive success probability take to produce a first success. Some conventions count preceding failures from zero; others count trials from one. Keeping that convention explicit prevents an otherwise correct formula from being shifted by one.

evidence.locator: 4.4 Geometric Distribution; inspected passage indices 2, 4, 5, 7, 8 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: list-00001; list-00002
evidence.note: Explains independent fixed-probability trials and failure-count versus trial-count conventions.

evidence.locator: Geometric Distribution -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 3, 4 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-4; paragraph-5
evidence.note: Confirms memorylessness and the alternative zero- and one-based definitions.

original_record.label: Geometric distribution
original_record.learning_takeaway: Model repeated independent trials until success, distinguishing conventions that count trials or preceding failures.

relations.note: The source explicitly states that the geometric distribution is the discrete memoryless distribution.

original_record.card: George Town’s religious buildings, quarters and shophouses preserve the layered history of a trading port. Malay, Chinese, Indian and European influences appear within the same urban setting. The city shows how repeated commercial contact can leave enduring patterns in architecture and communal organization.

evidence.note: Trading-port history and named cultural influences are documented.

original_record.label: George Town, Penang
original_record.learning_takeaway: Religious buildings, ethnic quarters and shophouses show how a trading port accumulated Malay, Chinese, Indian and European influences.

relations.note: The port’s built environment records cultural exchange through settlement patterns.

original_record.card: Germany's eternity clause makes certain constitutional amendments inadmissible, including changes affecting the federal division into Länder and principles protected by Articles 1 and 20. This differs from merely requiring a large majority: Article 79 sets substantive limits that the ordinary two-thirds amendment procedure cannot override.

evidence.note: Basic Law Article 79(2)–(3) distinguishes two-thirds votes from inadmissible amendments; including avoids claiming that the examples exhaust the clause, and no universal claim about all constitutions is made.

original_record.label: German eternity clause
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish a difficult amendment from a constitutionally inadmissible amendment.

relations.note: The clause exemplifies a constitutional limit on the power to amend basic governmental rules; the Basic Law provision and general constitution account support that editorial placement.

original_record.card: The Gettier problem asks why some justified true beliefs still seem not to be knowledge. A person can reason from a justified but false premise to a conclusion that happens to be true for an unrelated reason. The success is accidental despite the apparent justification.

evidence.note: SEP section 3's Smith/Jones disjunction case supports justified false premise, valid inference and accidental truth; some and seem preserve the philosophical status of the counterexample judgment.

original_record.label: Gettier problem
original_record.learning_takeaway: See why a justified belief can be accidentally true yet fail to count as knowledge.

relations.note: Gettier cases are directly formulated as counterexamples to the traditional tripartite analysis, separating justified truth from nonaccidental knowledge.

original_record.card: A ghazal joins relatively autonomous couplets through a shared rhyme-and-refrain pattern. Formal recurrence connects lines whose thoughts may remain distinct. This combination allows unity without continuous narrative, and it creates particular challenges when poets translate or adapt the form into another language.

evidence.note: Couplet autonomy, shared scheme and translation/adaptation challenges are explicit.

original_record.label: Ghazal
original_record.learning_takeaway: Autonomous couplets share a rhyme-and-refrain pattern, joining formal unity with discontinuity of thought.

relations.note: The glossary describes Ali’s advocacy for retaining the form’s constraints in English.
The Academy explains the ghazal through its couplets and poetic rhyme-refrain structure.

original_record.card: Gideon v. Wainwright established the right to appointed counsel for indigent defendants in state felony trials. After Gideon was denied a lawyer, the Supreme Court held that the Sixth Amendment guarantee applies to states through the Fourteenth Amendment. The case concerns fair criminal proceedings, not universal publicly funded legal representation.

evidence.note: US Courts Facts and Reasoning support Florida felony prosecution, indigence, denial and incorporation; the card confines its claim to state felony trials rather than all civil disputes or every minor offense.

original_record.label: Gideon v. Wainwright
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect an indigent defendant's denied lawyer with the right to appointed counsel in state felony trials.

relations.note: The case summary explicitly records Gideon's state habeas petition challenging his detention after the denial of counsel, before his later Supreme Court petition.

original_record.card: A giornata is the section of fresh finishing plaster prepared for a day’s fresco painting. Its size follows what the painter expects to complete while that surface remains workable. The division turns a large wall painting into a sequence of time-sensitive working areas.

evidence.note: A day’s fresh plaster and painting capacity are described.

original_record.label: Giornata
original_record.learning_takeaway: A fresco painter prepares fresh finishing plaster in daily working sections sized to what can be painted while the surface remains workable.

relations.note: Daily plaster sections are part of the wet-plaster fresco workflow.

original_record.card: Benjamin Franklin's glass armonica uses glass bowls of different sizes mounted on a spinning axle. A player's touch sustains their vibration through friction, much as a damp finger can make a glass rim sing. The instrument turns that small physical effect into a playable arrangement of pitches.

evidence.locator: Why does rubbing your finger around the rim of a wine glass make a note?
evidence.note: UNSW wineglass explanation names Franklin, rotating bowls and finger-driven stick-slip; no claim about exact construction dimensions or historical priority beyond the source.

original_record.label: Glass armonica
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect friction-driven glass vibration with Franklin's rotating-bowl instrument.

relations.note: The source compares rubbing glass with a violin bow's sticking and slipping, providing a factual basis for comparing friction-driven sound production.

original_record.card: Wheat flour contains glutenin and gliadin, proteins that form gluten when mixed with water. Working the dough develops a stretchy network that can hold gas bubbles. This connects mixing and kneading with a dough’s ability to expand, rather than treating rising as the yeast’s job alone.

evidence.note: Exploratorium identifies the two wheat proteins, hydration, kneading and gas-retaining gluten structure.

original_record.label: Gluten formation
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect flour hydration and mechanical working with a network that can hold expanding gas.

relations.note: Developing the gas-retaining wheat-protein network is one physical step within bread baking.

original_record.card: The Golden Gate Bridge’s 4,200-foot main span was the world’s longest when built. Critics had called the channel too deep and its winds and tides too strong. The project illustrates how assessing a proposed crossing involves site conditions as well as span length.

evidence.locator:
Golden Gate Bridge | ASCE
; inspected passage indices 4, 6, 7 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-5; paragraph-7; paragraph-8
evidence.note: A record-setting 4,200-foot main span crossed a channel considered difficult because of depth, wind, and tides.

original_record.label: Golden Gate Bridge
original_record.learning_takeaway: A record-setting 4,200-foot main span crossed a channel considered difficult because of depth, wind, and tides.

relations.note: ASCE identifies the project as a bridge and records the span and site constraints.

original_record.card: Good continuation is a visual grouping tendency: lines that form a smooth path are more likely to be perceived as belonging together than jagged, broken alternatives. It helps explain why an arrangement of separate marks can appear organized into continuous trajectories.

evidence.note: Section 5.6 calls continuity a tendency toward smooth flowing lines; the card keeps probabilistic wording and does not claim a compulsory rule of vision.

original_record.label: Good continuation
original_record.learning_takeaway: Understand why smooth continuations are often grouped rather than broken alternatives.

relations.note: The continuity and closure examples invite comparison between following a smooth path and completing an object from missing pieces, without identifying the two principles.

original_record.card: In Göreme and surrounding Cappadocia, eroded volcanic rock was adapted into dwellings, churches and refuges. Excavated spaces followed the possibilities of the terrain rather than simply standing on it. The landscape combines geological form with the practical and religious choices of its inhabitants.

evidence.note: Volcanic formations and rock-cut domestic/religious/refuge uses are documented.

original_record.label: Göreme and Cappadocia’s rock sites
original_record.learning_takeaway: Eroded volcanic terrain supports rock-cut dwellings, churches and refuges, joining geological form with settlement history.

relations.note: Compare two distinct settings where communities developed inhabited spaces within rock formations.

original_record.card: The Government in the Sunshine Act generally opens meetings of covered federal collegial agencies to public observation. Its definition does not cover every government gathering. Specified exceptions permit closure of portions, with formal voting and disclosure procedures, so openness is a structured legal requirement rather than an unlimited rule.

evidence.note: 5 USC 552b(a)–(d) defines covered collegial agencies, public observation, exceptions and recorded votes; covered and portions avoid universalizing coverage or suggesting every discussion must be public.

original_record.label: Government in the Sunshine Act
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explore public observation of covered federal agency meetings and formal closure procedures.

relations.note: Meeting observation under section 552b and access to records under FOIA address different forms of government transparency; neither mechanism is treated as an automatic substitute for the other.

original_record.card: Grace Hopper helped develop early compilers and compiler-based languages, then played an important role in defining COBOL. Her career shows a change in programming practice: building tools and shared language specifications that made computers easier to program, rather than treating every task only as machine-level calculation.

evidence.note: Checked early compiler work and the 1959 COBOL role; avoided claiming she alone invented the first compiler or authored SQL.

Supplementary inspected premise for the card or its comparison: Hopper's work on easier programming languages and SQL's declarative query design provide distinct examples of tools that let programmers express intent at a higher level.

original_record.label: Grace Hopper
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect early compiler work and COBOL standardization to efforts to make programming accessible beyond machine instructions.

relations.note: Hopper's work on easier programming languages and SQL's declarative query design provide distinct examples of tools that let programmers express intent at a higher level.

original_record.card: Johann Joseph Fux's Gradus ad Parnassum (1725) teaches contrapuntal composition through species counterpoint. The cited textbook explains this approach through one, two, three or four notes against another voice's note. The work offers a historical example of organizing musical instruction around constrained rhythmic relationships.

evidence.note: Puget Sound 30.1 gives Fux, 1725 and species pedagogy with rhythmic relationships. The revised wording does not imply that first species necessarily places a note against a longer note or claim a measured instructional outcome.

original_record.label: Gradus ad Parnassum
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explore Fux's historical organization of contrapuntal practice into rhythmic species.

relations.note: The textbook explicitly states that Fux's work teaches composition through species counterpoint.

original_record.card: Grameen Bank developed from a village-based research project in Bangladesh into a bank in 1983. Its account emphasizes lending without collateral and bringing services close to borrowers through village centers. The design changes how people reach credit; that alone does not establish every claimed effect on poverty.

evidence.locator: About Grameen Bank, pilot and collateral paragraphs
evidence.note: Checked pilot-to-bank history, collateral and village access; omitted promotional success rates and causal poverty-reduction claims.

original_record.label: Grameen Bank
original_record.learning_takeaway: Examine collateral-free village-based lending as an institutional design for reaching borrowers conventional banking may exclude.

relations.note: Grameen's official history explicitly describes its transformation into a bank and its collateral-free, locally delivered banking model.

original_record.card: Grand Pré combines reclaimed marshland and maintained dykes with archaeological traces and monuments associated with Acadian history. Its significance comes from ongoing agricultural practice as well as remembrance. A working landscape can therefore carry historical memory through both surviving structures and later acts of commemoration.

evidence.note: Agricultural continuity, archaeological traces and Acadian memorial importance are described.

original_record.label: Grand Pré landscape
original_record.learning_takeaway: Maintained dykes and marshland coexist with monuments and archaeological traces that make the place a focus of Acadian memory.

relations.note: The preserved land divisions offer one concrete element within the wider agricultural and commemorative landscape.

original_record.card: A grapheme cluster groups Unicode code points into an approximation of a user-perceived character. A letter and its combining accents may belong together, letting a cursor move over them as a unit. The default rules are useful but may require tailoring for particular scripts or editing tasks.

evidence.note: Checked approximation, combining-sequence example, and explicit tailoring caveat in UAX 29; not a universal one-cluster/one-glyph equation.

Supplementary inspected premise for the card or its comparison: The sources distinguish abstract code points from editing-oriented groups of them; this comparison explains why text length has several legitimate units.

original_record.label: Grapheme cluster
original_record.learning_takeaway: Group code points into a best-effort approximation of a user-perceived character for text editing.

relations.note: The sources distinguish abstract code points from editing-oriented groups of them; this comparison explains why text length has several legitimate units.

original_record.card: Gravimetric analysis determines composition by weighing a sample component or a chemically related product after separation. A known chemical formula links that measured mass to the amount of analyte. The measurement becomes informative because the separation and stoichiometric relationship are both understood.

evidence.locator: 4.5 Quantitative Chemical Analysis; inspected passage indices 25 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-idp27521328
evidence.note: Separate an analyte or known product and use its measured mass plus stoichiometry to infer concentration.

original_record.label: Gravimetric analysis
original_record.learning_takeaway: Separate an analyte or known product and use its measured mass plus stoichiometry to infer concentration.

relations.note: The quantitative-analysis section identifies gravimetric analysis as a method for determining analyte concentration.

original_record.card: For two separated masses in Newtonian gravity, choosing zero gravitational potential energy at infinite separation makes it negative at finite separation. Bringing the masses closer lowers it. A constant-gravity height formula is only a local approximation when the gravitational field changes little.

evidence.locator: 13.3 Gravitational Potential Energy and Total Energy; inspected passage indices 8, 9, 12 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-id1168329069323; fs-id1168326774371; fs-id1168329511648
evidence.note: Use separation-dependent potential energy rather than constant-g height formulas over large distances.

original_record.label: Gravitational potential energy
original_record.learning_takeaway: Use separation-dependent potential energy rather than constant-g height formulas over large distances.

relations.note: The section explicitly applies separation-dependent gravitational potential energy to escape conditions.

original_record.card: Great Zimbabwe’s dry-stone walls enclose the remains of a major Shona-built center. Archaeological finds, including imported objects, connect it with long-distance trade. The site brings monumental construction and commercial relationships together as evidence for the region’s own complex historical development.

evidence.note: Shona construction, dry-stone architecture and imported trade objects are documented.

original_record.label: Great Zimbabwe
original_record.learning_takeaway: Dry-stone enclosures and imported objects reveal a Shona-built urban center connected to long-distance trade.

relations.note: Architecture and associated imported finds show why relationships among remains matter.

original_record.card: Grounding in communication is collaborative work toward mutual belief that a message has been understood well enough for the current purpose. Responses and acknowledgments provide evidence for that belief. What counts as sufficient understanding can change with the task and communication medium.

evidence.locator: Opening; Grounding in Conversation; contribution model
evidence.note: The chapter defines the grounding criterion as participants mutually believing understanding is sufficient for current purposes. Responses supply evidence for this belief; neither perfect comprehension nor truth agreement is guaranteed. Grounding remains the process, distinct from common ground as the shared state.

original_record.label: Grounding in communication
original_record.learning_takeaway: Establish mutual evidence that a message is understood well enough for the participants' current purpose.

relations.note: Clark and Brennan explicitly describe grounding as the process by which contributions become part of common ground.

original_record.card: Growing block theory holds that the past and present exist, while the future does not yet exist. Reality expands as new events join its present edge. It differs from presentism, which excludes the past, and eternalism, which includes future objects in what exists.

evidence.locator: 6 Presentism, Eternalism, and the Growing Block Theory
evidence.note: SEP Time section 6 defines the increasing ontology and contrasts both alternatives; the card does not equate the growing block with four-dimensionalism or a settled physical theory.

original_record.label: Growing block theory
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explore a temporal ontology in which the past and present exist but the future does not.

relations.note: The section contrasts eternalism's past-and-future existence with the growing block's past-and-present existence, marking the future as their key difference.

original_record.card: Gulliver’s Travels sends its traveler through invented societies whose strangeness reflects recognizable problems closer to home. Swift’s distant settings become tools of satire. Reading the journeys as mirrors of social behavior reveals a purpose beyond treating the book as a collection of fantastic adventures.

evidence.note: The NEA allusion note explicitly explains distant worlds as social mirrors.

original_record.label: Gulliver’s Travels
original_record.learning_takeaway: Imaginary journeys let Swift reflect recognizable failings of his own society through apparently distant worlds.

relations.note: The guide identifies this satirical use of distant worlds as an earlier comparison for Bradbury’s novel.

original_record.card: Habeas corpus brings the legality of custody before a court. In US federal practice, a detainee's petition is a civil action challenging detention rather than an ordinary new criminal trial. It can protect against unlawful confinement, but jurisdictional and procedural requirements limit when relief is available.

evidence.note: Cornell's overview and federal-procedure discussion support custody review, civil action and procedural limits; the card does not promise a merits hearing or release whenever a petition is filed.

original_record.label: Habeas corpus
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish judicial review of detention's lawfulness from an ordinary new criminal trial.

relations.note: Gideon's unsuccessful state habeas petition supplies a concrete example of challenging detention through habeas before later Supreme Court review; it does not establish that every habeas claim succeeds.

original_record.card: The hairy ball theorem says that an ordinary two-dimensional sphere cannot carry a continuous tangent vector field that is nonzero everywhere. Trying to comb arrows smoothly along the whole sphere must leave a zero somewhere. The dimensional restriction matters; the statement is not true for every sphere.

evidence.locator: Hairy Ball Theorem -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2
evidence.note: Every continuous tangent vector field on a sphere has a zero somewhere.

original_record.label: Hairy ball theorem
original_record.learning_takeaway: Every continuous tangent vector field on a sphere has a zero somewhere.

relations.note: This is a topological obstruction to a globally nonvanishing field, illustrating a property that local drawings do not reveal.

original_record.card: The Haitian Revolution arose in a colony built on plantation slavery and led to independence. U.S. responses varied as leaders weighed slavery concerns, trade and relations with France. Official U.S. recognition came only in 1862, illustrating the distinction between achieving independence and receiving foreign recognition.

evidence.note: The account documents the slave revolt, independence, changing U.S. policies and delayed U.S. recognition in 1862.

original_record.label: Haitian Revolution
original_record.learning_takeaway: An uprising against plantation slavery led to independence, while U.S. policy and delayed recognition reflected shifting concerns about slavery, trade and diplomacy.

relations.note: The French Revolution changed factions and claims to civil rights in Saint-Domingue before and during the uprising.

original_record.card: Hemoglobin binds carbon dioxide more readily when less oxygen is attached to it. Oxygenation therefore changes its capacity to carry carbon dioxide, a relationship called the Haldane effect. This differs from the Bohr effect, where acidity changes how readily hemoglobin releases oxygen.

evidence.note: The Haldane paragraph compares CO2 binding by oxygenated and less-oxygenated hemoglobin; the Bohr paragraph provides the contrasting pH relationship.

original_record.label: Haldane effect
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish oxygenation-dependent carbon-dioxide carriage from pH-dependent oxygen affinity.

relations.note: These paired effects concern different directions of influence between hemoglobin’s gases and the chemical environment.

original_record.card: A Hanseatic kontor was an overseas trading establishment where merchants organized commercial activity and maintained privileges. At Bryggen, warehouses and living quarters preserve evidence of this arrangement. The built setting offers a case for studying how trading institutions organized commerce and merchant life.

evidence.note: Bryggen’s trading offices, privileges, warehouses and residences support the account.

original_record.label: Hanseatic kontor
original_record.learning_takeaway: Overseas trading offices combined commercial privileges, merchant residences and warehouses, as surviving Bryggen illustrates.

relations.note: The surviving merchant buildings make an institutional form legible through material evidence.

original_record.card: Havdalah marks the close of the Jewish Sabbath and the return to the ordinary week. A special candle and fragrant spices participate in blessings at this transition. A spice container is therefore a ritual object whose purpose becomes clearer when connected with a change in sacred time.

evidence.note: Candle, spice blessing and Sabbath-to-week transition are explicit.

original_record.label: Havdalah
original_record.learning_takeaway: A candle and fragrant spices help mark the transition from the Sabbath’s sacred time to the ordinary week.

relations.note: The museum places the spice vessel within the Jewish ritual marking the Sabbath’s end.
The museum identifies Havdalah as the Jewish ritual ending the Sabbath.

original_record.card: People who choose to participate in screening may differ from those who do not, including in health behaviors and other risks. Better outcomes in volunteers can therefore reflect those starting differences. Healthy-volunteer bias makes a simple screened-versus-unscreened comparison an unreliable measure of the screening’s effect.

evidence.note: NCI’s study-design discussion identifies self-selected participants’ different health behavior and lower unrelated mortality as a screening-evaluation concern.

original_record.label: Healthy-volunteer bias in screening studies
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explain why screened and unscreened groups can differ in outcomes for reasons unrelated to the screening.

relations.note: A randomized comparison can address initial selection differences that a simple volunteer/nonvolunteer contrast cannot, though later participation and follow-up still matter.

original_record.card: Heisenberg’s uncertainty principle limits how narrowly a quantum state can specify position and momentum together. Localizing a particle requires combining waves with different momenta. The resulting uncertainty is a feature of the state’s wave structure, rather than merely a consequence of using a poorly made measuring instrument.

evidence.locator: 7.2 The Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle; inspected passage indices 9, 10, 12 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-id1170901842781; fs-id1170902869050; fs-id1170901766281
evidence.note: Localizing a quantum state requires a spread of momenta, imposing a position-momentum uncertainty bound.

original_record.label: Heisenberg uncertainty principle
original_record.learning_takeaway: Localizing a quantum state requires a spread of momenta, imposing a position-momentum uncertainty bound.

relations.note: The source derives the position-momentum tradeoff using de Broglie relations and superposed matter waves.

original_record.card: Hemoglobin A1c testing measures glucose attached to hemoglobin, providing a picture of blood-glucose exposure over roughly two to three months. It differs from a glucose reading at one moment. Conditions affecting red blood cells can distort the result, so the measurement needs appropriate clinical context.

evidence.locator: What is the test?; Is there anything else?
evidence.note: MedlinePlus supports glycated hemoglobin, the approximate two-to-three-month window, the momentary-glucose contrast and red-cell-related limitations.

original_record.label: Hemoglobin A1c testing
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect glycated hemoglobin with longer-term glucose exposure and recognize red-cell-related limitations.

relations.note: Glucose-regulating hormones act over changing daily conditions, while A1c offers a longer-term measure of exposure to that regulated substance.

original_record.card: The Henderson–Hasselbalch equation estimates buffer pH from an acid’s pKa and the logarithm of the base-to-acid concentration ratio. Equal amounts give a pH near pKa. Using prepared concentrations requires the usual small-dissociation approximation, so the shortcut is not valid for every mixture.

evidence.locator: 14.6 Buffers; inspected passage indices 49, 50, 51 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-idp10558896; fs-idp7990848; fs-idp97287200
evidence.note: Estimate buffer pH from acid strength and the conjugate-base-to-acid ratio when the concentration approximation is valid.

original_record.label: Henderson–Hasselbalch equation
original_record.learning_takeaway: Estimate buffer pH from acid strength and the conjugate-base-to-acid ratio when the concentration approximation is valid.

relations.note: The buffer section explicitly uses this equation to calculate the pH of suitable buffer mixtures.

original_record.card: Henry Molaison, known in research as H. M., had severe difficulty forming new declarative memories after brain surgery. Yet he could improve at repeatedly practiced tasks without remembering previous practice. His case separates conscious memory for an episode from learning expressed through better performance.

evidence.note: PubMed abstract of Augustinack et al. directly identifies Henry Molaison as H. M.; OpenStax 8.2 supports surgery and declarative impairment, and 8.3 supports improved performance without recalled practice. Do not claim all old memories remained intact.
Identifies H. M. and the effect of his operation on declarative memory; does not supply his full name.
Directly identifies Henry Molaison as H. M. and describes the operation causing his amnesia.

original_record.label: Henry Molaison
original_record.learning_takeaway: Compare impaired new declarative memories with preserved improvement on practiced tasks.

relations.note: The textbook explicitly uses H. M. to contrast impaired new episodic/semantic memory with preserved procedural learning.

original_record.card: A heterodiegetic narrator tells a story without participating in its events. This does not by itself specify how much the narrator knows or where the telling sits within a larger narrative. Participation, information and narrative level need to be examined as separate features.

evidence.note: Non-diegetic status is distinguished from level; l08 supports separate informational limits.
Focalization identifies a separate question about narrative information.

original_record.label: Heterodiegetic narrator
original_record.learning_takeaway: A narrator can tell a story in which they are not a participant; this status is separate from narrative level.

relations.note: The contrast turns on participation in the story, not a simple first-person/third-person rule.

original_record.card: A heterogeneous equilibrium includes substances in different phases, such as a solid in contact with a gas. Pure solids and pure liquids are omitted from the usual equilibrium expression because their activities are fixed at unity under the standard approximation.

evidence.locator: 13.2 Equilibrium Constants; inspected passage indices 66, 93, 94 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-idp11719264; fs-idp27217312; fs-idp8357744
evidence.note: Equilibria span multiple phases, while pure solids and liquids do not appear in simplified concentration expressions.

original_record.label: Heterogeneous equilibrium
original_record.learning_takeaway: Equilibria span multiple phases, while pure solids and liquids do not appear in simplified concentration expressions.

relations.note: The equilibrium section explicitly defines heterogeneous equilibria as equilibria involving two or more phases.

original_record.card: Ideal hexagonal close packing builds a solid from alternating AB layers. The third layer sits above the first, unlike the ABC sequence of cubic close packing. Both arrangements give each atom twelve nearest neighbors, so equal coordination does not imply identical layer geometry.

evidence.locator: 10.6 Lattice Structures in Crystalline Solids; inspected passage indices 33 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-idp178963488
evidence.note: ABAB layer stacking distinguishes hexagonal close packing from the ABC sequence of cubic close packing.

original_record.label: Hexagonal close packing
original_record.learning_takeaway: ABAB layer stacking distinguishes hexagonal close packing from the ABC sequence of cubic close packing.

relations.note: The inspected paragraph compares the two close-packed layer sequences and their coordination numbers.

original_record.card: Hierarchical scale makes a figure larger or smaller according to importance rather than natural proportion. On a Benin palace plaque, an enlarged ruler stands out from attendants. Relative size becomes a way of displaying rank, so reading the image requires more than judging realistic dimensions.

evidence.note: The enlarged oba and smaller attendants explicitly express rank.

original_record.label: Hierarchical scale
original_record.learning_takeaway: Relative figure size can encode social importance rather than natural proportion, as an enlarged ruler does on a Benin palace plaque.

relations.note: The Met description identifies hierarchical scale in this particular composition.
