original_record.card: DNA wraps around histone proteins inside the nucleus. Chemical tags placed on these proteins can be recognized by other cellular machinery, helping determine whether a region of DNA is used. This regulates access through DNA packaging rather than changing the genetic letters.

evidence.note: The histone paragraphs describe DNA wrapped around histones and reader proteins responding to attached chemical tags; epigenomic regulation does not rewrite sequence.

original_record.label: Histone modification
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish marks on DNA-packaging proteins from chemical marks directly on DNA.

relations.note: Comparing tags on histones with tags directly on DNA distinguishes two documented routes of epigenomic regulation.

original_record.card: Historical sourcing asks who made a document, for what purpose and in what setting. Those questions affect how its claims become evidence. Two apparently conflicting accounts may make sense together once their authors’ positions and the circumstances of production are considered.

evidence.locator: Opposition to the Philippine-American War example, lines 20–22
evidence.note: Philippine-American War teaching example demonstrates author and context analysis.

original_record.label: Historical sourcing
original_record.learning_takeaway: A document’s author, purpose and production setting affect what it can count as evidence, even when its account differs from other documents.

relations.note: Sourcing is a method for interpreting historical documents as evidence.

original_record.card: In hollandaise, whisking disperses melted butter into tiny droplets within a water-based mixture. Egg-yolk emulsifiers help keep those droplets from merging again. The sauce’s stability therefore depends on both forming small droplets and maintaining their separation, rather than merely stirring fat and water together once.

evidence.note: Exploratorium describes whisking butter into droplets and yolk proteins/lecithin stabilizing the oil–water interface against coalescence.

original_record.label: Hollandaise emulsification
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explain how egg yolk helps tiny fat droplets remain dispersed in the water phase of a sauce.

relations.note: Hollandaise is a documented culinary oil-in-water emulsion; yolk supplies the stabilizers that keep its dispersed fat droplets separate.

original_record.card: A homeomorphism is a one-to-one correspondence between topological spaces that is continuous in both directions. It preserves topological structure while allowing distances to change. Requiring a continuous inverse matters; simply matching every point with another point is not enough to establish this equivalence.

evidence.locator: Homeomorphism -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1, 2 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2; paragraph-3
evidence.note: A bijection continuous in both directions expresses topological sameness without preserving distances.

evidence.locator: Graph Subdivision -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1, 2, 3 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2; paragraph-3; paragraph-4
evidence.note: Supplementary inspected passage establishes the alternate example, field identity, or alias used in the takeaway.

original_record.label: Homeomorphism
original_record.learning_takeaway: A bijection continuous in both directions expresses topological sameness without preserving distances.

relations.note: The topology source identifies topological equivalence in terms of homeomorphism.

original_record.card: A homodiegetic narrator is also a participant in the story being told. That relationship differs from the narrative level occupied by the telling. Asking whether a narrator appears in the events therefore answers a different question from asking how one story contains another.

evidence.note: Narrator status combines participation and level as separate variables.

original_record.label: Homodiegetic narrator
original_record.learning_takeaway: A narrator who participates in the story must be distinguished from the level at which that narrator performs the telling.

relations.note: The terms contrast participation and nonparticipation in the narrated events.

original_record.card: In homogeneous catalysis, catalyst and reactants occupy the same phase. The catalyst can react temporarily to form an intermediate, then reappear in a later step. Its regeneration explains how a substance can influence many reaction events without being consumed in the overall equation.

evidence.locator: 12.7 Catalysis; inspected passage indices 15, 20 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-idm243256336; fs-idm251830192
evidence.note: A catalyst in the same phase forms reaction intermediates and is regenerated by later steps.

original_record.label: Homogeneous catalysis
original_record.learning_takeaway: A catalyst in the same phase forms reaction intermediates and is regenerated by later steps.

relations.note: The source defines homogeneous catalysts as same-phase catalysts and describes their catalytic cycle.

original_record.card: In biology, homologous features resemble one another because they descend from a shared ancestral feature. Bird and bat forelimbs are homologous, even though their wings evolved separately as flight structures. The comparison shows why common ancestry and similarity of present-day function must be distinguished.

evidence.note: Berkeley explicitly treats bird/bat forelimbs as homologous and their wings as independently evolved analogous flight structures.

original_record.label: Homology (biology)
original_record.learning_takeaway: Identify similarity inherited from common ancestry, even when present-day functions differ.

relations.note: The same bird–bat comparison separates common-ancestry resemblance from independently evolved similarity in flight.

original_record.card: Building Hoover Dam required managing the heat released as enormous concrete blocks cured. Refrigerated water circulated through embedded pipes to remove that heat; the pipes were later filled with grout. The project shows why a massive structure’s construction must account for thermal behavior as well as final strength.

evidence.locator:
Hoover Dam | ASCE
; inspected passage indices 5, 8, 11 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-6; paragraph-9; paragraph-12
evidence.note: Embedded cooling pipes removed curing heat from enormous concrete blocks during dam construction.

original_record.label: Hoover Dam
original_record.learning_takeaway: Embedded cooling pipes removed curing heat from enormous concrete blocks during dam construction.

relations.note: The source explicitly describes the cooling system used in the dam’s curing concrete.

original_record.card: Genetic information can move between cells outside ordinary parent-to-offspring inheritance. In prokaryotes, transformation takes up environmental DNA, transduction uses viruses, and conjugation transfers DNA through cell contact. Horizontal gene transfer therefore offers several routes for acquiring genetic material without reproducing a whole new organism.

evidence.note: OpenStax defines horizontal transfer and separately describes transformation, transduction and conjugation.

original_record.label: Horizontal gene transfer
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish DNA exchange outside parent-to-offspring inheritance from ordinary reproduction.

relations.note: Horizontal transfer broadens the genetics discussion from vertical inheritance to acquisition of DNA from other cells.

original_record.card: Grafting joins a selected shoot, or scion, to a rootstock so the parts contribute different traits. In apple trees, the scion determines the fruit variety, while the rootstock strongly influences tree size and time to bearing. The resulting tree combines roles from two genetically different individuals.

evidence.note: UMN’s rootstock section explicitly describes genetically distinct scion/rootstock parts and their fruit, size and bearing-time roles.

original_record.label: Horticultural grafting
original_record.learning_takeaway: Join a selected shoot variety to a different root system so each contributes different traits.

relations.note: Dwarfing is one consequence of rootstock choice within the broader scion–rootstock propagation method.

original_record.card: An HTTP entity tag is an opaque label identifying a particular representation for validation. A server may derive it from a version number, hash, or another method, while clients simply compare tags. Strong and weak tags support different comparisons; an ETag need not reveal its construction.

evidence.note: Checked opacity, implementation freedom, and weak/strong distinction; tags are not necessarily content hashes or globally unique IDs.

original_record.label: HTTP entity tag
original_record.learning_takeaway: Use an opaque representation validator to detect changes without requiring clients to understand its construction.

relations.note: RFC 9110 section 13.1.1 explicitly uses entity tags in If-Match conditions and requires strong comparison.

original_record.card: An HTTP method is idempotent when repeating an identical request has the same intended server effect as performing it once. Responses may differ, and servers may still log each attempt. The property helps clients decide when retrying after an interrupted connection will avoid multiplying the requested change.

evidence.note: Checked intended-effect scope, distinct responses and incidental logging; no blanket authorization to retry every HTTP method.

original_record.label: HTTP method idempotency
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish repeated intended effects from identical responses or the absence of incidental logging.

relations.note: Idempotency addresses repeated intended effects, whereas If-Match addresses intervening representation changes; the RFC defines these distinct safeguards for uncertain updates.

original_record.card: An HTTP If-Match condition can require a representation to retain a matching entity tag before an update proceeds. If someone else has changed it, the precondition can stop an accidental overwrite. The check tests the version instead of assuming the client's earlier copy is current.

evidence.note: Checked strong entity-tag comparison and lost-update purpose. The card says can require a matching tag because the separate wildcard form checks existence, rather than an exact version.

original_record.label: HTTP If-Match update preconditions
original_record.learning_takeaway: Apply a state-changing request only when its representation tag still matches, preventing intervening updates from being overwritten.

relations.note: The If-Match definition explicitly applies strong entity-tag comparison to prevent accidental overwrites of intervening changes.

original_record.card: Hubble’s position above Earth’s atmosphere avoids the constantly changing refraction that blurs ground-based images. This helped deliver sharp visible-light views of distant objects. Space does not remove diffraction, however: the telescope’s finite aperture still limits the angular detail its optical system can resolve.

evidence.locator: 6.2 Telescopes Today; inspected passage indices 37, 38, 40 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-id1167471084189; fs-id1167470709434; fs-id1167470632380
evidence.note: Atmospheric turbulence blurs images; Hubble was launched above it for sharper imaging.

evidence.locator: 4.5 Circular Apertures and Resolution; inspected passage indices 8, 9, 11 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-id1172101688448; fs-id1172101945964; fs-id1172099490776
evidence.note: Finite apertures impose diffraction-based angular resolution limits even without atmospheric blur.

original_record.label: Hubble Space Telescope
original_record.learning_takeaway: Observing above Earth’s turbulent atmosphere gives Hubble sharper visible-light images.

relations.note: The telescope chapter explicitly identifies escape from atmospheric blurring as a reason for launching Hubble.

original_record.card: Huffman coding assigns variable-length bit strings to symbols using their frequencies. Frequent symbols can receive shorter codes. The result is an optimal prefix code for the given frequencies, so a decoder can identify consecutive symbols unambiguously without inserting a separator after every codeword.

evidence.note: Checked variable lengths, known frequencies, prefix decoding, and optimality limited to prefix codes for the specified frequencies.

original_record.label: Huffman coding
original_record.learning_takeaway: Assign variable-length prefix codes using symbol frequencies to minimize expected code length.

relations.note: RFC 1951 section 3.2.1 explicitly defines a Huffman code as an optimal prefix code for given symbol frequencies.

original_record.card: Hydroponics grows plants without relying on soil as the nutrient medium. A water-based solution supplies mineral nutrients, while the system must also accommodate the roots’ need for oxygen. Different arrangements support or bathe the roots differently, so soilless growing is more than placing a plant in plain water.

evidence.note: UMN defines soilless growing with nutrient solution and discusses root aeration and several system arrangements.

original_record.label: Hydroponics
original_record.learning_takeaway: Grow plants using a nutrient solution without making soil the source of their nutrients.

relations.note: Nutrient-film technique is one particular arrangement for supplying roots within hydroponics.

original_record.card: Low thyroid-hormone levels stimulate a signaling chain from hypothalamic TRH to pituitary TSH and then the thyroid gland. As thyroid hormones rise, they reduce further stimulation through negative feedback. The system regulates output through returning information, rather than a one-way sequence of commands.

evidence.note: The thyroid regulation section describes low T3/T4, TRH, anterior-pituitary TSH, thyroid secretion and inhibition of further TSH production.

original_record.label: Hypothalamic–pituitary–thyroid feedback
original_record.learning_takeaway: Trace TRH and TSH stimulation together with thyroid-hormone feedback.

relations.note: The returning thyroid-hormone signal provides a specific endocrine example of negative-feedback homeostasis.

original_record.card: Joe Brainard’s I Remember builds a book through recurring opening words that introduce ordinary recollections. Repetition turns separate memories into an accumulating structure. The work also became a model for a writing exercise, showing how a recognizable formal device can organize both reading and composition.

evidence.note: The glossary identifies the book’s anaphoric structure and use as an exercise model.

original_record.label: I Remember (Joe Brainard)
original_record.learning_takeaway: Repeated opening words accumulate ordinary memories into a book-length structure that also inspired a widely used writing exercise.

relations.note: The glossary presents Brainard’s recurring openings as a sustained example of anaphora.

original_record.card: The ideal rocket equation links velocity change to constant effective exhaust speed and the logarithm of initial-to-final mass ratio, neglecting gravity and drag losses. At fixed dry mass, adding propellant gives diminishing velocity gains because the extra propellant must initially be accelerated too.

evidence.locator: Ideal Rocket Equation | Glenn Research Center | NASA; inspected passage indices 2, 13, 21, 28, 31, 35, 36, 39, 40, 41, 43 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-3; paragraph-14; paragraph-22; paragraph-29; paragraph-32; paragraph-36; paragraph-37; paragraph-40; paragraph-41; paragraph-42; paragraph-44
evidence.note: Derives the variable-mass velocity change, states neglected forces, and connects effective exhaust speed with specific impulse.

original_record.label: Ideal rocket equation
original_record.learning_takeaway: Ideal velocity change grows with effective exhaust speed and the logarithm of initial-to-final mass ratio.

relations.note: The source explicitly rewrites the ideal rocket equation using specific impulse.

original_record.card: In the Kantian distinction discussed here, an imperfect duty remains obligatory while leaving latitude in how it is fulfilled. Flexibility about particular actions does not make the underlying duty optional. This separates discretion within an obligation from supererogation, which concerns morally good action beyond obligation.

evidence.note: SEP section 2 explicitly says imperfect duties are no less compelling and differ in application; the opening bounds this formulation to the Kantian discussion rather than every use of the term.

original_record.label: Imperfect duty
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish discretion over fulfilling a duty from permission to ignore it.

relations.note: The article contrasts imperfect duty's binding force and discretionary application with supererogatory optionality; it also acknowledges philosophers who dispute that separation.

original_record.card: The implied author is an image of a work’s maker inferred from its stylistic, aesthetic and evaluative choices. It is not simply the real writer or the narrator. The concept remains debated because textual clues and a reader’s interpretation both contribute to the reconstructed image.

evidence.note: Textual author-image, reader dependence and debate are explicit.

original_record.label: Implied author
original_record.learning_takeaway: Readers infer an author-image from a work’s stylistic and evaluative choices; this debated construct is not the real writer or narrator.

relations.note: The handbook treats the recipient-image as a counterpart whose construction is not perfectly symmetrical.

original_record.card: An implied reader is a recipient-image reconstructed from clues within a text. It concerns the knowledge, assumptions or responses the work appears to accommodate. This differs from an actual reader and from an intended audience known only through the author’s private plans or external statements.

evidence.note: Textual recipient-image is distinguished from an extratextual intended reader.

original_record.label: Implied reader
original_record.learning_takeaway: A text can presuppose a recipient’s knowledge and values without depicting an actual reader inside its story.

relations.note: The source explicitly explains the relation between inferred author and recipient images.

original_record.card: Impression management concerns how people present themselves through behavior, surroundings, and visible cues. Goffman's theatrical analogy highlights how different settings invite different performances; a judge's robe and courtroom props help shape expectations. The process need not imply deliberate deception or a completely invented identity.

evidence.locator: §4.3, Goffman's role performance and courtroom props
evidence.note: Checked dramaturgical presentation and courtroom example; not equated with research-demand bias or assumed to be conscious manipulation in every case.

evidence.locator: §1.1, What Are Society and Culture?; Studying Patterns
evidence.note: Supplementary inspected premise for the card or its comparison: Goffman's interactional account offers a specific sociological lens on how settings and shared expectations shape everyday encounters.

original_record.label: Impression management
original_record.learning_takeaway: Shape how others interpret a social performance through behavior, setting, and visible cues.

relations.note: Goffman's interactional account offers a specific sociological lens on how settings and shared expectations shape everyday encounters.

original_record.card: Inattentional blindness is missing a visible event while attention is occupied elsewhere. In the basketball-pass counting demonstration described by OpenStax, many viewers failed to notice an unexpected gorilla-costumed figure. The result concerns divided task demands, not an inability of the eyes to receive the image.

evidence.note: OpenStax 5.1 gives the counting task and unexpected figure; many avoids transferring one condition's numerical rate to every observer or task.

original_record.label: Inattentional blindness
original_record.learning_takeaway: Understand how a visible unexpected event can escape notice during another task.

relations.note: OpenStax explicitly presents the unexpected-figure demonstration as evidence that attention affects perception of the environment; inattentional blindness is the named perceptual failure in that discussion.

original_record.card: The indiscernibility of identicals says that if two names pick out the very same thing, every property of that thing must belong to both referents. It runs from identity to shared properties. The converse claim, that sharing all properties guarantees identity, is a different principle.

evidence.note: SEP section 1 explicitly distinguishes identity implying indiscernibility from the converse; the two-name formulation explains reference without suggesting that differing descriptions themselves prove distinct objects.

original_record.label: Indiscernibility of identicals
original_record.learning_takeaway: Understand why genuinely identical things cannot differ in a property.

relations.note: The entry states Leibniz's Law after distinguishing numerical from qualitative identity, and separately names its more controversial converse.

original_record.card: Some heavy main-group elements form ions that retain their outer s-electron pair instead of losing every valence electron. This inert pair effect helps explain lower oxidation states, such as thallium’s plus-one state, alongside the higher states suggested by its periodic-table group.

evidence.locator: 7.1 Ionic Bonding; inspected passage indices 16 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-idm147404048
evidence.note: Heavy main-group elements can retain a low-energy valence s-electron pair and form lower oxidation states.

original_record.label: Inert pair effect
original_record.learning_takeaway: Heavy main-group elements can retain a low-energy valence s-electron pair and form lower oxidation states.

relations.note: The effect connects periodic-table position with departures from the simplest expected ion charges.

original_record.card: An inertial reference frame lets Newton’s laws describe motion using forces from physical interactions without adding inertial-force terms. Accelerated or rotating frames can still be useful, but require those extra terms. A turning car illustrates how a passenger’s frame differs from an approximately inertial ground frame.

evidence.locator: 6.3 Centripetal Force; inspected passage indices 43, 44, 50 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-id1165039397195; fs-id1165039268847; fs-id1165039316978
evidence.note: Distinguish physical interactions from extra inertial-force terms introduced by accelerated coordinates.

original_record.label: Inertial reference frame
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish physical interactions from extra inertial-force terms introduced by accelerated coordinates.

relations.note: The cited discussion uses rotating frames and Coriolis force to explain the difference between inertial and noninertial accounts.

original_record.card: Information asymmetry occurs when one party to a transaction knows more relevant information than another. A used-car seller may know defects the buyer cannot readily observe. This differs from shared uncertainty: both parties can lack information, but asymmetry describes an unequal distribution of what they know.

evidence.note: Checked unequal versus incomplete information and used-car example; unequal knowledge need not imply deliberate dishonesty in every transaction.

Supplementary inspected premise for the card or its comparison: The insurance chapter explicitly links privately known risk to adverse selection, providing a concrete consequence of information asymmetry.

original_record.label: Information asymmetry
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish unequal knowledge between parties from uncertainty that both sides share.

relations.note: The insurance chapter explicitly links privately known risk to adverse selection, providing a concrete consequence of information asymmetry.

original_record.card: Informational social influence occurs when people treat others' responses as evidence about an uncertain situation. If smoke in a theater might be a special effect, nearby people's reactions can guide interpretation. Conformity here reflects reliance on presumed knowledge, rather than only a wish to belong.

evidence.locator: Why conform? normative versus informational influence
evidence.note: Section 12.4's ambiguous smoke example and competent-group definition support uncertainty-driven reliance; the hypothetical example is not presented as a measured emergency experiment.

original_record.label: Informational social influence
original_record.learning_takeaway: Understand relying on others as information when a situation is ambiguous.

relations.note: The textbook directly distinguishes believing the group is informed from seeking its acceptance, while allowing both as motivations for conformity.

original_record.card: Real instrument strings are not perfectly flexible. Their bending stiffness shifts higher vibration modes farther from exact whole-number multiples of the fundamental. This inharmonicity is especially relevant to plucked or struck strings; periodic bowing can instead draw the vibration into a harmonic pattern.

evidence.note: UNSW harmonics discussion supports stiffness and stronger high-mode shifts, with the bowed versus plucked/struck qualification; not every real string is claimed equally inharmonic.

original_record.label: Inharmonicity of musical strings
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explain why stiff strings have stretched modal frequencies rather than exact harmonic multiples.

relations.note: The article explicitly contrasts inharmonic string resonances with harmonic motion enforced by bow-driven mode locking.

original_record.card: Institutionalization establishes a convention or norm as a durable part of social life. A school functions as more than a building because people recognize roles and shared expectations around it. Those arrangements can predate current participants, showing how socially created institutions can still have real consequences.

evidence.note: Checked school example and persistence through shared recognition; not equated with any building, any formal organization, or putting a person into residential care.
Supplementary inspected premise for the card or its comparison: The source directly describes institutionalization as establishing conventions or norms and illustrates it with a school.

original_record.label: Institutionalization
original_record.learning_takeaway: Understand how shared conventions become established social institutions that outlast the original participants.

relations.note: The source directly describes institutionalization as establishing conventions or norms and illustrates it with a school.

original_record.card: Insulin and glucagon help keep blood glucose within a usable range. Insulin favors glucose uptake and storage after levels rise; glucagon helps mobilize glucose, including from liver glycogen, when levels fall. Their opposing actions connect changing food availability with the body’s ongoing fuel needs.

evidence.note: The pancreas chapter describes insulin-associated uptake/storage and glucagon-associated liver glycogen breakdown during low glucose.

original_record.label: Insulin–glucagon regulation of blood glucose
original_record.learning_takeaway: Contrast glucose storage and uptake after a meal with glucose mobilization during fasting.

relations.note: Opposing responses to rising and falling glucose provide a concrete regulated-variable example within homeostasis.

original_record.card: An insurance deductible is an amount the policyholder pays before specified coverage starts paying. It leaves some loss with the insured party instead of transferring every cost to the insurer. In the textbook's incentive account, retaining that stake can discourage risk-taking that full coverage might otherwise encourage.

evidence.note: Checked threshold structure and qualified incentive rationale; not advice about an appropriate deductible for any person or policy.

original_record.label: Insurance deductible
original_record.learning_takeaway: Require an initial out-of-pocket loss amount before the insurance coverage begins paying.

relations.note: The moral-hazard section explicitly identifies deductibles as a cost-sharing method intended to preserve incentives to avoid losses.

original_record.card: The integer partition function counts ways to write a positive integer as a sum of positive integers when order is ignored. Four has five partitions. Consequently, three plus one and one plus three count as the same possibility, unlike an ordered composition.

evidence.locator: Partition Function P -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1, 2, 3, 10 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2; paragraph-3; paragraph-4; paragraph-11
evidence.note: Count decompositions of an integer into positive summands while ignoring their order.

original_record.label: Integer partition function
original_record.learning_takeaway: Count decompositions of an integer into positive summands while ignoring their order.

relations.note: Partition counts and Catalan numbers are different sequences arising from different combinatorial structures; this is a comparison, not equivalence.

original_record.card: Integral windup occurs when a controller accumulates error while an actuator cannot deliver the requested output because it is saturated. After the command changes, that accumulated demand may take time to unwind. The result can be a delayed recovery even though the actuator’s limits are already known.

evidence.locator: Anti-Windup Control Using PID Controller Block; inspected passage indices 1, 10, 12, 14 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2; paragraph-11; paragraph-13; paragraph-15
evidence.note: An integrator can accumulate unusable control demand during actuator saturation, delaying recovery afterward.

original_record.label: Integral windup
original_record.learning_takeaway: An integrator can accumulate unusable control demand during actuator saturation, delaying recovery afterward.

relations.note: The source explicitly presents back-calculation as an anti-windup strategy for saturated PID controllers.

original_record.card: Intention-to-treat analysis keeps participants in their originally assigned trial groups, even when they do not follow treatment as planned. This preserves the comparison created by randomization for estimating assignment effects. Missing outcome data still require attention; the label alone does not solve that separate problem.

evidence.note: Cochrane §8.2.2 states original-group analysis regardless of received intervention and separately treats bias from missing outcomes.

original_record.label: Intention-to-treat analysis
original_record.learning_takeaway: Preserve original randomized groups when estimating the effect of treatment assignment.

relations.note: This analysis principle preserves the original randomized grouping when assessing assignment to an intervention.

original_record.card: Inter-rater reliability concerns agreement between observers evaluating the same event. If two researchers classify a behavior differently, the coding procedure may be inconsistent. Agreement helps establish reproducibility across observers, but by itself does not show that their shared measure captures the intended psychological construct.

evidence.note: Section 2.3 defines observer agreement and distinguishes reliability from validity; the coding example applies that definition without claiming agreement proves accuracy.

original_record.label: Inter-rater reliability
original_record.learning_takeaway: Check whether different observers classify the same behavior consistently.

relations.note: The source lists inter-rater and test–retest reliability as distinct consistency checks: across observers versus across administrations.

original_record.card: A bond's resale value can change when market interest rates move. If newer bonds offer higher interest, an older fixed-rate bond may need to sell at a discount to attract buyers. This price risk is distinct from an issuer failing to make its promised payments.

evidence.locator: What are the benefits and risks of bonds?, Interest rate risk
evidence.note: Checked old-versus-new coupon comparison and resale qualification; not claimed that every bond has identical sensitivity or that maturity eliminates default risk.

original_record.label: Interest-rate risk in bonds
original_record.learning_takeaway: Understand why an older fixed-rate bond may need a price discount when newly issued bonds offer higher rates.

relations.note: Investor.gov explicitly distinguishes interest-rate risk from credit risk in its bond-risk explanation.

original_record.card: Interleaved practice mixes different kinds of problems rather than grouping one type into a long block. In the cited mathematics intervention, students had to choose a suitable strategy for each problem. The challenge is partly recognizing which method applies, not simply carrying out a method already signaled by repetition.

evidence.locator: Structured Abstract, Intervention and Control Condition
evidence.note: Checked the mathematics intervention's ordering manipulation and strategy-selection rationale; not claimed effective for every subject or identical to spacing.

Supplementary inspected premise for the card or its comparison: Mixing problem types concerns strategy selection, whereas spacing concerns timing of repeated encounters; the sources provide distinct instructional dimensions to compare.

original_record.label: Interleaved practice
original_record.learning_takeaway: Mix different mathematical problem types so learners must select a strategy instead of repeating one blocked routine.

relations.note: Mixing problem types concerns strategy selection, whereas spacing concerns timing of repeated encounters; the sources provide distinct instructional dimensions to compare.

original_record.card: The International Cooperative Alliance was founded in 1895 to connect cooperatives across countries. Its initial aims included sharing information, defending common principles, and developing international trade. It illustrates how independent member enterprises can coordinate through a federation without becoming a single ordinary business under one owner.

evidence.note: Checked founding aims and cooperative membership; no claim about current membership counts or authority over every cooperative.

evidence.locator: Principle 4, Autonomy and Independence; Principle 6, Cooperation among Cooperatives
evidence.note: Principle 4 states member control and cooperative autonomy when entering agreements; Principle 6 describes cooperation through local, national, regional and international structures. Together they support the independence/coordination premise. The 1895 founding aims are separately supported by the history source.

original_record.label: International Cooperative Alliance
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explore how an international federation coordinated information, common principles, and trade among otherwise separate cooperatives.

relations.note: The Alliance's history expressly describes delegates from cooperatives establishing an international body to support their shared principles and trade.

original_record.card: The International HapMap Project charted common patterns of human DNA variation, especially groups of variants often inherited together. These genomic neighborhoods helped researchers connect variation with disease. Its contribution was a map of shared variation patterns, rather than merely another sequence from a single individual.

evidence.note: NHGRI identifies the project, co-inherited haplotypes, common human variation and the use of linkage-disequilibrium patterns in disease studies.

original_record.label: International HapMap Project
original_record.learning_takeaway: See how patterns of co-inherited DNA variants helped connect genomic variation with disease.

relations.note: HapMap’s co-inherited variant neighborhoods give a named research example of genomic linkage patterns; the project is not the general linkage mechanism.

original_record.card: Intrinsic motivation comes from satisfaction in the activity itself, such as baking because it is enjoyable. External rewards can also motivate the same person. Distinguishing these sources helps explain why turning a favorite activity into paid work can sometimes change its appeal.

evidence.note: Section 10.1's intrinsic/extrinsic distinction and Odessa baking example support mixed motives and a possible change after payment; sometimes preserves the section's later qualifications.

original_record.label: Intrinsic motivation
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish doing an activity for satisfaction from doing it for an external reward.

relations.note: The section moves from intrinsic motivation to evidence that external rewards can change it, while distinguishing tangible rewards, praise and expectations.

original_record.card: Ionic bonding holds positively and negatively charged ions together through electrostatic attraction. The ions are constrained in a solid lattice, so they cannot readily carry electric current. Melting the material or dissolving it can free the ions to move and conduct.

evidence.locator: 7.1 Ionic Bonding; inspected passage indices 5, 6 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-idm163451984; fs-idm91147568
evidence.note: Electrostatic attraction holds oppositely charged ions together, with conductivity changing when ions become mobile.

original_record.label: Ionic bonding
original_record.learning_takeaway: Electrostatic attraction holds oppositely charged ions together, with conductivity changing when ions become mobile.

relations.note: The bonding chapter identifies ionic bonds as electrostatic attractions between cations and anions.

original_record.card: An IPM action threshold marks conditions under which pest management becomes warranted. It may reflect a pest population level or environmental circumstances indicating unacceptable harm. The threshold separates seeing a pest from deciding to intervene, making control a decision based on context rather than mere presence.

evidence.note: EPA defines action thresholds by pest populations or environmental conditions indicating that control action is needed.

original_record.label: IPM action thresholds
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish the presence of a pest from a level that warrants an intervention.

relations.note: Threshold-setting is a named decision step within EPA’s integrated pest-management framework.

original_record.card: IR8 emerged from crossing the tall rice variety Peta with the dwarf Dee-geo-woo-gen, followed by selection of useful offspring. Released by IRRI in 1966, it became an influential semidwarf variety. Its history makes crop improvement visible as a sequence of crosses, observations and selection.

evidence.note: IRRI’s breeding history identifies Peta and Dee-geo-woo-gen, the crossing/selection sequence, 1966 release and semidwarf significance.

original_record.label: IR8
original_record.learning_takeaway: Trace a historically influential semi-dwarf rice variety to a specific cross and selection program.

relations.note: IR8’s crossing-and-selection history can be compared with later marker-assisted selection, without falsely claiming IR8 was originally created using that later method.

original_record.card: On Isle Royale in Lake Superior, a long-running study follows wolves, moose and their environment. Predator numbers matter, but disease, climate and available food also influence population changes. The island illustrates why a predator–prey relationship cannot be understood from two population counts alone.

evidence.locator: Why is Isle Royale a Unique Research Location?; Predator-Prey Relationships
evidence.note: NPS locates the island in Lake Superior and documents the long-running study, disease effects and changing roles of climate and forage.

original_record.label: Isle Royale
original_record.learning_takeaway: Use an isolated island study to distinguish predator effects from climate, disease and food availability.

relations.note: The island study demonstrates ecology’s need to consider interacting predators, prey and environmental conditions.

original_record.card: In US litigation, issue preclusion can bar relitigation of an issue actually litigated and necessarily decided in a valid final judgment. It generally binds a party who had a full and fair opportunity to litigate, with recognized nonparty exceptions. The issue may recur within a different claim.

evidence.note: The original collateral-estoppel entry supports the factual/legal issue and final-necessary-determination core. Its concise definition does not alone supply the full applicability boundary; the explicit Cornell issue-preclusion entry and Taylor opinion supply those conditions.
The claim-level definition supports the stated contrast with a previously decided issue.

evidence.locator: Opening; elements 1–4; contrast with claim preclusion; nonparty paragraph (lines 5–16)
evidence.note: Requires the identical issue to have been actually litigated and determined, essential to a valid final judgment. A different later cause of action can still involve that issue. The nonparty discussion is read alongside the primary opinion, not as an absolute same-parties rule.

The Court describes actual litigation and necessary resolution, full and fair opportunity, the general rule against binding nonparties, and limited recognized exceptions. Supports can bar and generally binds without requiring identical parties in every later suit.

original_record.label: Issue preclusion
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish relitigating a decided issue from repeating an entire claim.

relations.note: The linked accounts distinguish preventing a repeated claim from preventing a repeated decision on an essential issue, while acknowledging varied uses of the term res judicata.

original_record.card: Iterative narration tells once what happened repeatedly. Instead of recounting every separate occasion, a narrative can gather a habit or recurring activity into one statement. The repeated events belong to the story world, while their presentation occurs only once in the telling.

evidence.note: The source defines several occurrences represented in one telling.

original_record.label: Iterative narration
original_record.learning_takeaway: One narrative statement can gather events that happened repeatedly, compressing habitual experience into a single telling.

relations.note: The modes reverse the relation between repeated happenings and repeated tellings.

original_record.card: The optional Jacoby rule makes a gammon or backgammon count as a single game unless a double has been offered. It encourages use of the cube rather than waiting for a multiple-value win. The cited standard match-play rules do not use it.

evidence.locator: Optional Rules: Jacoby Rule; FAQ on match play
evidence.note: USBGF Optional Rules gives the condition and incentive; its match-play FAQ explicitly excludes Jacoby. The card preserves that format boundary instead of treating the optional convention as universal.

original_record.label: Jacoby rule
original_record.learning_takeaway: See how an optional scoring rule encourages use of the doubling cube.

relations.note: The source explains Jacoby's purpose through whether players use the doubling cube during the game.

original_record.card: In 1747, James Lind compared different remedies among sailors with scurvy; those given citrus improved. Yet he did not understand vitamin deficiency and retained other theories about the disease. His work separates the value of a treatment comparison from a correct explanation of its mechanism.

evidence.note: RCPE recounts the remedy groups, lemons/oranges outcome and Lind’s digestive/excretory theory without vitamin-deficiency understanding.

original_record.label: James Lind
original_record.learning_takeaway: Separate a useful controlled comparison from a correct explanation of why the treatment worked.

relations.note: Lind’s historical comparison offers a contrast with modern randomized trials; the relationship does not claim that his allocation was randomized.

original_record.card: James Naismith devised basketball at Springfield in 1891 to provide an engaging indoor winter activity. Avoiding the rough collisions of outdoor games shaped the design. Elevated peach baskets required players to toss the ball toward a goal rather than charge through it.

evidence.locator: A New Game; The Birth of Basketball
evidence.note: Springfield's account supports the winter brief, concern about roughness, elevated baskets and tossing; it does not establish that every modern rule originated unchanged in 1891.

original_record.label: James Naismith
original_record.learning_takeaway: See how indoor space and injury constraints shaped basketball's original design.

relations.note: The college's historical account identifies Naismith as basketball's inventor and explains the game's design constraints.

original_record.card: The Janissaries were an elite Ottoman infantry corps and household guard. Recruits trained for service to the ruler, including boys taken through devshirme. The sultans intended this force to reduce dependence on hereditary nobles, expecting recruits’ status and privileges to bind them to the ruler.

evidence.note: Elite corps, recruitment and reduced noble dependence are explicit.

original_record.label: Janissary corps
original_record.learning_takeaway: The Ottoman elite infantry and household guard drew recruits from state training and was intended to reduce dependence on hereditary nobles.

relations.note: The text connects the recruitment system with the formation of the corps.

original_record.card: Sarasa textiles made for Japanese buyers show that restrictions on overseas travel did not end foreign exchange. Indian cotton designs were adapted for this market and circulated through trade. Their surviving patterns make selective connections visible within a period often associated with isolation.

evidence.locator: Chinese Silk Exports and Trade Textiles in Japan, lines 132–136
evidence.note: Trade textiles for Japanese buyers continued despite travel restrictions.

original_record.label: Japanese sarasa trade textiles
original_record.learning_takeaway: Indian cottons designed for Japanese buyers circulated despite restrictions on Japanese overseas travel, showing selective trade rather than total isolation.

relations.note: Compare Japanese-market adaptation with Indian cottons made for other overseas buyers.

original_record.card: Jensen’s inequality compares two orders of operations. For a convex function and nonnegative weights summing to one, applying the function to a weighted average gives no more than averaging the function’s values. A nonlinear transformation therefore need not commute with taking an average.

evidence.locator: Jensen's Inequality -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1, 2, 3, 4 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2; paragraph-3; paragraph-4; paragraph-5
evidence.note: For a convex function, averaging before applying the function does not exceed averaging afterward.

original_record.label: Jensen’s inequality
original_record.learning_takeaway: For a convex function, averaging before applying the function does not exceed averaging afterward.

relations.note: Interpreting the weights as probabilities turns the finite weighted-average inequality into a comparison of average outcomes.

original_record.card: Jidoka builds a response to abnormalities into production. Toyota describes machines stopping when something goes wrong, helping prevent defects from continuing unnoticed. The approach can reduce the need for someone to watch a machine constantly, linking productivity to detecting problems rather than simply increasing operating speed.

evidence.locator: Jidoka or Autonomation; Roots of Ideas
evidence.note: Checked automatic stopping and reduced constant monitoring; does not claim every stopped problem is diagnosed or repaired automatically.

original_record.label: Jidoka
original_record.learning_takeaway: Stop work when an abnormality appears so defects are addressed without requiring constant human machine-watching.

relations.note: Toyota's production-system account pairs abnormality-responsive jidoka with just-in-time flow as its two central approaches.

original_record.card: Raft changes membership through a transitional joint configuration. Decisions during that phase require separate majorities of both the old and new configurations. This prevents the two memberships from making incompatible decisions independently while allowing servers to learn about the change at different times.

evidence.note: Checked old/new majority requirements and asynchronous transition; not reduced to a majority of the combined membership.

original_record.label: Joint consensus in Raft
original_record.learning_takeaway: Require separate old- and new-configuration majorities during membership changes to prevent incompatible simultaneous majorities.

relations.note: Section 6 explicitly defines joint consensus as Raft's transitional membership-change mechanism requiring both majorities.

original_record.card: A simple closed curve in a plane separates it into an inside and an outside. The Jordan curve theorem makes this familiar picture precise: the complement has two connected components, and the curve borders both. Self-intersections would change the problem and are excluded.

evidence.locator: Jordan Curve Theorem -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1, 2 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2; paragraph-3
evidence.note: A simple closed planar curve separates the plane into an inside and an outside.

original_record.label: Jordan curve theorem
original_record.learning_takeaway: A simple closed planar curve separates the plane into an inside and an outside.

relations.note: The result turns the connectivity of a planar complement into a rigorous topological statement.

original_record.card: Just-in-time production coordinates making and replenishing items with when they are needed. Toyota describes a pull system in which a later process obtains parts already used from an earlier one. This aims to shorten production time and limit unnecessary stock rather than keep every machine producing continuously.

evidence.note: Checked downstream pull and inventory/lead-time goals; no claim that all inventory is waste or that the method removes supply disruption risk.

original_record.label: Just-in-time production
original_record.learning_takeaway: Coordinate production and replenishment with downstream demand to shorten lead times and avoid unnecessary stock.

relations.note: Toyota explicitly presents just-in-time and jidoka as complementary components of its production system.

original_record.card: Just intonation favors intervals described by simple frequency ratios. Yet pure fifths and pure thirds do not fit every chain of notes identically: repeated three-to-two fifths can conflict with a pure third. Fixed-pitch instruments must therefore confront compromises that adjustable voices or strings can handle differently.

evidence.locator: What is all the fuss about temperament?
evidence.note: UNSW temperament discussion supplies the chain-of-fifths mismatch and fixed versus adjustable instrument distinction; no claim that one tuning is universally best.

original_record.label: Just intonation
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explore why pure small-ratio intervals create compromises when changing keys.

relations.note: The FAQ directly contrasts just intonation with meantone's compromise between thirds and fifths.

original_record.card: A just-noticeable difference measures the change needed to distinguish two stimulus intensities. The same added light can be conspicuous in a dark room yet barely noticeable in bright surroundings. This differs from asking whether any light can be detected at all, the question behind an absolute threshold.

evidence.note: OpenStax 5.1 contrasts difference and absolute thresholds using dark versus bright settings; avoid treating Weber's approximate scaling as universal across every intensity range.

original_record.label: Just-noticeable difference
original_record.learning_takeaway: See why noticing a change depends on the starting stimulus intensity.

relations.note: The textbook explicitly distinguishes detecting a stimulus from detecting a difference between stimuli.

original_record.card: The justified true belief analysis proposes that knowledge requires a belief to be true and adequately justified, with those conditions together sufficient. Truth excludes error; justification excludes unsupported lucky guesses. Gettier cases challenge the proposal by combining justification and truth with another kind of epistemic luck.

evidence.note: SEP sections 1 and 3 describe the tripartite proposal and its challenge; proposes and challenge prevent the analysis from being presented as the settled definition of knowledge.

original_record.label: Justified true belief analysis
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish a belief's truth and justification in a traditional analysis of knowledge.

relations.note: The entry explicitly presents Gettier counterexamples as a challenge to the sufficiency of justification, truth and belief together.

original_record.card: Kīlauea’s 2018 eruption linked activity far apart on the same volcano. Magma moved from summit storage toward the lower East Rift Zone, while the summit floor repeatedly collapsed. Increased pressure after collapse could boost the distant eruption rate, revealing a connected underground magma system.

evidence.note: USGS describes summit drainage and collapse, the hydraulic connection and post-collapse surges at the lower-rift vent.

original_record.label: Kīlauea
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explore how a flank eruption and summit collapse can be connected through a magma system.

relations.note: The named volcano’s 2018 summit subsidence illustrates collapse within a caldera and links it to distant magma discharge.

original_record.card: Karner blue butterfly larvae can exchange a sugary secretion for protection from ants. The ants gain food, while their attendance can reduce threats to the caterpillars. This butterfly offers a concrete example of mutualism, with the particular ant partners varying between locations.

evidence.note: The community-ecology passage describes carbohydrate-rich larval secretions, ant protection and variation in attending ant species.

original_record.label: Karner blue butterfly
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explore how ant attendance can protect butterfly larvae while the ants receive carbohydrate-rich secretions.

relations.note: The documented food-for-protection exchange illustrates mutualism in this named butterfly.

original_record.card: In karst terrain, water enlarges soluble-rock fractures and can travel through underground openings before emerging at springs. Surface streams alone may therefore miss important drainage routes. Rapid movement through these openings can also carry contamination with little filtration, linking rock structure to water quality.

evidence.note: NPS describes dissolution-created underground drainage and rapid water transport with limited filtration in karst aquifers.

original_record.label: Karst drainage
original_record.learning_takeaway: Trace water through fractures enlarged by dissolution rather than assuming it remains in surface streams.

relations.note: Comparing solution-driven drainage with an emptied lava conduit distinguishes two very different origins of underground passages.

original_record.card: Kepler’s original survey repeatedly measured the brightness of stars in one crowded field. Small, recurring dips could reveal planets crossing in front of their host stars. Concentrating on a stable field made long time series possible, turning subtle changes in starlight into evidence about unseen planetary systems.

evidence.locator: Kepler / K2; inspected passage indices 12, 13 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-13; paragraph-14
evidence.note: Long, continuous stellar-brightness measurements reveal repeated planetary transits across a crowded fixed field.

original_record.label: Kepler Space Telescope
original_record.learning_takeaway: Long, continuous stellar-brightness measurements reveal repeated planetary transits across a crowded fixed field.

relations.note: The mission description explicitly says Kepler detected planets through stellar-brightness transit dips.

original_record.card: Kerf bending cuts a series of slots into one side of wood while leaving a thin outer layer intact. The remaining web can flex around a curve. Slot spacing and depth affect the result, and the weakened piece usually needs a supporting form or backing to hold its shape.

evidence.note: WOOD’s demonstrated method describes cross-grain slots, retained outer material, spacing/depth tradeoffs and supporting attachment.

original_record.label: Kerf bending
original_record.learning_takeaway: Create a bend by cutting relief slots while retaining an outer web of material.

relations.note: Kerf bending removes material to permit flexure, while steam bending softens intact wood through heat and moisture.

original_record.card: A keystone species plays an especially important role in its community. On rocky shores, sea stars eat mussels that might otherwise dominate available space. Removing that predator can therefore change which other organisms are able to persist alongside the mussels.

evidence.note: The NPS sea-star account identifies keystone predation and mussel competition for intertidal space, with diversity effects.

original_record.label: Keystone species
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explain how a predator can maintain community diversity by limiting a space-dominating competitor.

relations.note: Pisaster ochraceus is the named sea-star example behind the predator–mussel community mechanism.

original_record.card: Khinalig’s cultural landscape includes a mountain village, seasonal grazing areas and the route joining them. Summer and winter locations form parts of one living system. The site demonstrates why a mobile way of life may need to be understood through a connected landscape rather than one settlement.

evidence.note: Village, pastures and migration route form the listed landscape.

original_record.label: Khinalig and Köç Yolu
original_record.learning_takeaway: A mountain village, lowland winter pasture and connecting route together make seasonal mobility visible at landscape scale.

relations.note: Seasonal movement between the site’s pastures is the transhumant practice described by UNESCO.

original_record.card: Khipus used knotted cords to record information in the Inka world. Differences in knots, colors and cord arrangements supported numerical administration, including accounts of labor and goods. They demonstrate a system of record keeping whose organization cannot be understood by looking for written alphabetic words.

evidence.note: Knot/color structure and administrative recording are described.

original_record.label: Khipu
original_record.learning_takeaway: Knotted cords with differing colors and structures recorded numerical information used to administer labor, goods and taxation.

relations.note: Record keeping and state storage offer complementary views of Inka administration.

original_record.card: Kiichiro Toyoda advocated coordinating automobile parts just when they were needed while working with limited resources. Toyota's history connects that concern with just-in-time production and later downstream pull arrangements. The case shows how production timing emerged from a concrete coordination problem, rather than from simply demanding faster work.

evidence.locator: Roots of Ideas, How did the idea of Just-in-Time come about?
evidence.note: Checked the founder's timing concern and later development; did not credit one person with every subsequent Toyota-system technique.

original_record.label: Kiichiro Toyoda
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explore how limited resources shaped his effort to coordinate automobile parts just when production needed them.

relations.note: Toyota expressly connects Kiichiro Toyoda's resource-constrained manufacturing plans with the origins of just-in-time production.

original_record.card: Knickerbocker Trust Company's 1907 crisis intensified after it lost clearing support and depositors withdrew funds. Potential rescuers could not quickly establish its solvency, and the company suspended operations. The case distinguishes an urgent need for liquidity from having enough information to judge whether rescue lending is sound.

evidence.note: Checked denied support, uncertain solvency and suspension sequence; uncertainty is not rewritten as proof that the institution was insolvent.

original_record.label: Knickerbocker Trust Company
original_record.learning_takeaway: Examine how uncertain solvency, lost clearing support, and deposit withdrawals culminated in a trust company's suspension.

relations.note: The history identifies Knickerbocker's suspension as a key event in the widening Panic of 1907.

original_record.card: Knitting gauge counts stitches and rows within a given length of fabric. A swatch tests the yarn, needles and stitch pattern together before a larger project is made. If the gauge differs from the pattern, the same stitch count can produce a different finished size.

evidence.note: Craft Yarn Council defines stitch/row density, the gauge swatch and changing needle size when the swatch dimensions differ.

original_record.label: Knitting gauge
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect stitches and rows per unit length with the dimensions a knitting pattern will produce.

relations.note: Blocking can change fabric dimensions, so the source’s recommendation to test blocking on a swatch links finishing behavior with measured gauge.

original_record.card: A baseball's seams make its surface aerodynamically uneven. As their orientation changes during flight, the effective location and direction of aerodynamic forces can vary. NASA connects these unsteady forces with the knuckleball's erratic motion, rather than explaining it solely through a steady spin-generated curve.

evidence.locator: Lift: stitches and center of pressure
evidence.note: NASA Forces on a Baseball, Lift, supports seam-dependent pressure changes and erratic motion; contrast with its separate simplified curveball model is labeled editorial in the relationship.
Steady spinning-ball trajectory is a comparison premise, not the knuckleball explanation itself.

original_record.label: Knuckleball aerodynamics
original_record.learning_takeaway: Understand erratic flight from seam-dependent forces varying during the pitch.

relations.note: Contrasting seam-sensitive, time-varying forces with a regular spinning-ball model separates two different explanations of curved baseball flight.

original_record.card: A ko capture can create an opportunity for immediate recapture that would restore the previous position. The basic ko rule forbids that immediate reply. The player must first play elsewhere, giving the opponent an opportunity to respond or end the local cycle.

evidence.note: BGA ko diagrams and explanatory paragraph support immediate-recapture restriction and intervening play; this does not claim that a single intervening move overrides every superko rule.
Superko forbids longer repeating positions; the comparison is editorial.

original_record.label: Ko rule
original_record.learning_takeaway: See why immediate recapture must wait for a play elsewhere.

relations.note: Immediate ko and situational superko both limit repetition, but the latter also addresses longer cycles such as triple ko.

original_record.card: Komi compensates the player using White stones for Black's first move in Go. It adds points to White's final score rather than adding stones to the board. The British Go Association's cited default uses seven-and-a-half points; other rules or agreements can use different values.

evidence.note: BGA Default Rules gives 7½ and contrasts traditional Japanese values; How to Play explains compensation rather than placement of stones.
The guide explains compensation to White for Black moving first.

original_record.label: Komi
original_record.learning_takeaway: Understand points compensating White for playing second.

relations.note: The tournament rules identify komi as a score adjustment within Go, separately from handicap-stone placement.

original_record.card: A ksar is a fortified settlement grouping homes and shared spaces within defensive walls. Southern Moroccan examples use earthen construction adapted to their setting. Looking at dwellings together with communal facilities reveals how collective defense and everyday settlement organization could share the same built form.

evidence.note: Ait-Ben-Haddou’s collective earthen settlement supports the definition and organization.

original_record.label: Ksar
original_record.learning_takeaway: A fortified collective settlement groups homes and communal spaces within defensive walls, exemplified by southern Moroccan earthen villages.

relations.note: The named site is explicitly presented as a ksar with defensive and communal features.

original_record.card: OpenStax uses L.L.Bean's mail-order business as a case of selling goods customers cannot inspect beforehand. A guarantee and a reputation for quality can reduce that uncertainty. The example illustrates how trust supports remote retail, rather than establishing the company's current return policy or every customer's experience.

evidence.note: Checked historical/textbook attribution and reputation mechanism; no current policy term is inferred from an older explanatory case.

original_record.label: L.L.Bean
original_record.learning_takeaway: Use the textbook's mail-order case to see how guarantees and reputation can reduce buyers' uncertainty without inspecting goods.

relations.note: The textbook explicitly uses L.L.Bean to illustrate reputation and guarantees as reassurance under imperfect information.

original_record.card: A laboratory reference interval describes results found in a selected comparison population. Being outside it does not automatically establish disease, and being inside it does not guarantee health. Different laboratories, methods and patient groups can use different ranges, so the reported context matters.

evidence.note: MedlinePlus bases ranges on healthy comparison groups and explicitly warns about out-of-range healthy results, in-range illness and method/group differences.

original_record.label: Laboratory reference intervals
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explain why being outside a population reference range does not by itself establish disease.

relations.note: A1c illustrates why a laboratory number must be interpreted with the test’s purpose and biological limitations, alongside any reported range.

original_record.card: Lagrange’s group theorem explains why a subgroup’s size divides the size of a finite group. Its cosets partition the group into equally sized blocks. The divisibility condition is necessary, but it does not guarantee that a subgroup exists for every divisor of the group’s order.

evidence.locator: Lagrange's Group Theorem -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1, 2, 3, 4 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2; paragraph-3; paragraph-4; paragraph-5
evidence.note: Equal-sized subgroup cosets partition a finite group, forcing subgroup order to divide group order.

original_record.label: Lagrange’s group theorem
original_record.learning_takeaway: Equal-sized subgroup cosets partition a finite group, forcing subgroup order to divide group order.

relations.note: The quotient-group reference invokes Lagrange’s theorem to relate the group, subgroup, and coset counts.

original_record.card: A lahar is a moving mixture of water and volcanic debris, not a stream of molten lava. It can rush through valleys during an eruption, afterward or even while a volcano is quiet. Recognizing the mixture and its possible timing changes how volcanic hazards are understood.

evidence.note: The USGS lahar explanation distinguishes debris-and-water flows from lava and states that lahars can occur during eruptions or inactivity.

original_record.label: Lahar
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish fast volcanic debris-and-water flows from molten lava.

relations.note: Lahars and lava tubes contrast water–debris transport with molten-rock transport, avoiding a common conflation of volcanic flow types.

original_record.card: Cold air moving across a warmer, unfrozen lake gains heat and moisture. As that air rises, narrow cloud bands can form and deliver lake-effect snow downwind. Wind direction strongly affects where the snow falls, so heavy snowfall can occur close to places receiving very little.

evidence.note: NWS describes heat/moisture transfer over unfrozen Great Lakes, rising air, narrow snow bands and strong wind-direction dependence.

original_record.label: Lake-effect snow
original_record.learning_takeaway: Trace narrow snow bands to cold air gaining heat and moisture over unfrozen lake water.

relations.note: These are different routes to precipitation: local moisture uptake over a lake versus concentrated long-distance vapor transport.

original_record.card: Lalibela’s churches were carved into rock and connected through passages and carefully managed drainage. Together they form a sacred landscape rather than a set of isolated monuments. Their arrangement expressed religious meaning while addressing the practical demands of moving through and maintaining excavated spaces.

evidence.note: Rock-cut churches, passages, drainage and sacred landscape are described.

original_record.label: Lalibela’s rock-hewn churches
original_record.learning_takeaway: Carved churches, passages and drainage works made a sacred landscape that served as a symbolic alternative to distant holy places.

relations.note: The connected sacred complex links religious meanings with the shaping and management of terrain.

original_record.card: Landsat’s repeated satellite observations provide a long record of changes on Earth’s surface. Careful calibration helps researchers compare images across years and distinguish real changes in forests, cities or coastlines from changes in measurement. The archive’s value grows through continuity as well as through individual pictures.

evidence.locator: About Landsat, calibration and long-term comparisons
evidence.note: NASA describes the long continuous record, science-grade calibration and applications to cities, coasts, crops and forests.

original_record.label: Landsat
original_record.learning_takeaway: Use consistently calibrated imagery to distinguish real long-term land changes from sensor differences.

relations.note: The NPS thermokarst account uses Landsat images to monitor lake-area change, providing a concrete application of the long surface record.

original_record.card: Language documentation creates records of language use and the knowledge expressed through it. Recording community stories can preserve family histories as well as linguistic forms. Such records may support future work, but making an archive is different from ensuring that people continue learning and using the language.

evidence.note: Checked story-recording and family-legacy functions; explicitly avoided treating documentation as sufficient evidence of revitalization.

original_record.label: Language documentation
original_record.learning_takeaway: Create records of language use and community knowledge that can serve both research and family legacies.

relations.note: The Michif case distinguishes preserving records from choosing locally appropriate reclamation priorities; documentation and sustained use are connected but not equivalent.

original_record.card: A lava tube begins when the surface of a flowing lava stream cools into a crust while molten material continues beneath it. If the lava later drains away, an empty passage remains. The cave records a former flow route rather than a space carved by underground water.

evidence.note: NPS’s formation account describes a roof forming over flowing lava and subsequent drainage leaving a tube.

original_record.label: Lava tube
original_record.learning_takeaway: Trace a volcanic cave from a crusted-over lava stream to an emptied conduit.

relations.note: Lava tubes and karst passages can both be caves, but their formation mechanisms differ: cooling/drainage versus dissolution by water.

original_record.card: Le Châtelier’s principle predicts how equilibrium responds when conditions change. At fixed temperature, compressing a gaseous mixture favors the side with fewer gas molecules when the sides differ. Temperature changes also shift equilibrium, with direction depending on whether the reaction absorbs or releases heat.

evidence.locator: 13.3 Shifting Equilibria: Le Châtelier’s Principle; inspected passage indices 5, 24, 42 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-idp113339808; fs-idm173238784; fs-idp156642144
evidence.note: Predict how concentration, volume, or temperature changes disturb and re-establish chemical equilibrium.

original_record.label: Le Châtelier’s principle
original_record.learning_takeaway: Predict how concentration, volume, or temperature changes disturb and re-establish chemical equilibrium.

relations.note: The passage explicitly presents the principle as a description of equilibrium shifts following imposed changes.

original_record.card: Screening can move a diagnosis earlier without changing when a person dies. Survival measured from diagnosis then looks longer simply because the clock started sooner. Lead-time bias explains why improved survival after detection does not, by itself, prove that a screening program saves lives.

evidence.note: NCI explains earlier diagnosis adding lead time to measured survival without necessarily delaying death.

original_record.label: Lead-time bias
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explain how earlier diagnosis can lengthen measured survival without delaying death.

relations.note: Lead-time bias shifts the survival clock, whereas overdiagnosis adds cases that would not have become clinically harmful; both can distort apparent screening success.

original_record.card: The principle of least collaborative effort proposes that conversational partners minimize their combined work through mutual acceptance of a contribution. A perfectly prepared utterance is not always cheapest overall. A shorter presentation followed by a quick clarification may require less total effort than preventing every possible misunderstanding in advance.

evidence.note: Checked combined rather than speaker-only effort and completion through acceptance; this is an explanatory principle, not a measured law of every conversation.

original_record.label: Least collaborative effort
original_record.learning_takeaway: Model conversational choices by the combined work of both participants through mutual acceptance, rather than minimizing only speaking effort.

relations.note: Clark and Brennan explicitly introduce the joint-effort principle to explain grounding choices, repairs and differences across media.

original_record.card: Leather temper describes how readily a hide bends, drapes or holds its shape. It is different from thickness: equally thick pieces can feel quite different. A soft garment panel and a firm structured bag may require different tempers, so flexing a sample reveals information a thickness measurement cannot.

evidence.locator: Definition; Matching temper to the job; Describing temper
evidence.note: United Leather distinguishes temper from thickness and relates soft/firm behavior to garment and structured-bag uses; Tandy independently defines pliability.
The independent supplier glossary defines temper as finished-leather pliability from stiff to supple.

original_record.label: Leather temper
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish a hide’s pliability from its thickness when choosing between draping and shape-holding uses.

relations.note: Temper is a particular mechanical property of finished leather, not a different material identity or simply its thickness.

original_record.card: Lectio divina is prayerful engagement with scripture through reading, meditation, prayer and contemplation. In the Catholic account cited here, the practice is intended to lead toward action. Its aim is to let attentive reading shape religious life, rather than merely extracting information from a passage.

evidence.note: The cited paragraph identifies the stages and consequence for action.

original_record.label: Lectio divina
original_record.learning_takeaway: Prayerful scriptural reading moves through attention to the text, meditation, prayer and contemplation, with an intended consequence for action.

relations.note: The Vatican account presents this as a Christian practice of scriptural reading.

original_record.card: A liberty is an empty intersection directly beside a Go stone along a horizontal or vertical line. Connected stones share their liberties as one string. Surrounding every liberty captures the entire string, so adding a connection can change the survival prospects of several stones at once.

evidence.note: BGA capture section supports orthogonal adjacency and whole-string treatment; the connection consequence follows directly from sharing the resulting string's liberties.

original_record.label: Liberties in Go
original_record.learning_takeaway: Count shared adjacent empty points for an entire connected string.

relations.note: The Go guide uses liberties to define when individual stones and connected strings are captured.

original_record.card: Elizabeth Peyton’s Lichtenstein, Flowers, Parsifal combines references to Lichtenstein’s dots, Wagner’s opera and still-life imagery in a monotype. The dots are hand-applied before printing. An editorial reading emphasizes the contrast between mechanically associated marks and their manual realization.

evidence.note: The MoMA account identifies all three references and handwork in the dots.

original_record.label: Lichtenstein, Flowers, Parsifal
original_record.learning_takeaway: Elizabeth Peyton’s monotype brings references to Lichtenstein’s dots, Wagner’s opera and still-life painting into one image, translating mechanically associated marks into handwork.

relations.note: MoMA identifies this specific work as a monotype and discusses its hand-applied marks.

original_record.card: A linguistic change from above spreads with social awareness, often through adoption of a prestigious variant from outside a community.
