The arrangement differs from deeply immersing the whole root system, and depends on keeping that moving supply available.

evidence.note: UMN describes shallow continuous flow through channels, return circulation and the root-zone arrangement.

original_record.label: Nutrient-film technique
original_record.learning_takeaway: Circulate a shallow nutrient stream past roots while retaining access to oxygen.

relations.note: The channel-and-shallow-flow arrangement is a specific hydroponic system described in the source.

original_record.card: An oasis settlement joins habitation and agriculture to a dependable local water supply within an arid region. At Al Ain, irrigation works and settlement remains record this relationship over time. Water management helps explain how settled life could persist in an otherwise demanding desert landscape.

evidence.note: Al Ain links irrigation and sustained desert settlement.

original_record.label: Oasis settlement
original_record.learning_takeaway: Reliable managed water lets settled agriculture and habitation persist within desert landscapes, as archaeological evidence at Al Ain illustrates.

relations.note: The named archaeological landscape preserves evidence of the settlement-water relationship.

original_record.card: The observer's paradox in sociolinguistics is that researchers want to study how people speak when they are not being observed, yet must observe them to collect evidence. A recording or unfamiliar interviewer can change self-monitoring, so natural rapport helps but cannot guarantee completely unmonitored speech.

evidence.note: Checked observation/self-monitoring tension and absence of a foolproof elicitation method; not equated with experimenter expectancy or socially desirable answers generally.

original_record.label: Observer's paradox in sociolinguistics
original_record.learning_takeaway: Recognize that systematically recording everyday speech may change the very speech researchers want to observe.

relations.note: The methods chapter explicitly identifies the observer's paradox as a central difficulty in obtaining vernacular speech through interviews.

original_record.card: When seawater absorbs carbon dioxide, chemical reactions increase hydrogen ions and reduce the availability of carbonate ions. Ocean acidification can therefore make building some shells and skeletons more difficult. The change concerns a shift in ocean chemistry, not a claim that seawater has become acidic in everyday terms.

evidence.note: NOAA explains CO2 uptake, increased hydrogen ions, reduced carbonate availability and effects on calcifying organisms.

original_record.label: Ocean acidification
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect absorbed atmospheric CO2 with more hydrogen ions and less available carbonate.

relations.note: Acidification and bleaching are distinct pressures on marine organisms: carbonate chemistry versus loss of coral symbiotic algae.

original_record.card: Shelley’s Ode to the West Wind adapts terza rima into five units resembling sonnets. Interlocking tercets lead into closing couplets, joining forward movement with repeated moments of closure. The poem offers a specific case of reshaping an inherited rhyme pattern for a different design.

evidence.note: Five sonnet-like sections, tercets and closing couplets are described.

original_record.label: Ode to the West Wind
original_record.learning_takeaway: Shelley adapts interlocking tercets into five sonnet-like units, each closing with a couplet.

relations.note: The glossary names Shelley’s poem as an adaptation of this rhyme form.

original_record.card: An offside position is judged when a teammate plays or touches the ball, but position alone is not an offence. Penalization requires the specified involvement in active play. A player receiving the ball directly from a goal kick, throw-in or corner kick commits no offside offence.

evidence.note: IFAB Law 11.1–11.3 fixes the position assessment at the teammate play/touch and separately requires active involvement. Direct goal-kick, throw-in and corner-kick receipt are the stated exceptions; no exhaustive geometry or contact-point nuance is asserted.

original_record.label: Offside in association football
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish occupying an offside position from committing an offside offence.

relations.note: IFAB identifies offside as Law 11 within association football's Laws of the Game.

original_record.card: Ofuda are shrine tablets of paper or wood bearing a kami’s or shrine’s name. Commonly placed on a household altar, they are understood by practitioners to extend sacred protection into the home. The object links domestic veneration with the shrine from which it was received.

evidence.note: Named paper/wood tablets, household placement and attributed protection are explicit.

original_record.label: Ofuda
original_record.learning_takeaway: A shrine tablet bearing a kami or shrine name supports veneration in the home, extending a visit into domestic religious life.

relations.note: Jinja Honcho describes ofuda as a shrine-related form of domestic kami veneration.

original_record.card: Omamori are small protective amulets associated with shrines and particular requests, such as seeking good fortune or avoiding danger. Often carried in bags, they are understood to hold a kami’s presence. Their portability connects a shrine visit with a person’s ordinary movements and concerns.

evidence.note: Personal requests, attributed kami presence and carrying in bags are described.

original_record.label: Omamori
original_record.learning_takeaway: A portable shrine amulet is often selected for a particular request and carried as an expression of a kami’s protection.

relations.note: The source contrasts portable personal amulets with tablets commonly placed on household altars.

original_record.card: Elizabeth Bishop’s One Art moves from small misplaced things toward more intimate loss within a villanelle’s returning lines. An editorial reading hears the repeated assurance becoming harder to sustain. The poem offers a way to examine how formal repetition can expose strain as well as control.

evidence.note: The poem supports the sequence of losses; l12 explicitly identifies the villanelle form.
Names One Art as a villanelle with refrain variation.

original_record.label: One Art
original_record.learning_takeaway: Bishop’s villanelle moves from small losses toward personal loss; an editorial reading hears increasing strain in its repeated assurance.

relations.note: The Academy’s glossary identifies One Art as a villanelle that varies its refrains.

original_record.card: An open repair request signals that something in the previous message was unclear without identifying the troublesome part. A brief Huh? is one example. Because the speaker receives little information about the problem, resolving it may require repeating or reformulating more of the earlier utterance.

evidence.locator: Results, Three basic types recur in all languages, pp. 4–5
evidence.note: Checked unspecified trouble and qualified longer/repeated response tendency; not treated as interchangeable with a targeted question.

original_record.label: Open repair request
original_record.learning_takeaway: Request help with an unclear message without specifying which part caused difficulty.

relations.note: The repair study explicitly defines open requests as one of three functionally distinct other-initiated repair types and describes their response patterns.

original_record.card: Open security design keeps protection from depending on attackers being ignorant of how the mechanism works. Specific keys or passwords remain secret instead. This separation allows the design to be examined by reviewers without assuming that publishing its structure necessarily defeats the protection.

evidence.note: Checked public mechanism versus secret key; openness is not claimed sufficient for security or a reason to disclose credentials.

Supplementary inspected premise for the card or its comparison: The source explicitly contrasts open mechanisms with protected keys; cryptographic protocols offer a concrete setting for exploring that distinction.

original_record.label: Open security design
original_record.learning_takeaway: Keep protection dependent on guarded keys rather than secrecy of the mechanism, enabling public review.

relations.note: The source explicitly contrasts open mechanisms with protected keys; cryptographic protocols offer a concrete setting for exploring that distinction.

original_record.card: Neo-Impressionists placed separate colored strokes beside one another in the hope that they would interact in the viewer’s perception. They sought effects different from physically mixing pigments beforehand. Understanding optical mixing here means examining an artistic strategy and its historical ambitions, rather than assuming literal pigment fusion.

evidence.note: The Met explains the artists’ optical-mixture aim and separated strokes.

original_record.label: Optical mixing
original_record.learning_takeaway: Neo-Impressionists separated colored strokes in the hope that their interaction in the viewer’s eye would produce more vibrant effects than physically mixed pigments.

relations.note: The essay presents Seurat’s painting as a major demonstration of the separated-color approach.

original_record.card: An oral-history lead-in records basic context at the start of a session: who is speaking, when and where it happens, and the intended subject. Appropriate names or pseudonyms preserve identification while avoiding unnecessary exposure, such as stating a private home address.

evidence.note: Interviewing 2 specifies contextual identifiers and cautions about residential addresses.

original_record.label: Oral-history interview lead-in
original_record.learning_takeaway: Recording participant names or pseudonyms, date, setting and proposed subject preserves the interview’s context for future users.

relations.note: A recorded lead-in is a specific interviewing practice within oral history.

original_record.card: An organic organizational structure gives people more room to coordinate and make decisions as circumstances change. Authority is less tightly concentrated, and work relies less exclusively on fixed routines. The idea describes a flexible design orientation, rather than simply naming the friendships that arise inside any workplace.

evidence.note: Checked design flexibility versus informal relationships; an organic structure is not assumed to have no responsibilities, hierarchy or rules.

original_record.label: Organic organizational structure
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distribute decisions and rely on adaptive coordination when work and circumstances change quickly.

relations.note: OpenStax explicitly contrasts organic flexibility and distributed decisions with mechanistic hierarchy and standardization.

original_record.card: Organizational formalization describes how explicitly roles, duties, and accountability are defined. A highly formalized system spells them out closely; a looser one relies more on relationships that emerge through work. Formalization is a matter of degree, distinct from whether an organization has any structure at all.

evidence.note: Checked degree of definition and contrast with emergent coordination; formalization is not equated with the existence of a formal organization chart alone.

original_record.label: Organizational formalization
original_record.learning_takeaway: Specify roles, responsibilities, and accountability to different degrees instead of leaving all coordination to emergent relationships.

relations.note: The organizational-design chapter explicitly identifies formalization as one of the dimensions managers consider when arranging structure.

original_record.card: An orientable surface admits a consistent choice of orientation across its tangent planes. That choice can vary continuously as you move across the surface. A Möbius strip shows what can go wrong: its half-twist prevents a locally chosen side from remaining globally consistent.

evidence.locator: Orientable Surface -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2
evidence.note: Defines orientability through continuously chosen tangent-space structure.

evidence.locator: Möbius Strip -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2
evidence.note: Defines the half-twisted Möbius band as one-sided and nonorientable.

original_record.label: Orientable surface
original_record.learning_takeaway: Local tangent-space orientations can be chosen continuously across an orientable surface.

relations.note: The Möbius strip’s stated nonorientability provides the concrete contrast for the abstract continuous-orientation definition.

original_record.card: Original order preserves the arrangement a record creator used, when that order can be established and remains meaningful. Keeping the sequence may reveal how an office or person worked. Rearranging everything by a modern subject scheme can erase those functional connections.

evidence.note: Creator arrangement and evidential relationships support the principle.

original_record.label: Original order in archives
original_record.learning_takeaway: Preserving a creator’s record sequence can retain evidence of how the records functioned, rather than replacing it with a modern subject arrangement.

relations.note: Creator-based grouping and internal arrangement preserve different relationships among records.

original_record.card: An oscillator’s quality factor describes how sharply it responds near resonance. With light damping, oscillations persist and the resonance peak is narrow; stronger damping broadens it. A tuned radio circuit uses a narrow response to select one frequency while reducing its response to nearby ones.

evidence.locator: 15.6 Forced Oscillations; inspected passage indices 16 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-id1167131421041
evidence.note: Light damping produces narrow resonance curves and high frequency selectivity; the tuned-radio example applies this qualitative relation.

evidence.locator: 15.5 Damped Oscillations; inspected passage indices 9 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-id1167131181569
evidence.note: Weak damping lets oscillations persist while their amplitude gradually decreases.

original_record.label: Oscillator quality factor
original_record.learning_takeaway: Lower damping produces a narrower resonant response and more selective frequency discrimination.

relations.note: The source introduces quality factor through the width and damping of resonant oscillator responses.

original_record.card: Othello changes the ownership of pieces already on the board. A player places a disc to bracket an uninterrupted line of opposing discs, then flips those discs to their color. The winner has more discs when neither player can make a legal move.

evidence.note: Official outflanking and ending rules support placement, flipping and the final majority; the game need not fill all sixty-four squares.

original_record.label: Othello
original_record.learning_takeaway: Understand how a placement changes ownership of intervening discs.

relations.note: A lack of outflanking moves determines both forced passes and the eventual end of the game.

original_record.card: Other-initiated repair occurs when a listener signals trouble with someone else's message and the original speaker helps resolve it. The response may repeat words, clarify a missing detail, or confirm an interpretation. This creates a collaborative detour aimed at restoring understanding so the conversation can proceed.

evidence.locator: Introduction; Materials and Methods, repair-sequence definition
evidence.note: The paper defines trouble source, repair initiator and repair solution. Repair may require more than one attempt; reported brief durations are averages in the sampled corpus. The card describes the collaborative aim without guaranteeing a brief or immediately successful outcome.

evidence.locator: Opening; Grounding in Conversation; contribution model
evidence.note: Supplementary inspected premise for the card or its comparison: Repair makes a breakdown explicit, while grounding also includes routine evidence of understanding; the two sources support their connection without making them equivalent.

original_record.label: Other-initiated conversational repair
original_record.learning_takeaway: Signal trouble with another speaker's message so the original speaker can repeat, clarify, or confirm it.

relations.note: Repair makes a breakdown explicit, while grounding also includes routine evidence of understanding; the two sources support their connection without making them equivalent.

original_record.card: The cochlea can produce very quiet sounds when its sensory hair cells respond to stimulation. An otoacoustic-emission test records these responses through a probe in the ear canal. Weak or absent emissions need careful interpretation because outer- or middle-ear problems can also obstruct the returning sound.

evidence.note: The hearing-test source describes cochlear hair-cell responses and warns that blockage or middle-ear problems can prevent emissions from being recorded.

original_record.label: Otoacoustic emissions
original_record.learning_takeaway: Use tiny cochlear sounds as evidence about inner-ear function while considering transmission blockages.

relations.note: Middle-ear assessment can help interpret an emission result because sound must pass through that pathway to be recorded.

original_record.card: The Otto cycle idealizes a spark-ignition piston engine through compression, rapid heat addition, expansion, and heat rejection. Heat is added and removed at fixed volume in the model. The enclosed area on its pressure–volume diagram represents net work, after accounting for work spent compressing the gas.

evidence.locator: Ideal Otto Cycle; inspected passage indices 2, 3, 4 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-3; paragraph-4; paragraph-5
evidence.note: A simplified spark-ignition engine cycle converts heat into net work represented by enclosed pressure-volume area.

original_record.label: Otto cycle
original_record.learning_takeaway: A simplified spark-ignition engine cycle converts heat into net work represented by enclosed pressure-volume area.

relations.note: The NASA reference presents the thermodynamic cycle as an explanation of an engine producing work from heat.

original_record.card: Overdiagnosis occurs when testing finds a real condition that would never have caused symptoms or harm during a person’s life. The finding is not necessarily a false-positive result. Detecting it can still expose someone to unnecessary investigations or treatment, so more diagnoses need not mean better health.

evidence.note: NCI describes screen-detected cancers that would never become clinically apparent and ensuing harms from diagnosis/treatment.

original_record.label: Overdiagnosis
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish detecting a real condition from finding one that would ever have harmed the patient.

relations.note: Overdiagnosis changes which cases are counted, while lead time changes when the survival clock begins; they are separate screening biases/harms.

original_record.card: An overlong UTF-8 sequence uses more bytes than the encoding permits for a character. Accepting such sequences can make one character appear in multiple byte patterns. Security checks may reject a forbidden normal encoding yet overlook an invalid alternative that a later parser interprets identically.

evidence.note: Checked invalidity and the bypass mechanism; no actionable exploit procedure or claim that all parsers accept such sequences.

original_record.label: Overlong UTF-8 encodings
original_record.learning_takeaway: Reject longer-than-permitted encodings so alternate byte sequences cannot bypass character-based security checks.

relations.note: RFC 3629 sections 3 and 10 explicitly prohibit invalid overlong sequences and describe their parser-security consequences.

original_record.card: A palampore is a large Indian painted cotton textile often used as a bedcover or hanging. Many export examples arrange abundant flowers around a central tree. Their designs show how makers shaped local techniques and motifs for the tastes of distant buyers.

evidence.locator: Indian Painted and Printed Cottons, line 147
evidence.note: Large painted cottons, central-tree patterns and European-market adaptation are explicit.

original_record.label: Palampore
original_record.learning_takeaway: Indian hand-painted cotton bedcovers commonly organized luxuriant flowers around a central tree and were tailored to European markets.

relations.note: The museum presents palampores within the overseas trade in Indian painted cottons.

original_record.card: The Panic of 1907 spread through trust companies that were important lenders but largely outside New York's clearing-house support network. Runs on their deposits disrupted wider market liquidity. The episode shows how vulnerability can grow at institutional boundaries, rather than remaining confined to the first troubled bank.

evidence.note: Checked trust-company importance, runs and liquidity propagation; no claim that one cause alone explains the entire worldwide crisis.

original_record.label: Panic of 1907
original_record.learning_takeaway: Trace how runs on institutions outside the main clearing-house support network disrupted wider financial-market liquidity.

relations.note: Federal Reserve History explicitly explains the clearing house's membership boundary and its role in supporting some institutions during the panic.

original_record.card: A pantoum repeats lines in new positions across successive stanzas. The words return, but their neighbors and grammatical connections can change. Following those shifts shows how a fixed pattern of recurrence can generate new meanings without requiring every repeated line to be rewritten.

evidence.note: Repeated lines move between stanza positions and change context.

original_record.label: Pantoum
original_record.learning_takeaway: Lines recur in new stanza positions, so changing context and punctuation can shift their meaning.

relations.note: Both use recurrence, but pantoum line recycling differs from the villanelle’s paired refrains.
The Academy presents the pantoum as a poetic form organized by recurring lines.

original_record.card: Machine-made paper often has fibers preferentially aligned in one direction, called its grain. Folding across that direction can produce uneven creases, and moisture from adhesive causes greater expansion across the grain. These directional differences matter when arranging folds and glued parts in bookbinding.

evidence.note: Cornell’s preservation tutorial describes machine-aligned fibers, cross-grain fold puckering and larger moisture expansion across grain.

original_record.label: Paper grain direction in bookbinding
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect aligned paper fibers with easier folding along the grain and unequal expansion when adhesive wets the sheet.

relations.note: Grain direction is a specific material consideration when folds and glued paper elements are assembled in bookbinding.

original_record.card: Paris law estimates fatigue-crack growth in an intermediate growth regime. Crack advance per loading cycle follows an empirical power of the stress-intensity range. The fitted constants depend on the material and conditions, and the law does not describe every near-threshold or final rapid-fracture stage.

evidence.locator: Chapter 10: Creep, Fracture, and Fatigue; inspected passage indices 204, 210, 211, 212, 213 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-205; paragraph-211; paragraph-212; paragraph-213; paragraph-214
evidence.note: In the middle growth regime, an empirical power law links crack advance per cycle to stress-intensity range.

original_record.label: Paris law for fatigue crack growth
original_record.learning_takeaway: In the middle growth regime, an empirical power law links crack advance per cycle to stress-intensity range.

relations.note: The cited section explicitly presents Paris law as a model of fatigue-crack growth.

original_record.card: Park Grass has studied grassland responses to fertilizer and liming since the nineteenth century. Its long record is not a single unchanging protocol: later liming subplots and changes in harvesting affect comparisons. Reading the experiment requires the treatment and measurement history alongside the hay-yield numbers.

evidence.locator: Study description; Liming design; Harvest methods
evidence.note: The e-RA dataset describes the experiment’s 1856 origin, 1965 liming subplots, hay yields and historical harvesting changes affecting comparability.

original_record.label: Park Grass Experiment
original_record.learning_takeaway: Interpret a long-term grassland experiment in light of treatment design and changes in measurement methods.

relations.note: Both experiments offer long records, but the inspected Park Grass design is a distinct grassland/liming study rather than another name for Broadbalk wheat plots.

original_record.card: The Parliament Act 1911 followed the Lords' rejection of the 1909 budget. It replaced their veto over most Commons public bills with delay, while excluding bills extending Parliament beyond five years. The 1949 Act shortened that delay, showing how legislative power shifted between the chambers.

evidence.locator: Why were the Parliament Acts brought into force?; Bills not subject to the Parliament Acts
evidence.note: UK Parliament history and Bills not subject sections support the 1909 conflict, qualified veto reduction, exclusion of extensions beyond five years and 1949 shortening. This is not a rule for every bill or all changes to parliamentary duration.

original_record.label: Parliament Act 1911
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect the 1909 budget conflict with replacing most Lords vetoes by delay.

relations.note: The official explanation sets the Act within normal Commons–Lords agreement and specifies circumstances where one chamber's consent can be bypassed.

original_record.card: Parliamentary sovereignty is the UK's principle that Parliament is the supreme legal authority and can make or repeal laws. One Parliament cannot generally prevent a later Parliament from changing its legislation. Institutional reforms may constrain how power is exercised without, in this account, extinguishing that legal principle.

evidence.locator: Opening and Developments affecting Parliamentary sovereignty
evidence.note: UK Parliament's sovereignty page states supremacy, future repeal and reforms; generally and in this account preserve the official explanation's legal qualifications and avoid denying practical political constraints.

original_record.label: Parliamentary sovereignty
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explore Parliament's legal supremacy in the UK and its relationship with institutional reforms.

relations.note: The official page presents sovereignty as a central principle of the UK's partly written, uncodified constitution, directly connecting principle and constitutional form.

original_record.card: Some greenhouse cucumber varieties can form seedless fruit without pollination, an example of parthenocarpy. Pollinating those varieties may instead introduce seeds. The case separates fruit development from seed production, while reminding growers that a pollination rule useful for one cucumber type may not fit another.

evidence.note: UMN’s cucumber passage specifically identifies parthenocarpic greenhouse varieties, fruit without pollination and possible seed production if pollinated.

original_record.label: Parthenocarpy
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish fruit formation without pollination in selected cucumber varieties from ordinary pollination-dependent fruit set.

relations.note: The cucumber case contrasts fruit formation without pollination with fruit crops that need pollen from a compatible partner.

original_record.card: Password salting adds a separate value when a password is hashed for storage. Different salts help prevent equal passwords from routinely producing equal stored hashes. A suitable password-hashing scheme also makes each guess costly; salting and computational expense address different parts of an offline guessing attack.

evidence.note: Checked salt collision minimization, stored salt/hash pair, and cost factor; no claim that salt alone makes weak passwords safe.

Supplementary inspected premise for the card or its comparison: NIST's salted password-hashing process applies cryptographic transformations to password storage rather than encrypting a message for later reading.

original_record.label: Password salting
original_record.learning_takeaway: Add per-password salt before costly hashing to prevent shared passwords from routinely producing identical stored hashes.

relations.note: NIST's salted password-hashing process applies cryptographic transformations to password storage rather than encrypting a message for later reading.

original_record.card: Patronage-based surplus distribution returns cooperative benefits in proportion to members' transactions with the cooperative. This differs from distributing returns solely according to invested capital. The cooperative principles also allow surplus to support reserves, development, or other approved purposes, so member payouts are not the only permitted use.

evidence.note: Checked transaction basis, alternative surplus uses and limited capital compensation; not every cooperative must distribute all surplus this way.

original_record.label: Patronage-based surplus distribution
original_record.learning_takeaway: Allocate cooperative surplus in proportion to member transactions rather than only in proportion to invested capital.

relations.note: The International Cooperative Alliance's third principle explicitly lists transaction-proportional member benefit among ways to allocate cooperative surplus.

original_record.card: Paul Signac helped develop and promote Neo-Impressionism through both artistic practice and theoretical writing. His later exploration of watercolor extended his investigation of color into a different medium. The case shows a movement continuing through explanation and experiment after the death of its leading innovator, Seurat.

evidence.note: The essay describes Signac’s writing, continuing role and watercolor experimentation.

original_record.label: Paul Signac
original_record.learning_takeaway: Signac helped carry Neo-Impressionism forward through theoretical writing and through watercolor experiments that extended its investigation of color.

relations.note: The essay places Signac’s artistic and theoretical work within the movement’s investigation of separated color.

original_record.card: A negative eDNA test may mean the assay was inhibited, not that the species was absent. Substances such as humic acids can interfere with PCR. An internal positive control helps reveal this problem by checking whether DNA amplification succeeds inside the tested sample.

evidence.note: USGS defines inhibited samples, names humic acids and describes internal positive controls detecting inhibition or false negatives.

original_record.label: PCR inhibition in eDNA samples
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explain why a negative molecular detection can reflect assay inhibition rather than species absence.

relations.note: Inhibition is a specific limitation of interpreting environmental-DNA tests; it concerns assay performance rather than the biological absence of a species.

original_record.card: Pectin molecules can form a network that gives fruit spreads their gel structure. Setting conditions depend on the pectin formulation: conventional types rely on appropriate sugar and acid, while other types can work with little or no sugar. Substituting one formulation blindly can therefore change the result.

evidence.note: UMN defines the pectin mesh and distinguishes formulation-specific sugar/acid needs and low/no-sugar products.

original_record.label: Pectin gelation
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explain fruit-spread setting as a network whose requirements depend on the kind of pectin used.

relations.note: Pectin gel formation can be compared with syneresis, where a gel later releases liquid; no claim is made that every pectin gel will weep.

original_record.card: A pedal point holds one note while surrounding harmonies change. It begins as a chord tone but can become a non-chord tone against later chords. Often heard in the bass, it can also appear higher up, creating continuity while its harmonic meaning shifts.

evidence.note: Puget Sound 10.8 supports changing harmonic status, frequent bass placement and upper-voice pedals; the card does not restrict the device to a literal organ pedal.

original_record.label: Pedal point
original_record.learning_takeaway: Hear a held note change harmonic status while surrounding chords move.

relations.note: Both can sustain a note across a harmonic change, but the pedal persists across harmonies while a suspension has a prepared stepwise resolution.

original_record.card: Peer Instruction inserts conceptual questions into a lecture. Students first commit to individual answers, explain their reasoning to nearby peers, then answer again before the instructor explains. The sequence gives discussion a specific job: compare reasons and reconsider an answer, rather than simply listen to another mini-lecture.

evidence.note: Checked initial answer, discussion, second poll and instructor feedback; not claimed that all answers improve or that every peer-learning format follows this protocol.

original_record.label: Peer Instruction
original_record.learning_takeaway: Sequence an individual conceptual answer, peer explanation, a second vote, and instructor feedback during class.

relations.note: The paper directly describes structured peer explanation as the central collaborative activity within its classroom protocol.

original_record.card: Perceptual closure is the tendency to see a complete object from incomplete visual parts. Broken arcs can look like a circle rather than unrelated segments. The perceived whole therefore contains an organization that is not supplied by a continuous drawn outline.

evidence.note: Section 5.6, closure definition and Figure 5.29, explicitly contrast whole circles and rectangles with fragmented segments; this is a perceptual tendency, not a guarantee for any broken image.

original_record.label: Perceptual closure
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explore how incomplete parts can be perceived as a complete object.

relations.note: Closure fills an incomplete whole, whereas good continuation favors smooth trajectories; comparing their illustrations prevents treating all visual grouping as one mechanism.

original_record.card: Chemist Percy Lavon Julian developed ways to obtain useful steroid compounds from plentiful plant materials. Working with soybean sterols helped make progesterone and other hormones more accessible. His work shows how changing a chemical starting material can reshape the practical scale of production.

evidence.locator: 1.1 Chemistry in Context; inspected passage indices 11 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-idp139124096
evidence.note: Julian used plentiful plant sterols to make steroid compounds more accessible through chemical synthesis.

original_record.label: Percy Lavon Julian
original_record.learning_takeaway: Julian used plentiful plant sterols to make steroid compounds more accessible through chemical synthesis.

relations.note: Julian’s change of starting material is a documented example of chemistry altering the practical production of useful substances.

original_record.card: Repeated checking is not a safe route to a draw in shogi. Under the Japan Shogi Association's cited explanation, if continuous checks produce the same position four times, the player giving those checks loses. Ordinary repetition without continuous checking is treated differently.

evidence.locator: 連続王手の千日手というのは反則なのですか
evidence.note: The official Japanese FAQ supports the fourth-occurrence loss and distinguishes ordinary repetition; the broad Shogi card instead explains piece reuse.

original_record.label: Perpetual check in shogi
original_record.learning_takeaway: Compare ordinary repetition with repeated checks that make the checking player lose.

relations.note: The Japan Shogi Association identifies this as shogi's special treatment of repetition by continuous check.

original_record.card: Peshat seeks a text’s plain or contextual sense by attending to how its words work within the surrounding passage. That does not make interpretation automatic. Commentators can disagree because their assumptions shape what they take to be the most straightforward reading.

evidence.note: Contextual sense and disagreement shaped by assumptions are discussed.

original_record.label: Peshat
original_record.learning_takeaway: A contextual reading asks what biblical words mean within their surrounding narrative, while commentators can disagree about that plain sense.

relations.note: The lesson contrasts contextual explanation with readings that draw further instructive meaning.

original_record.card: Phishing-resistant authentication binds the authentication process to the legitimate verifier or communication channel. An impostor cannot simply relay a captured output to sign in elsewhere. NIST therefore distinguishes cryptographic verifier binding from manually entered one-time codes, whose outputs can be relayed despite being temporary.

evidence.note: Checked channel/name binding and manually entered output limitation; no claim that user vigilance or a short-lived code alone provides phishing resistance.

original_record.label: Phishing-resistant authentication
original_record.learning_takeaway: Bind cryptographic authentication to the real verifier or channel so an impostor cannot relay a reusable output.

relations.note: The same NIST guideline separates verifier/channel binding from replay freshness, supporting a precise comparison of these protections.

original_record.card: A photogram places objects on light-sensitive paper and exposes it directly. In the process described here, opaque objects leave light areas while translucent ones can produce intermediate tones. The image records contact and light transmission rather than a camera’s view of a scene.

evidence.note: Opaque/translucent objects and tonal effects are explicit.

original_record.label: Photogram
original_record.learning_takeaway: In the described paper process, opaque objects leave light areas while translucent objects can yield intermediate tones during direct exposure.

relations.note: A photogram supplies a camera-free method within light-based image making.

aliases: Photographs of British Algae: Cyanotype Impressions
original_record.card: Anna Atkins’s Photographs of British Algae arranged specimens directly on sensitized paper to make cyanotype images. Botanical names accompanied the delicate traces. The project brings scientific identification together with the visual decisions involved in placing an individual specimen against the blue photographic field.

evidence.locator: Specimen making and handwritten labels, lines 10–12
evidence.note: Algae contact images, handwritten nomenclature and cyanotype book project are documented.

original_record.label: Photographs of British Algae
original_record.learning_takeaway: Anna Atkins arranged algae directly on sensitized paper for cyanotype images, combining botanical naming with the visual traces of individual specimens.

relations.note: The Met identifies cyanotype as the method used for the book’s specimen impressions.

original_record.card: Photogravure translates a photographic image into an intaglio printing plate. A light-sensitive gelatin resist helps produce etched recesses of differing depth, which hold varying amounts of ink. Those differences reproduce tonal variation through printing rather than through a conventional photographic paper image alone.

evidence.note: Gelatin resist, variable etching and ink-bearing tones are described.

original_record.label: Photogravure
original_record.learning_takeaway: A light-sensitive gelatin resist helps etch varying depths into a printing plate, whose ink-bearing recesses reproduce photographic tones.

relations.note: The photographic resist controls the etched matrix used to print the image.
The V&A explains etched-plate transfer through a printing press.

original_record.card: Plants can use the duration of light and darkness as a seasonal signal. Photoperiodism helps regulate events such as flowering or winter-bud formation, with different species responding differently. A plant’s calendar can therefore depend on day–night timing, rather than only on whether the weather is warm.

evidence.note: OpenStax describes photoperiod-dependent flowering/bud formation and different plant responses.

original_record.label: Photoperiodism
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explain seasonal plant responses through the duration of light and darkness rather than temperature alone.

relations.note: Seasonal light signals can influence flowering, while bolting is the crop-quality consequence of an early shift into reproductive growth.

original_record.card: Steve Reich's Piano Phase makes a repeating twelve-note pattern change through alignment rather than replacement. A second pianist gradually increases speed relative to the other part, causing the patterns to slip out of phase. The process lets different combinations emerge from recurring material.

evidence.note: Section 35.2 supports the twelve-note pattern and second pianist's gradual speed change; emergent combinations follow from changing alignment, without an unsupported claim about exact complete formal design.

original_record.label: Piano Phase
original_record.learning_takeaway: Follow two repeated patterns as one pianist gradually changes their alignment.

relations.note: The source explicitly presents the work as Reich's application of phase shifting to live pianists.

original_record.card: In a basic formulation, PID control combines three responses to error: proportional action responds to present error, integral action accumulates it, and derivative action responds to its rate of change. Adjusting their gains changes how a system approaches its target, including persistent offset, overshoot, and settling.

evidence.locator: What Is PID Control?; inspected passage indices 68, 70, 72, 74 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-69; paragraph-71; paragraph-73; paragraph-75
evidence.note: Combine present error, accumulated error, and error-rate feedback to regulate a system.

original_record.label: PID control
original_record.learning_takeaway: Combine present error, accumulated error, and error-rate feedback to regulate a system.

relations.note: The anti-windup source explicitly examines a practical saturation problem in PID control.

original_record.card: When lava flows into water, its exposed surface cools rapidly, producing rounded forms known as pillow lava. These shapes can survive within ancient rock. Recognizing them helps geologists infer that molten rock once met water, rather than assuming every lava flow formed in open air.

evidence.note: USGS describes pillow basalts forming when lava enters water and is rapidly cooled from exposed sides, including preserved examples at Shenandoah.

original_record.label: Pillow lava
original_record.learning_takeaway: Recognize rounded lava forms as evidence of rapid cooling in water.

relations.note: Pillow forms illustrate how geologists use a rock’s preserved structure to infer its formation environment.

original_record.card: The ochre sea star, Pisaster ochraceus, feeds on mussels along rocky shores. By limiting mussels that would otherwise occupy much of the available surface, it helps other organisms retain space. This makes its feeding behavior a useful case of a predator shaping community diversity.

evidence.note: NPS names the sea star and California mussels and explains how predation prevents mussels from crowding out other intertidal species.

original_record.label: Pisaster ochraceus
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explore why ochre sea-star predation on mussels helps preserve rocky-shore diversity.

relations.note: The named sea star provides the documented ecological example for the keystone-species concept.

original_record.card: Tar-derived pitch can feel solid and break under a quick hammer blow, yet flow over much longer times. The University of Queensland’s pitch-drop experiment demonstrates this contrast: material placed in a funnel slowly forms drops over years, with the flow rate affected by temperature.

evidence.locator: Pitch Drop experiment; inspected passage indices 4, 6, 8, 9, 11 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-5; paragraph-7; paragraph-9; paragraph-10; paragraph-12
evidence.note: Pitch may shatter under a quick blow yet flow extremely slowly over years.

original_record.label: Pitch (tar-derived material)
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explain how tar-derived pitch can shatter under a quick blow yet flow extremely slowly over years.

original_record.card: Pitch is a sound's perceived highness or lowness. On a piano, moving right produces higher notes. For periodic musical tones, doubling the vibration frequency raises pitch by an octave, showing why musical intervals depend on frequency ratios rather than equal additions of hertz.

evidence.note: Puget Sound 1.1 supports keyboard direction; UNSW's pitch discussion supplies periodic-tone frequency and octave ratio. Keep this auditory meaning separate from material pitch.

evidence.locator: Pitch, frequency, harmonics and missing fundamental
evidence.note: Frequency ratios, including doubling for an octave, support the quantitative explanation.

original_record.label: Pitch (music)
original_record.learning_takeaway: Relate perceived high and low notes to their ordering on a keyboard.

relations.note: The UNSW pitch discussion explicitly uses a missing fundamental to show that perceived pitch can persist when the lowest-frequency component is absent.

original_record.card: A graph is planar if it can be drawn in a plane without edges crossing except at shared vertices. One messy drawing does not disprove planarity: another arrangement might remove the crossings. The distinction concerns the existence of a suitable drawing, not its first appearance.

evidence.locator: Planar Graph -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1, 4, 5 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2; paragraph-5; paragraph-6
evidence.note: Planarity means some crossing-free drawing exists, even if another drawing of the same graph crosses.

original_record.label: Planar graph
original_record.learning_takeaway: Planarity means some crossing-free drawing exists, even if another drawing of the same graph crosses.

relations.note: The dual-graph source starts from a planar graph together with a particular planar embedding.

aliases: Plaque with equestrian oba and attendants
original_record.card: This Benin brass palace plaque makes its ruler larger than the surrounding attendants. Size expresses rank within the composition rather than simply reproducing natural proportions. The mounted figure and accompanying people show how a particular court artwork can organize political relationships visually.

evidence.note: Equestrian ruler, attendants, palace context and hierarchical scale are documented.

original_record.label: Plaque with equestrian ọ́bà and attendants
original_record.learning_takeaway: The enlarged ruler and smaller attendants on this Benin brass palace plaque use relative size to make rank visible.

relations.note: The collection description explicitly explains relative size as an expression of status.

original_record.card: Pochoir applies color by hand through a stencil, without the mesh used in screen printing. Brushes can leave visible traces as pigment passes through the cut openings. The process combines a repeatable shape with variations created by the way each impression is colored.

evidence.note: Hand-brushed stencil without a screen and visible marks are described.

original_record.label: Pochoir
original_record.learning_takeaway: Brushing pigment through a stencil without a screen creates hand-colored impressions that can retain visible brush marks.

relations.note: The glossary distinguishes pochoir’s open stencil from the mesh-based screen-printing process.

original_record.card: A constant-rate Poisson process has independent event counts in nonoverlapping time intervals. For very short intervals, one-event probability is approximately proportional to duration, while multiple events become negligible by comparison. Random clusters can occur even though the model’s average event rate stays constant.

evidence.locator: Poisson Process -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2; paragraph-3; paragraph-4; paragraph-5; paragraph-6
evidence.note: Model independent event counts in disjoint intervals at a constant rate.

original_record.label: Poisson process
original_record.learning_takeaway: Model independent event counts in disjoint intervals at a constant rate.

relations.note: The exponential-distribution reference identifies the waiting-time law corresponding to Poisson events.

original_record.card: A polder landscape is enclosed and drained land whose usability depends on water management. Dykes, canals and drainage works make fields and settlement possible, while requiring continued maintenance. Reclamation therefore creates a lasting relationship between the land’s apparent stability and the infrastructure that controls water.

evidence.note: Beemster’s reclaimed land and managed water network support the case.

original_record.label: Polder landscape
original_record.learning_takeaway: Draining and enclosing wet land creates inhabitable agricultural space that depends on a maintained network of dykes, canals and drainage.

relations.note: Beemster offers a named example of reclaimed land organized by a drainage and settlement grid.

original_record.card: A population bottleneck sharply reduces the number of individuals contributing genes to later generations. Chance can eliminate variants during that small-population period. Even if numbers subsequently rebound, the lost diversity need not return, as the history of heavily hunted northern elephant seals illustrates.

evidence.locator: Population bottlenecks; An example of a bottleneck
evidence.note: Berkeley defines bottlenecks and uses northern elephant seals to show numerical recovery with persistently reduced genetic variation.

original_record.label: Population bottleneck
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explain why rapid numerical recovery need not restore lost genetic diversity.

relations.note: A bottleneck is a demographic circumstance that magnifies genetic drift through a small surviving sample.

original_record.card: Positive predictive value is the probability of having a condition after a positive test. Even with unchanged sensitivity and specificity, it falls when the condition is rarer in the tested population. A positive result therefore gains meaning from both test performance and the starting prevalence.

evidence.note: NCI defines PPV and explicitly states that lower prevalence reduces PPV for given sensitivity and specificity.

original_record.label: Positive predictive value
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explain why a positive test is less convincing when the target condition is rare.

relations.note: The distinction shows why knowing sensitivity does not directly answer the question posed by a positive result.

original_record.card: Prasad connects offerings made to a deity with their later sharing among worshippers. In many pujas, food or other offerings move through this ritual sequence. Receiving and distributing them joins an individual act of devotion with a shared material practice within the community.

evidence.note: Offerings later shared with worshippers are explicit.

original_record.label: Prasad
original_record.learning_takeaway: Offerings made to a deity can later be shared among worshippers, connecting devotion with communal distribution.

relations.note: The case study presents shared offerings as a common element of puja.
The case study locates the shared offerings in Hindu puja practice.

original_record.card: The Pratimoksha is a code of Buddhist monastic discipline governing ordained practitioners. It extends beyond the basic ethical precepts shared with lay followers. Distinguishing these layers shows how common commitments coexist with more detailed obligations attached to a particular religious role.

evidence.note: Additional monastic code beyond shared precepts is explicit.

original_record.label: Pratimoksha
original_record.learning_takeaway: A monastic code adds extensive rules for ordained Buddhists beyond ethical precepts shared with lay followers.

relations.note: The source explains the code within the distinction between monastic and lay communities.

original_record.card: A Tibetan Buddhist prayer wheel contains rolls of written mantras within a rotating cylinder. Turning it joins repeated bodily motion with devotional text, even when the words remain enclosed. Wheels range from handheld objects to larger stationary installations, giving the practice several material forms.

evidence.note: Enclosed mantra rolls, rotation and handheld/stationary forms are described.

original_record.label: Prayer wheel
original_record.learning_takeaway: A rotating cylinder encloses written mantras, joining textual devotion with repeated physical motion in Tibetan Buddhist practice.

relations.note: The prayer wheel supplies a tradition-specific example of textual and material Buddhist practice.

original_record.card: An author can reasonably believe each carefully researched claim in a book while admitting that the book probably contains an error. Combining all the individual beliefs conflicts with that admission. The preface paradox tests how rational confidence in particular claims fits with recognition of one's fallibility.

evidence.note: SEP section 4 explains Makinson's author case and its conflict with agglomeration; the card preserves rational belief rather than recasting every assertion as knowledge or certainty.

original_record.label: Preface paradox
original_record.learning_takeaway: Examine believing each researched claim while reasonably expecting some mistake in the whole book.

relations.note: The source connects both paradoxes through agglomeration while distinguishing the preface's ordinary recognition of fallibility from a numerical probability-acceptance rule.

original_record.card: A prefix-free code gives each symbol a bit string that is never the beginning of another symbol's complete code. A decoder follows bits until it reaches a symbol, then starts again. Variable-length messages can therefore be separated into codewords without additional boundary markers.

evidence.note: Checked the binary-tree leaves and symbol-by-symbol decoding; prefix-free does not mean every possible bit string is a valid codeword.

original_record.label: Prefix-free code
original_record.learning_takeaway: Decode concatenated codewords unambiguously because no codeword is another codeword's prefix.

relations.note: The RFC's prefix-coding explanation directly introduces Huffman coding as a frequency-based construction of such codes.

original_record.card: A preliminary injunction provides court-ordered protection before final judgment. In US federal practice, the cited test considers likely success, likely irreparable harm, competing hardships and the public interest. The question is whether interim relief is justified while the dispute remains unresolved, not whether the applicant has already won.

evidence.note: Cornell's Winter factors and Rule 65 discussion support the four considerations and interim role; federal qualification avoids treating varying state procedures as identical.

original_record.label: Preliminary injunction
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explore temporary relief before final judgment and why irreparable harm matters.

relations.note: Contrast temporary relief pending resolution with an adjudication without trial when material facts do not require a factfinder; the procedures answer different questions despite possible pretrial timing.

original_record.card: A prepared piano changes its sound through objects placed beneath or between its strings. John Cage used such physical alterations to expand the instrument's available timbres. The keys remain a familiar interface, while the altered vibrating system produces sounds unlike those of an unprepared grand piano.

evidence.note: John Cage Trust explains objects placed among a grand piano's strings and the resulting transformed instrument; no invented preparation materials or exact acoustic mechanism is specified.

original_record.label: Prepared piano
original_record.learning_takeaway: Hear how objects placed between piano strings transform its available timbres.

relations.note: The Trust explicitly connects its prepared-piano samples with materials used for Cage's Sonatas and Interludes.

original_record.card: Prequestioning asks learners questions before they encounter new material. This can activate relevant knowledge and direct attention to what they need to learn. The cited guide cautions that selective reading may neglect material not covered by the questions, and its classroom evidence for this recommendation was limited.

evidence.note: Checked pre-exposure timing, attention rationale, nonquestioned-material risk, and the guide's low-evidence classification rather than asserting a universal benefit.

original_record.label: Prequestioning
original_record.learning_takeaway: Ask questions before exposure to focus study, while preserving attention to material the questions do not cover.

relations.note: Questions before exposure differ from retrieving already studied material; contrasting them prevents all uses of quizzes being treated as one testing mechanism.

original_record.card: Presentism holds that only temporally present objects exist. Merely past or future objects are excluded from its inventory of reality, though abstract entities may fall outside time. The claim concerns existence itself, not simply which events people can currently observe or remember.

evidence.locator: 6 Presentism, Eternalism, and the Growing Block Theory
evidence.note: SEP Time section 6 defines presentism and explicitly distinguishes temporal presence from spatial presence and timeless abstract objects; no claim that the past never occurred.

original_record.label: Presentism
original_record.learning_takeaway: Explore the thesis that only temporally present objects exist.

relations.note: The source directly opposes presentism to eternalism, which includes objects at past and future times in what exists.

original_record.card: Pressure thrust is the force contribution from a difference between nozzle-exit and ambient pressure. With uniform exit pressure, it equals that difference times exit area, alongside momentum-flow thrust. Equal pressures remove this term, but need not remove the engine’s remaining thrust.

evidence.locator: Specific Impulse; inspected passage indices 4 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-5
evidence.note: A nozzle’s exit-pressure mismatch contributes force in addition to exhaust momentum flux.

original_record.label: Pressure thrust
original_record.learning_takeaway: A nozzle’s exit-pressure mismatch contributes force in addition to exhaust momentum flux.

relations.note: The thrust equation separates exhaust momentum flow from pressure force, clarifying what contributes to a jet engine’s propulsive force.

original_record.card: A principal–agent problem arises when one party depends on another's action or attributes, but their interests differ and a contract cannot fully guarantee the desired result. Employers may value effort that is hard to verify. The framework separates who wants the outcome from who controls the relevant behavior.

evidence.note: Checked conflicting interests and unverifiable action; principal-agent relationships also cover hidden attributes, so the concept is not reduced to moral hazard alone.

original_record.label: Principal–agent problem
original_record.learning_takeaway: Analyze conflicting interests when one party relies on another's behavior or attributes that contracts cannot fully guarantee.

relations.note: CORE explicitly defines principal-agent relationships in terms of behavior or attributes not guaranteed in a binding contract.

original_record.card: The sociolinguistic principle of accountability requires counting all occasions when a variant could occur, not only the instances that attract attention. Ten examples in one setting may represent a lower usage rate than eight in another. The relevant denominator makes comparisons across speaking contexts interpretable.

evidence.note: Checked eligible alternatives and count-versus-rate distinction in the source table; no rate inferred without the opportunity denominator.
Supplementary inspected premise for the card or its comparison: The quantitative-analysis section explicitly names this denominator rule as a foundation of variationist sociolinguistic analysis.

original_record.label: Principle of accountability in sociolinguistics
original_record.learning_takeaway: Count every eligible variant to form a denominator instead of counting only the interesting pronunciation.

relations.note: The quantitative-analysis section explicitly names this denominator rule as a foundation of variationist sociolinguistic analysis.

original_record.card: Least privilege gives each user or program only the authority needed for its job. If an error or misuse occurs, fewer permissions limit what can be damaged. The principle also reduces the number of privileged components that must be examined when investigating an unexpected access path.

evidence.note: Checked minimum necessary authority, limiting damage, and reducing privileged interactions; least privilege is not a guarantee that permitted actions are harmless.

original_record.label: Principle of least privilege
original_record.learning_takeaway: Give each program and user only necessary permissions to limit accidents and the code requiring trust.

relations.note: Saltzer and Schroeder explicitly list least privilege among the basic design principles for protecting information in computer systems.

original_record.card: A private-value auction models each bidder's valuation as personal: learning that someone else values the object highly does not change one's own value. It is an idealized case. A house, for example, may mix personal enjoyment with resale concerns that introduce a common-value component.

evidence.note: Checked independence of personal value from others' valuations and mixed housing example; private value is not equated with secret bidding.

original_record.label: Private-value auction
original_record.learning_takeaway: Model each bidder's value as personal and unaffected by learning others' valuations, an idealized limiting case.

relations.note: The lecture explicitly contrasts the two limiting valuation models and uses housing to illustrate mixtures between them.

original_record.card: Proactive interference occurs when older learning gets in the way of remembering newer information. After changing phone numbers, you might keep giving the old number automatically. The direction matters: an established memory is obstructing access to its more recently learned replacement.

evidence.note: OpenStax 8.3 defines old-to-new interference and gives the phone-number example; this concerns retrieval competition, not proof that the new memory was erased.

original_record.label: Proactive interference
original_record.learning_takeaway: Understand how an older memory can obstruct recall of newly learned information.

relations.note: The source explicitly distinguishes the two forms by whether older or newer information interferes.

original_record.card: The problem of closeness challenges the line between intended means and foreseen side effects. A harmful result may be so closely connected with an agent's chosen means that calling it unintended seems artificial. The difficulty is classifying the action without already assuming the moral verdict.

evidence.note: SEP section 4.2 identifies closely connected harms, and 4.3 raises evaluation-driven descriptions; the card presents a criticism rather than declaring that every intention distinction collapses.

evidence.locator: Sections 4.2 The Problem of Closeness and 4.3 The Side Effect Effect
evidence.note: The closely connected harm problem and normative influence on action descriptions together support the classification concern.

original_record.label: Problem of closeness in double effect
original_record.learning_takeaway: Examine when a harmful side effect seems inseparable from the agent's chosen means.

relations.note: The entry names the problem of closeness as a criticism of double effect's distinction between intended means and merely foreseen harms.

original_record.card: The problem of temporary intrinsics asks how one persisting object can have incompatible intrinsic properties at different times. A metal plate may change from round to square. Explaining that change requires an account of what it means to possess a property at a time.

evidence.note: SEP Identity Over Time sections 2.3–2.4 use the plate's shape change and discuss competing solutions; the card does not infer that ordinary change is logically impossible.

original_record.label: Problem of temporary intrinsics
original_record.learning_takeaway: Ask how one persisting object can possess incompatible intrinsic properties at different times.

relations.note: The section explicitly frames the temporary-intrinsics problem through Leibniz's Law: identity and differing properties require explaining the temporal qualification.

original_record.card: Procedural memory is expressed in skilled actions, such as balancing on a bicycle or driving. Practice can improve performance even when a person cannot fully describe the knowledge guiding it. This distinguishes remembering how to do something from consciously reporting facts or past events.

evidence.note: OpenStax Long-Term Memory defines implicit procedural skill and contrasts reportable explicit memories; not every component of driving is claimed unconscious.

original_record.label: Procedural memory
original_record.learning_takeaway: Distinguish remembering how to perform a skill from verbally recalling its instructions.

relations.note: Molaison's preserved improvement despite impaired new declarative memory provides a concrete comparison between performance-based and consciously reportable remembering.

original_record.card: Puja is a Hindu form of worship that can bring a devotee into a ritual encounter with a deity. Images, visual attention and offerings often participate in the encounter. Practices vary with the deity and community, and pujas can occur at home, in temples or elsewhere.

evidence.note: Visual encounter, offerings, varied locations and contextual diversity are explicit.

original_record.label: Puja
original_record.learning_takeaway: Offerings and visual interaction with deity images are common elements of Hindu puja; practices vary with the deity and community.

relations.note: The case study identifies visual interaction with an image as a common element of puja.
The case study explicitly identifies puja as a form of Hindu worship while emphasizing variation.

original_record.card: Pulmonary surfactant helps the lungs remain expanded so air sacs can participate in breathing. Premature newborns may have too little, allowing lung collapse and making breathing much harder. The example connects a substance within the lung with the mechanical ability to keep air spaces open.

evidence.note: NHLBI identifies inadequate surfactant as a cause of neonatal respiratory distress, lung collapse and increased work of breathing.

original_record.label: Pulmonary surfactant
original_record.learning_takeaway: Connect surfactant deficiency with air-sac collapse and difficult breathing in premature newborns.

relations.note: Surfactant concerns lung mechanics, while spirometry measures aspects of breathing performance; the link is a learning comparison, not a claim that neonatal surfactant deficiency is diagnosed by spirometry.

original_record.card: A pulse oximeter shines light through tissue to estimate blood oxygen saturation. A small sensor can provide this information without drawing arterial blood. The reading is an estimate, however, and factors including poor circulation, cold skin or skin pigmentation can affect its accuracy.

evidence.note: MedlinePlus describes the optical sensor and estimated oxygen saturation; its listed limitations include poor circulation, cold skin and darker skin pigmentation.

original_record.label: Pulse oximetry
original_record.learning_takeaway: Estimate blood oxygen saturation from light passing through tissue.

relations.note: Skin pigmentation is one specifically documented limitation of the broader optical measurement method.

original_record.card: Pure-tone audiometry measures the quietest tones a person can detect at different pitches. Through headphones, sounds are presented while the listener signals when they hear them. The resulting pattern separates sensitivity across frequencies, rather than reducing hearing to a single yes-or-no ability.

evidence.note: MedlinePlus describes pure-tone presentation at varied pitches/volumes and the listener’s response to the softest audible sound.

original_record.label: Pure-tone audiometry
original_record.learning_takeaway: Map the quietest tones a person detects at different frequencies.

relations.note: Pure-tone detection and eardrum movement are complementary but distinct types of hearing-test evidence.

original_record.card: Qibla is the direction toward Mecca used in Muslim prayer. It coordinates worshippers’ orientation across very different locations. A mosque’s mihrab indicates that direction, but the niche and the direction are different things: one is an architectural marker of the other.

evidence.locator: Summary and prayer preparation, lines 149 and 156
evidence.note: Mecca orientation and the indicating mihrab are described.

original_record.label: Qibla
original_record.learning_takeaway: A shared orientation toward Mecca organizes Muslim prayer; a mosque’s mihrab indicates this direction rather than being the direction itself.

relations.note: The source explicitly identifies the mihrab as a marker of the prayer direction.

original_record.card: Quantile classification places roughly equal numbers of mapped features in each class. This spreads observations across the legend, but nearby values can fall on opposite sides of a class boundary. Conversely, quite different values may share a class when the data are unevenly distributed.

evidence.note: Equal-count grouping and separation/combination caveats are explicit.

original_record.label: Quantile map classification
original_record.learning_takeaway: Putting equal numbers of geographic features in each class can separate close values or combine widely different values.

relations.note: Compare grouping by numbers of features with grouping by equal numeric intervals.
Equal-count numerical classes are a specific decision in representing attributes on maps.

original_record.card: Quantum tunneling allows a particle’s wave state to extend through a finite potential barrier higher than its total energy. Some amplitude can emerge beyond the barrier even when a classical particle would turn back. The transmission probability depends on the barrier’s width, height, and particle energy.

evidence.locator: 7.6 The Quantum Tunneling of Particles through Potential Barriers; inspected passage indices 7, 9, 15, 16 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: fs-id1170902689053; fs-id1170901605351; fs-id1170901769645; fs-id1170903049760
evidence.note: A quantum state can transmit through a finite barrier that forbids passage at the same classical energy.

original_record.label: Quantum tunneling
original_record.learning_takeaway: A quantum state can transmit through a finite barrier that forbids passage at the same classical energy.

relations.note: The source explicitly identifies scanning tunneling microscopy as an application of barrier tunneling.

original_record.card: A quotient group replaces a group’s individual elements with cosets of a normal subgroup. Multiplying those cosets gives a new group whose elements each represent an entire collection of original elements. The construction organizes selected distinctions into classes while retaining an algebraic operation.

evidence.locator: Quotient Group -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1, 2, 3 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2; paragraph-3; paragraph-4
evidence.note: Cosets of a normal subgroup become group elements, collapsing selected distinctions while preserving an operation.

original_record.label: Quotient group
original_record.learning_takeaway: Cosets of a normal subgroup become group elements, collapsing selected distinctions while preserving an operation.

relations.note: For finite groups, the quotient-group source connects the sizes of groups and cosets with Lagrange’s group theorem; the quotient construction itself need not be finite.

original_record.card: Raft manages a replicated log by electing a leader that receives commands and sends entries to followers. Its design separates leader election, log replication, and safety rules. This decomposition was chosen to make the protocol easier to understand while preserving agreement when machines stop or become disconnected.

evidence.note: Checked leader role and design decomposition; failure language excludes arbitrary malicious behavior and does not promise availability during every partition.

original_record.label: Raft consensus algorithm
original_record.learning_takeaway: Separate leader election, log replication, and safety to make a replicated-log consensus algorithm easier to understand.

relations.note: The Raft paper explicitly presents the algorithm as a solution to consensus for a replicated log under non-Byzantine failures.

original_record.card: Moist air rising over a mountain cools and can release precipitation on the windward side. After crossing the summit, descending air warms and becomes drier. This rain-shadow effect helps explain why nearby places on opposite sides of a mountain can have sharply different rainfall.

evidence.locator: Windward precipitation and leeward drying mechanism
evidence.note: NOAA’s Hawaii explanation connects windward ascent/cooling/precipitation with leeward descent/warming/drying.

original_record.label: Rain shadow
original_record.learning_takeaway: Trace contrasting mountain rainfall through rising moist air and descending dry air.

relations.note: Comparing a mountain’s lifting effect with atmospheric-river moisture transport separates where vapor arrives from how terrain can release it as precipitation.

original_record.card: Ramp metering uses entrance-ramp signals to regulate freeway entry. Breaking up merging platoons can reduce sudden mainline braking and improve traffic flow. Metering also creates waiting queues, so its design must account for ramp storage and effects on adjacent streets.

evidence.locator: About Ramp Metering; inspected passage indices 12, 16, 17 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: contenttext
evidence.note: Regulate freeway entry to break up merging platoons and reduce flow breakdown.

original_record.label: Ramp metering
original_record.learning_takeaway: Regulate freeway entry to break up merging platoons and reduce flow breakdown.

relations.note: The ramp-management handbook explicitly links metering success with containing and managing the resulting ramp queues.

original_record.card: A ramp meter can protect freeway flow while allowing its waiting queue to spill into nearby streets. Queue detectors and available storage therefore matter. Increasing the release rate can relieve the ramp but worsen freeway conditions, making queue management a balance between connected parts of the road system.

evidence.locator: Ramp Management and Control Handbook | Chapter 10 Planning and Design Considerations; inspected passage indices 72, 73, 107, 108, 109 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-73; paragraph-74; paragraph-108; paragraph-109; paragraph-110
evidence.note: Balance freeway entry control with finite ramp storage so queued vehicles do not block adjacent streets.

original_record.label: Ramp-queue spillback management
original_record.learning_takeaway: Balance freeway entry control with finite ramp storage so queued vehicles do not block adjacent streets.

relations.note: The handbook explicitly treats queue management as a design and operational concern for ramp metering.

original_record.card: A Ramsey number gives the smallest vertex count that forces either a clique of one chosen size or an independent set of another in any simple undirected graph. The party analogy treats vertices as people and edges as mutual acquaintance.

evidence.locator: Ramsey Number -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1, 2 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2; paragraph-3
evidence.note: Find when every sufficiently large graph must contain a chosen clique or independent-set pattern.

original_record.label: Ramsey number
original_record.learning_takeaway: Find when every sufficiently large graph must contain a chosen clique or independent-set pattern.

relations.note: Ramsey numbers express an unavoidable-pattern question using graph vertices and edges.

original_record.card: A random walk builds a path from successive randomly chosen steps. The allowed directions, step lengths, and surrounding space define the model. Walks on a line, a plane, or a lattice can behave differently, so specifying the rules matters as much as calling the motion random.

evidence.locator: Random Walk -- from Wolfram MathWorld; inspected passage indices 1, 2, 3 (zero-based in saved snapshot); HTML anchors: paragraph-2; paragraph-3; paragraph-4
evidence.note: Repeated random steps form paths whose behavior changes with dimension and allowed movement.

original_record.label: Random walk
original_record.learning_takeaway: Repeated random steps form paths whose behavior changes with dimension and allowed movement.

relations.note: The Markov-chain reference explicitly names a simple random walk as an example.

original_record.card: A randomized controlled trial uses chance to assign participants to an intervention or comparison group. Comparing outcomes helps separate the intervention’s effects from differences that might influence who receives it. Randomization is a design tool; clear follow-up and careful analysis are still needed for a trustworthy result.
